# Typhoon Champi unlikely to hit Hong Kong, Observatory says

China's weather agency says a tropical depression east of Guam is set to become Typhoon Champi within 24 hours, possibly reaching super typhoon strength. The Hong Kong Observatory says a direct hit on the city is unlikely, with tropical cyclones not expected to affect Hong Kong for the rest of Octob

[![Image 4: Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)

 By [Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk), Editor in Chief

 15 Oct 2026 at 17:54 HKT · 1 min read

[](https://wa.me/?text=Typhoon%20Champi%20unlikely%20to%20hit%20Hong%20Kong%2C%20Observatory%20says%20https%3A//clb.org.hk/en/hong-kong/Typhoon-Champi-unlikely-to-hit-Hong-Kong-Observatory-says-0b47ea "WhatsApp")[](https://t.me/share/url?url=https%3A//clb.org.hk/en/hong-kong/Typhoon-Champi-unlikely-to-hit-Hong-Kong-Observatory-says-0b47ea&text=Typhoon%20Champi%20unlikely%20to%20hit%20Hong%20Kong%2C%20Observatory%20says "Telegram")[](https://www.facebook.com/sharer/sharer.php?u=https%3A//clb.org.hk/en/hong-kong/Typhoon-Champi-unlikely-to-hit-Hong-Kong-Observatory-says-0b47ea "Facebook")[](https://twitter.com/intent/tweet?url=https%3A//clb.org.hk/en/hong-kong/Typhoon-Champi-unlikely-to-hit-Hong-Kong-Observatory-says-0b47ea&text=Typhoon%20Champi%20unlikely%20to%20hit%20Hong%20Kong%2C%20Observatory%20says "X")[](https://clb.org.hk/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection# "Email")

China's National Meteorological Center said a tropical depression east of Guam is forecast to become this year's 30th typhoon, Champi, within 24 hours, and it could develop into a super typhoon as it moves west-northwest.

The Hong Kong Observatory said the city is less likely to be hit directly, and tropical cyclones are unlikely to affect Hong Kong for the rest of October. The storm may move toward waters east of Luzon early to mid next week. Its later track remains uncertain, but there is a higher chance it will turn north and pass through waters east of Taiwan.

AI weather models all show Champi making a 90-degree northward turn near eastern Taiwan. Model Pangu forecasts the storm will cross Japan on October 26, while Fuxi and Fengwu show it passing near Tokyo between October 25 and 26.

Locally, the Observatory said a fresh easterly airstream will bring stronger winds and one or two showers to the Guangdong coast over the next two or three days. As an upper-air anticyclone strengthens, the South China coast should be generally sunny and dry early to mid next week, with hot daytime weather. A northeast monsoon is expected to affect southern China late next week.

The Observatory predicted mostly sunny weather over the next nine days. Saturday will be mostly cloudy with one or two showers, and Sunday will start mostly cloudy with one or two light showers. Next week will be cooler, with the lowest temperature on October 23 dropping to 25 degrees, with sunny periods and dry daytime conditions.

title: Cabinet approves upgraded dementia care plan targeting '888' goals by 2035 - Focus Taiwan
zh_title: 内阁批准升级版痴呆症护理计划，目标是到 2035 年实现“888”目标 - 聚焦台湾
summary: 中新社台北10月15日电 台湾内阁周四批准升级版国家痴呆症预防和护理计划，旨在到2035年实现“痴呆友好台湾888”目标，扩大对年轻患者的支持，同时加强早期诊断、长期护理和公众意识。卫生福利部提出的痴呆症预防和护理政策与行动计划3.0，纳入政府长期护理计划3.0，重点关注“全年龄段、全疾病阶段、综合支持”。根据该计划，政府的目标是到 2035 年
content:
中新社台北10月15日电 台湾内阁周四批准升级版国家痴呆症预防和护理计划，旨在到2035年实现“痴呆友好台湾888”目标，扩大对年轻患者的支持，同时加强早期诊断、长期护理和公众意识。

卫生福利部提出的痴呆症预防和护理政策与行动计划3.0，纳入政府长期护理计划3.0，重点关注“全年龄段、全疾病阶段、综合支持”。

根据规划，到2035年，痴呆症诊断准确率达到80%，痴呆症患者服务覆盖率达到80%，定点机构和服务行业人员痴呆症素养达到80%。

该倡议建立在2025年实现的“认知障碍友好台湾777”目标的基础上，根据该目标，超过70％的认知障碍患者得到诊断和服务，超过70％的家庭照顾者获得支持，并且至少7％的公众表现出足够的认知障碍意识。

该计划首次将 50 岁以下患有早发性痴呆症的残疾人纳入其中，目的是减缓疾病的进展。
卫生部副部长吕建德表示，卫生部发现年轻人痴呆症病例有所增加，将与劳工部合作，帮助患者调整就业或工作安排。

根据卫生健康部的数据，台湾约有 10,000 名早发性痴呆症患者和约 400,000 名老年人患有这种疾病。

该计划还寻求扩大预先护理计划，增加痴呆症护理资源，并改善对患者和护理人员的支持。

到2035年，政府的目标是将痴呆症综合护理中心的数量从目前的133个增加到153个，将社区痴呆症服务点从约580个扩大到628个，并将护理人员支持中心的数量从191个增加到200个。还计划提供4,000个专门的痴呆症护理床位，并向42万人提供长期护理服务。

当局还计划通过就业援助和工作重新设计计划，帮助至少 665 名早发性痴呆症患者留在或重返劳动力市场。

根据该计划，政府还将通过发布公共场所服务指南和扩大痴呆症友好社区和组织来促进痴呆症友好环境。

内阁发言人李慧芝表示，卓荣泰总理指示卫生部更加重视健康促进、风险预防和早期筛查，同时确保提供足够的心理咨询和诊断服务。
卫生部周四早些时候在一份声明中表示，该计划将重点关注四个领域：前端预防、精准诊断、增强服务能力和权益保护。

该公司表示，将研究是否将痴呆症药物纳入国民健康保险。

（赖玉珍、陈杰玲、高伊芙撰）

结局/AW

【原文 English Original】
Taipei, Oct. 15 (CNA) Taiwan's Cabinet on Thursday approved an upgraded national dementia prevention and care plan aimed at achieving the "Dementia-Friendly Taiwan 888" targets by 2035, expanding support for younger patients while strengthening early diagnosis, long-term care and public awareness.

The Dementia Prevention and Care Policy and Action Plan 3.0, proposed by the Ministry of Health and Welfare (MOHW), is integrated into the government's Long-Term Care Plan 3.0 and focuses on "all ages, all stages of the disease and comprehensive support."

Under the plan, the government aims by 2035 to achieve an 80 percent accurate dementia diagnosis rate, 80 percent service coverage for people with dementia, and 80 percent dementia literacy among personnel in designated organizations and service sectors.

The initiative builds on the "Dementia-Friendly Taiwan 777" targets achieved in 2025, under which more than 70 percent of people with dementia received diagnoses and services, over 70 percent of family caregivers obtained support, and at least 7 percent of the public demonstrated adequate dementia awareness.

For the first time, the plan will include people under age 50 with disabilities who have young-onset dementia, with the aim of slowing the progression of the disease.

Deputy Health Minister Lue Jen-der (呂建德) said the ministry has seen an increase in dementia cases among younger people and will work with the Ministry of Labor to help patients adjust their employment or work arrangements.

According to MOHW data, Taiwan has about 10,000 people with young-onset dementia and around 400,000 older adults living with the condition.

The plan also seeks to expand advance care planning, increase dementia care resources and improve support for patients and caregivers.

By 2035, the government aims to increase the number of integrated dementia care centers from the current 133 to 153, expand community dementia service sites from about 580 to 628, and increase the number of caregiver support hubs from 191 to 200. It also plans to provide 4,000 dedicated dementia care beds and extend long-term care services to 420,000 people.

The authorities also plan to help at least 665 people with young-onset dementia remain in or return to the workforce through employment assistance and job redesign programs.

The government will also promote dementia-friendly environments by issuing service guidelines for public venues and expanding dementia-friendly communities and organizations, according to the plan.

Cabinet spokesperson Michelle Lee (李慧芝) said Premier Cho Jung-tai (卓榮泰) instructed the MOHW to place greater emphasis on health promotion, risk prevention and early screening while ensuring adequate psychological counseling and diagnostic services.

The MOHW said earlier Thursday in a statement that the plan will focus on four areas: front-end prevention, accurate diagnosis, stronger service capacity and rights protection.

It said it would study whether to include dementia drugs under National Health Insurance.

(By Lai Yu-chen, Chen Chieh-ling and Evelyn Kao)

# MND says zero tolerance for bullying after new suicide case evidence

CNA file photo

Taipei, Oct. 15 (CNA) A Ministry of National Defense (MND) spokesperson said Thursday that the ministry has zero tolerance for bullying in the armed forces after evidence surfaced of alleged bullying in the case of a female Army first lieutenant who died by suicide.

The first lieutenant, surnamed Wang (王), jumped to her death from a building at the Army's 206th Brigade base in Hsinchu County on Sept. 30. The military conducted a postmortem examination the following day, ruling out foul play.

An audio recording uploaded to the social media site Threads was provided by Wang's family to the 6th Army Command on Oct. 12.

The recording apparently captures a conversation between Wang and a male human resources officer. In it a woman can be heard apologizing to a man for "irritating" him while asking about the details of her work. The man repeatedly berated her for failing to remember what she had been taught.

Some local news outlets reported on Oct. 2 that 6th Army Command Director of Political Warfare Chien Ying-hung (簡熒宏) had said bullying played no role in Wang's death, which he said was under judicial investigation.

At a news conference Thursday, Chien was repeatedly asked whether he had ruled out bullying as a factor in Wang's death, but he sidestepped the question.

"We will not be lenient, conceal or protect. The judiciary will find out the whole truth," Chien said, adding that an MND legal team launched an investigation on Oct. 1 and would forward all the evidence it collects to the Hsinchu District Prosecutors' Office and the Hsinchu Military Police Force for review.

MND spokesperson Sun Li-fang (孫立方) said the ministry's fundamental position is to fully cooperate with judicial investigations.

"The Ministry of National Defense has zero tolerance for all forms of bullying, whether between personnel of the same rank, senior-ranking personnel toward junior-ranking personnel, or between more senior and less experienced personnel, regardless of rank," Sun said.

He added that Defense Minister Wellington Koo (顧立雄) is paying close attention to the case.

Chien added that the HR officer in the recording did not outrank Wang, as both were platoon leaders.

（By Sean Lin）Enditem/AW

title: The latest BRICS Summit: India’s test, China’s shadow, and Europe’s dilemma
summary: India hosted the 18th BRICS summit on September 12 and 13, 2026. The group currently represents 11 member countries, accounting for roughly 49% of the world’s population and about 40% of the world’s GDP. Leaders from the non-Western Bloc, i
content:
India hosted the 18th BRICS summit on September 12 and 13, 2026. The group currently represents 11 member countries, accounting for roughly 49% of the world’s population and about 40% of the world’s GDP. Leaders from the non-Western Bloc, including among others Chinese President Xi Jinping, Russian President Vladimir Putin, Iran’s President Masoud Pezeshkian, Abu Dhabi’s Crown Prince Sheikh Khaled bin Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan, and South African President Cyril Ramaphosa, met in New Delhi for their annual meeting to discuss about cooperation and share perspectives on matters of mutual importance. Inter alia, leaders talked about the escalation in West Asia, condemned unilateral tariff and non-tariff measures, and reiterated their support for a multipolar world order and for reforming the United Nations. Yet, if on the one hand these countries are driven together by a common interest in refusing a Western-led international order, on the other they also face their intra-group controversies, including histories of border disputes and even current military confrontations.

**![Image 1](https://aspeniaonline.it/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/India-brics-summit.jpg)**

**India as the Chair and the main outcomes of the Summit**

BRICS is a very important platform to India, who seeks to be seen as a leader of the developing world, and yet refrains from taking a clear stance in critical situations that involve many of its Global South fellows. This year’s presidency was indeed a real test for New Delhi, as it needed to manage its relations with China; preserve Russia without inheriting its confrontation with the West; and accommodate Iran’s interests while deepening relations with the UAE, who had faced recent attacks from Tehran. The real test for India was thus to hold together such a diverse group, arguably more divided than it was some years ago.

Ultimately, the head of states converged on a series of matters. New Delhi hosted the summit under the official theme of “Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability”, which sought to highlight its “Humanity First” approach. The 45 pages long joint declaration ranged from conflicts and terrorism to trade, development, energy, health, technology and global governance. It voiced “deep concern over the continued escalation of tensions” across the Middle East and West Asia,[[1]](https://aspeniaonline.it/the-latest-brics-summit-indias-test-chinas-shadow-and-europes-dilemma/#_ftn1) calling for “maximum restraint” and warning against deliberate attacks on civilian infrastructure and on nuclear facilities, in particular. It further expressed concerns over the situation in the Gaza strip. The declaration also addressed the expansion of non-Western cross-border payment channels, cooperation on artificial intelligence and opposition to unilateral sanctions and tariffs. The question of currency and de-dollarization in particular was heavily debated ahead of the Summit; yet, India ensured the outcome document contained no explicit anti-Western language. As such, the declaration leaves room for flexible alternatives, but stops short of delivering any clear anti-Western policy overall.

##### Read also: **[What India wants: global influence and freedom of choice](https://aspeniaonline.it/what-india-wants-global-influence-and-freedom-of-choice/)**

For some aspects, the declaration was a diplomatic success, as it brought together the voices of states – such as Iran and UAE who are holding competing positions and facing confrontation elsewhere. What is relevant to note is not that differences disappeared, but that the members still managed to find a common stance, even if it required a carefully negotiated language. It might be fair to argue that this was a classic move of India’s diplomacy, and nowhere is that balancing act more visible than in New Delhi’s own relationship with China. However, beyond declarations, the practical impact of this balancing effort still remains open to debate.

**Spotlight on India-China relations**

China is one of India’s central BRICS dilemmas. The relationship between the two countries is marked by an unresolved border dispute which continues to be managed without a long-term resolution, amid a broader regional “cooperation while at competition” relationship. Extensive declarations were made by both sides at the Summit, towards reaching a mutual understanding and resolution of the border issue, as well as facilitation of economic ties and common market access. But behind these official statements, deep mistrust remains at the contested Himalayan frontier, together with an Indian trade deficit vis-à-vis China which has widened to $112.16 billion in 2025-26, and an enduring regional strategic rivalry. The 25th round of Special Representatives talks between India’s national security advisor Ajit Doval and China’s foreign minister Wang Yi was held in August 2026, followed by the first senior military “flag meeting” at Vacha and Damai in early September, which testifies that the dialogue between the two countries is active, but far from reaching a resolution of the existing dispute.

Beijing appears to be seeking a wider array of economic leverages vis-a-vis India; for some, the prospect of Chinese investments flowing into India would require New Delhi to shift its position that the state of the border will determine the state of overall ties. China thus expects India to downplay its immediate security worries, even as Beijing remains quietly driven by its own long-term security anxieties. Yet, India holds a different vision, and has maintained its bottom line regarding the state of the border’s effect on overall relations.

##### Read also: **[How India looks at China: dealing with uncertainty](https://aspeniaonline.it/how-india-looks-at-china-dealing-with-uncertainty/)**

Xi’s presence in New Delhi for the Summit, his first visit to India in seven years, signals that BRICS matters to China, and that its preferred approach is that both sides should handle their differences more discreetly and away from the public sphere. Indeed, the bilateral meeting between Indian PM Modi and Chinese President Xi was officially marked by a deliberate and controlled interaction. Yet, even if the dominant narrative since Modi’s 2025 visit to China for the Tianjin SCO summit has been of gradual normalization, New Delhi remains cautious about restoring full economic ties. Clearly, they both have strong reasons to seek a (more) positive relationship and avoid conflict, but it remains questionable how they are seeking to reach such an outcome.

Summit declarations alone are not enough when economic and military asymmetry persist and hinder strategic trust. Since the 2025 SCO summit that official warmth has held, but in the India-China bilateral relationship, coexistence between cooperation and unresolved sovereignty dispute is rather normal. In this sense, BRICS are an institutional tool to retain dialogue, but shall not be viewed as a proof they have settled what divides them.

**India’s Balancing Act and Europe’s Dilemma**

BRICS is no longer the five-member forum founded in 2009 to give the Global South a voice and seat at the table. With its current eleven members, expanded geographic reach, and a growing share of global GDP, it now carries real weight in shaping how the international order is contested. The September final declaration reiterates two main points overall: a frustration with the Western-led international order and the aspiration of the Global South. This is not enough to change the global strategic equation, but amid global fragmentation, countries with the diplomatic reach and trust to engage across opposing political blocs would become indispensable.

For Europe, the Summit is a reminder that this contestation is no longer an abstract concept. Despite significant differences in interests and perceptions among the BRICS members, they converge on shared positions on tariffs, sanctions, and flexible payment infrastructures that directly touch the European trade and financial ecosystem.

##### Read also: **[India and Europe: a window of convergence](https://aspeniaonline.it/india-and-europe-a-window-of-convergence/)**

The EU has long framed itself as a champion of a “rules-based order”; the BRICS display coherence and convergence on precisely those issues where that order is being tested, and this narrows the space for Europe to treat multipolarity as someone else’s concern. At the same time, the Summit’s internal fault lines and the different visions across members suggest that Europe should not treat the group as monolithic. India’s presidency shows a country trying to lead the Global South while avoiding entanglement or confrontation with the West.

This posture leaves room for a European engagement with India specifically. Delhi understands the constraints and priorities that exist across global divides, and is well placed to identify where compatibility is possible. In that sense, India’s global clout is still to be fully tested and consolidated, but its strategic value for Europe is undeniable.

content:
0月15号法国各大报头版关注焦点各异。《解放报》关注乌克兰议题，大字标题点出：乌克兰被美国抛弃了。指出，由于美国总统特朗普和俄罗斯总统普京之间的协议，美国情报机构不再向乌克兰提供俄罗斯空袭的信息，因此加剧了乌克兰平民的危险。

《费加罗报》头版关注国内议题：指出退休选民成为总统竞选策略的核心。文章认为，过去一年，50岁以上的法国选民已占多数。退休人员积极参与政治，构成了一个稳固的选民基础，足以左右总统选举的走向。尽管年轻人的积极参与掩盖了老年人的光芒，但由于其在选举中的影响力，老年人在塑造未来政治格局方面仍然至关重要。极右翼国民联盟（RN）正指望这一群体赢得胜利。国民联盟目前在65岁及以上选民中占据多数，并将维护退休人员权益作为其竞选纲领的核心内容。

天主教《十字架报》头版配图关注的是：加沙，废墟中的幸存者。背景是巴勒斯坦权力机构于10月10日宣布推迟原定于近期举行的立法和总统选举。新的选举日期定于2027年9月11日，但这一举措引发了广泛的质疑。这一决定令欧洲国家，特别是法国感到失望，它们一直呼吁巴勒斯坦机构进行民主改革。但十字架报指出，文章战争爆发三年后，这片飞地超过80%的建筑已被摧毁或损坏。对于一个饱受苦难的民族而言，投票意味着什么？这个问题在加沙地带居民即将再次在赤贫中度过寒冬之际凸显出来。

**中国式压路机一路碾压**

这是经济类《回声报》头版头条大标题。这里指的"碾压"是中国出口激增对国际市场的压力。根据北京本周三上午公布的统计数据，中国贸易增速在9月份加快。在全球强劲需求的推动下，尤其是在人工智能爆炸式增长的带动下，中国9月份出口增长超过三分之一，为今年创纪录的贸易顺差铺平了道路。

尽管美国和欧盟采取了应对措施，但中国产品依然毫无阻力，一路碾压。这些数据无疑会让大西洋两岸的一些西方领导人感到不快。就在特朗普与习近平会晤一个月后，两国脆弱的贸易休战协议得以延长，9月份中国对美国的出口增长了39.65%。近期与欧洲达成协议减少中国汽车出口的欧洲，对欧洲的出口也呈现蓬勃发展：增长了25.25%，达到七个月来的最高水平。

至于对东盟国家的出口，其增幅继续领跑，高达52.26%。这主要是因为，除了密切的贸易联系外，包括越南在内的一些东盟国家还是对美出口的门户，从而缓解了华盛顿和北京之间贸易战的影响。自特朗普入主白宫以来，这场贸易战愈演愈烈。随着上个月平陆运河的开通，成为中国商品输出的新通道，这种情况未来可能会进一步恶化。

这种热情导致价格飙升。集成电路的情况尤为明显：尽管9月份中国集成电路的销量仅增长了1%，但销售额却增长了136%。至于受到北京严格管控的稀土元素，其出口也持续增长，9月份增长了6.74%。

文章也指出，这些令人瞩目的业绩仅仅是中国商业活力的最新体现，但这个世界第二大经济体存在诸多脆弱迹象，正因如此，国际货币基金组织刚刚下调了对中国的经济增长预期。

**人类在工厂的工作是否即将机器人完全取代**

这是《费加罗报》一篇文章的主题。文章称，很难想象还有比这更具象征意义的场景。一位海信员工身穿防护服，戴着口罩，弯腰在生产线上，仔细查看眼前缓缓移动的电视面板，似乎完全没有注意到右侧的机器人及其两只机械臂。人与机器依然并肩工作。但这种状态还能持续多久呢？海信集团的一位工程师解释说：“他们的生产线的自动化程度目前在整个电视行业中是最高的：整体流程自动化程度为70%，关键环节则达到了100%。”

这个趋势已经蔓延到诸多行业。小米声称，其位于北京昌平区占地8万平方米的智能手机工厂已达到这一技术里程碑，该工厂平均每秒可生产一部手机。据报道，位于中国东北宁波的汽车制造商Zeekr在其工厂中运行数千台机器人，每天生产800辆电动汽车，自动化程度高达90%。特斯拉也声称其上海超级工厂的自动化程度达到95%，年产100万辆电动汽车。

海信也计划在其位于青岛的电视工厂实现这一目标，目标是在2030年实现，并预期将带来诸多益处。海信发言人介绍，“理论上，我们已经可以完全取代人工。但我们正在遵循一套精确的路线图：优先采用自动化来取代那些对质量或精度要求极高，以及需要进行体力劳动或质量控制的工作岗位。”

这篇文章最后指出，根据国际机器人联合会的数据，到2025年，中国工厂将安装35.4万台机器人，比上一年增长20%。中国占全球新增机器人安装量的60%，而美国仅占不到5%。 洛桑大学经济学家理查德·鲍德温教授在今年夏天发表的一项研究中解释道：“中国目前的工业就业正沿着与几十年前发达经济体相同的轨迹发展：随着生产率的提高，以及劳动密集型生产环节转移到工资水平较低的国家，工业就业正在下降。”他重申，与普遍的看法相反，北京并非从西方窃取工业就业岗位，而是窃取其生产能力。

务实的中国政府深知，自动化及其带来的生产率提升是抵消人口结构崩溃并维持其全球领导地位的唯一途径。中国工人是否会毫无抗拒地接受这一重大变革，还有待观察。

**法国人如何看中国汽车？**

另一篇《费加罗报》上与中国相关的文章继续关注巴黎国际汽车展上的中国车型比以往任何时候都更引起参观者的兴趣，文章标题为：中国汽车是“欧洲车的仿制品，但更好”。这并非是费加罗报的评论，而是引用一名车展参观者的评价。

本周，在总共60家巴黎国际车展参展商中，约有20个品牌来自中国，中国汽车强势亮相巴黎车展，吸引着那些主要追求性价比的法国消费者。许多中国品牌对法国大众来说还很陌生，是因为一些中国制造商首次在法国参展，但魅力攻势似乎对在巴黎车展上接受采访的法国消费者奏效了。一个关键论点反复出现：价格。

咨询公司C-Ways的首席执行官埃里克·尚帕诺（Éric Champarnaud）几天前在《费加罗报》报道中指出：“如今，35%到40%的法国人表示他们愿意购买中国汽车。” 当前油价飙升也间接惠及中国汽车制造商，推动了电动和混合动力汽车的销售，而这正是中国品牌的强项。

但面对中国汽车，一些法国车主仍然心存疑虑。究其原因，有参观者说 “这既是为了维护我的民族自豪感，也是因为我对中国车的可靠性有所怀疑。而且，这些品牌在法国的售后服务网络是否足够完善？还有零配件的供应问题。”

两位现已退休的前同事，58岁的布鲁诺和57岁的迪迪埃告诉《费加罗报》，中国车在外观设计方面也有待提高。“我觉得它们的设计过时了，很平淡。它们没有法国车那种独特的气质。”

也有两位《费加罗报》记者在车展上采访到的汽车行业人员认为中国汽车制造商“取得了长足的进步”，他们指出：“中国的车是欧洲车的仿制品，但更好一些，”

# AI demand highlights Taiwan's semiconductor capabilities: Lai

10/15/2026 04:00 PM

[](jsvscript:)[](jsvscript:)[](javascript:void(0))[Listen](javascript:)

President Lai Ching-te delivers remarks at the inauguration of Micron Technology Inc.’s new facility in Taichung on Thursday. CNA photo Oct. 15, 2026

Taichung, Oct. 15 (CNA) President Lai Ching-te (賴清德) said Thursday that as global demand for artificial intelligence (AI) grows, the world will increasingly rely on Taiwan for its comprehensive semiconductor capabilities and trusted supply chain.

Speaking at the inauguration of U.S. memory chipmaker Micron Technology Inc.'s new advanced assembly and testing facility in Taichung, Lai said Taiwan combines the world-leading advanced chip manufacturing and packaging technologies of Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. (TSMC) with Micron's continued investment in advanced memory.

The more the world needs AI, the more it needs Taiwan -- a trusted partner with complete industrial capabilities, Lai said.

The new facility, completed in just over a year, demonstrates Micron's commitment to Taiwan and will strengthen both the company's global competitiveness and Taiwan's semiconductor ecosystem, he added.

Micron has invested more than NT$1.4 trillion (US$43.18 billion) in Taiwan over the past three decades, reflecting its confidence in the country, Lai said.

He said chips and memory are both indispensable in the AI era, adding that the new facility will enhance advanced packaging and testing capabilities for high-bandwidth memory (HBM) to meet rising global AI demand.

Micron Technology Inc.'s new advanced assembly and testing facility in Taichung on Thursday. CNA photo Oct. 15, 2026

Lai noted that the government has extended its three major Taiwan investment incentive programs through 2027, expanding eligibility to overseas Taiwanese businesses and foreign companies while providing financing support and one-stop services to help address land, water and electricity needs.

He added that Micron has also secured funding under the Ministry of Economic Affairs' A+ Industrial Innovation R&D Program to accelerate HBM research and development in Taiwan, boosting investment and production capacity.

Lai also reiterated the government's "dual-engine" strategy of developing both high-tech and traditional industries, saying it aims to help precision manufacturers upgrade technologies and integrate into high-tech supply chains.

He called for closer cooperation between central and local governments, employers and workers to foster a healthy industrial environment, saying harmonious labor-management relations are essential to sustainable business growth.

(By Chao Li-yen and Evelyn Kao)

「[**偷拍**](https://udn.com/search/tagging/2/%E5%81%B7%E6%8B%8D)」公審以及證據問題常惹爭議。有[**香港**](https://udn.com/search/tagging/2/%E9%A6%99%E6%B8%AF)女子於[Threads](https://www.threads.com/@rachelywww/post/DeZGyJKAlxN?xmt=AQG0jSVbfig9lgkqP-8fjHIsyW2mfsW9Xq5_DYknM8tIrFT4ptzvSx83XV1D6VyQJzCvDAiB&slof=1)發布影片，公審在[**中環**](https://udn.com/search/tagging/2/%E4%B8%AD%E7%92%B0)卑利街被2名男子偷拍。雖然她最終未能在2名男子[**手機**](https://udn.com/search/tagging/2/%E6%89%8B%E6%A9%9F)中發現任何偷拍她的相片，但她認為只是對方在其不知情下刪除了相片，揚言「不知道他是怎麼把照片弄走（刪除）的，但他很明顯就是拍了我們啊」，並將男子樣貌放到網路公審，批評「就算被我當場抓到，他也會厚著臉皮否認。這些人能不能有點男子氣概啊！」

事件引起網友爭議，認為女子沒有證據證明男子偷拍，卻放到網路「公審」對方做法不妥當，「真的太扯了」、「那個男人到底要怎麼做，才能證明自己沒有偷拍？難道要靠發文者的主觀認定嗎？」、「沒有證據、毫無根據，就說人家偷拍」。還有網友發現，**女子身份為以18歲之齡參加《香港小姐2026》的KOL李欣穎（Rachel Li）**。

面對網友圍攻，李欣穎留言反駁「不要把猥瑣的偷拍行為包裝成合情合理的藉口」，又表示：「如果把手機轉交給別人，事後檢查不到就叫作沒做過，那這個世界上所有小偷偷完東西再把贓物丟掉，是不是就變清白了？」結果再觸發罵戰。

## 港姐參選人李欣穎拍片公審中環遭2男子偷拍

影片長約2分鐘，看到李欣穎追著2名被她指控「偷拍」的男人拍攝，並要求對方展示手機相簿。對方起初拒絕展示手機，重覆「I didn't take a picture（我沒有拍照）」，惟李欣穎追著拍攝對方相貌，爆粗罵「FXXK YOU」，男子則明言「I will sue you if you do that（如果妳那樣做，我會控告妳）」，再次強調「I didn't take a picture（我沒有拍照）」。

## 未發現男子偷拍證據 李欣穎：不知道他怎麼把照片刪除的，但很明顯就是偷拍

畫面一轉，男子向李欣穎展示手機相簿，未有發現任何拍攝她的照片，惟李欣穎形容對方是「已刪」照片，並非沒有拍攝，聲言「不知道他是怎麼把照片弄走（刪除）的，但他很明顯就是拍了我們啊」。

李欣穎又問男子如果沒有偷拍，為何要躲藏，對方否認躲藏，但李欣穎不接受解釋，表示會放上網路公審，明言「thank you for the reel content（感謝您提供影片題材）」。

## 男子多次否認偷伯 李欣穎：感謝提供影片題材

李欣穎事後補充，「他（男子）把手機交給他的朋友了，接著他的朋友就離開了，然後我們要追上去問他。那個時候我們顧不上其他事，他就說沒有（偷拍），手機裡全都是他家人的照片」。

## 李欣穎批男子羞恥無賴：香港真系太多偷拍狂

雖然找不到偷拍證據，但李欣穎批評男子「可恥」、「無賴」，「他（有家庭）還要出去這樣偷拍別人，真的很可恥啊，有損市容啊。可以當面問我要不要合照，但不要偷拍」，又聲稱不只1次被人偷拍，「香港真的有太多偷拍狂了。全部被我抓到的話，全部都會厚著臉皮否認。這些男人能不能有點男子氣概啊！」

## 網友圍攻李欣穎：沒有證據、毫無根據就說人家偷拍，難道妳的眼睛就是證據嗎？

不過李欣穎「公審」不成，反被大批網友圍攻，指摘她沒有證據就指控男子偷拍並「公審」，做法離譜，「妳拍不到他偷拍妳，妳就把影片放上網，不是大家就一定要支持妳。整段影片只看到妳追著別人、一直騷擾人家，人家都說沒有拍妳的照片了，妳卻硬說人家把照片刪掉了」、「妳真的太過分了，明明就是在誣賴人啊，想博取流量也不用這樣吧？現在是妳偷拍別人、妳騷擾別人，還誣賴人家，看到整段影片真的很生氣！」、「1. 妳沒有證據；2. 法例明文規定的是私密部位；3. 無罪推定原則」、「只知道妳在偷拍別人，不要整天覺得自己被人偷拍，好不好？」、「那個被拍的男人到底要怎麼做，才能證明自己沒有偷拍？難道要靠發文者的主觀認定嗎？」

## 李欣穎反擊網友：查不出來就代表沒做過嗎？

面對網友圍攻，李欣穎再強調男子有偷拍，「如果把手機轉交給別人，事後檢查不到就叫作沒做過，那這個世界上所有小偷偷完東西再把贓物丟掉，是不是就變清白了？」李欣穎又搬出香港法例中的「非法拍攝私密部位」及「窺淫罪」，強調「一般街拍和『偷拍』是兩回事，不要把猥瑣的偷拍行為包裝成合情合理的藉口」，結果網友罵聲更多。「不如妳先定義一下什麼是『私密部位』吧！」、「其實妳有沒有想過，妳這樣做會連真正需要幫助的女性也一起害了？」

## 非法拍攝私密部位、窺淫罪可監禁5年

根據《刑事罪行條例》（第200章）第159AA 條，「私密部位」定義為個人的生殖器官、臀部、肛門範圍或胸部（不論是露出或僅有內衣遮蔽），或個人所穿的、遮蔽著生殖器官、臀部、肛門範圍或胸部的內衣，明顯與一般「街拍」不同。

而根據香港法例第200章《刑事罪行條例》第159AAC條「非法拍攝或觀察私密部位」，任何人拍攝某名個人的私密部位，而拍攝情況是若非遭拍攝，該部位本來不是可讓人看到的，即屬犯罪，可處監禁5年。

另根據香港法例第200章《刑事罪行條例》第159AAB條「窺淫」，任何人拍攝某名個人的私密部位，或某名個人進行私密作為，即屬犯罪，同樣可處監禁5年。

content:
【大紀元2026年10月15日訊】今年5月、9月，美國總統川普和中共黨魁習近平實現了互訪。兩次「川習會」後，國際上對美台關係議論紛紛。儘管兩次「川習會」上，習近平都跟川普談了台灣問題，但是，並沒有改變美國政府對台灣的立場。相反，美台關係持續全面升級，至少有六大進展。

## **一、美台關係全面升級的六大進展**

### **第一，台灣對美國5000****億美元的投資承諾在兌現中。**

川普總統第二任期開始後，據美國官方數據，台灣對美國承諾的投資總額已達5000億美元。

7月16日，美國商務部宣布：台積電將在美國亞利桑那州追加1,000億美元投資，用於生產先進半導體及封裝設備。加上此前的投資承諾，台積電在美投資總額將達到2,650億美元，規劃廠區增至12座，成為美國歷史上規模最大的外來直接投資。

美國商務部的聲明稱，台積電的新增投資將給美國帶來數以萬計的就業機會，將先進半導體的製造帶回美國，並帶動數十億美元的間接經濟產出。

美國在台協會（AIT）處長谷立言（Raymond F. Greene）說，這項投資「充分展現美國與台灣對彼此的信任與信心，而這正是美台夥伴關係的核心」。

### **第二，台灣購買美國液化天然氣被稱為「史上最大的交易之一」。**

川普在阿拉斯加瓦西拉的集會上宣布：台灣已同意在未來20年內購買阿拉斯加液化天然氣管道項目約30%的產量。據路透社報導，川普稱這直接保證了該項目的徹底成功，也是史上最大的交易之一。

10月14日，台灣經濟部證實，台灣「中油股份有限公司」已於2025年3月簽署買賣暨投資意向書，歷經近一年半協商後取得重大進展。規劃內容包括項目投產後每年採購600萬噸液化天然氣，並參與項目開發，投資金額最高44億美元，最快2032年起供氣。

台灣經濟部強調，該項目可經太平洋航線直達台灣，有助於分散運輸路線與地緣供應風險。

### **第三，美國企業加大對台灣的投資力度。**

10月8日，美國總統川普在華盛頓舉行的「科學：新黃金時代」峰會上，向6位科技界領袖頒發了美國科學與技術領域的最高國家榮譽。

其中，兩位出生於台灣的美國科技巨頭——英偉達創始人兼首席執行官黃仁勳，超微半導體董事長兼首席執行官蘇姿丰，獲頒「國家科學獎章」。

黃仁勳的英偉達、蘇姿丰的超微，與台灣AI產業有千絲萬縷的聯繫。

英偉達絕大部分的高端圖形處理器與人工智能芯片，都交由台灣的台積電進行獨家或主要代工生產。英偉達在台灣的合作夥伴還包括鴻海、廣達、緯創、華碩、微星、技嘉等。

5月27日，黃仁勳在台北宣布：英偉達將在台灣建立總部並擴大投資，每年預估投入約1500億美元。

超微半導體在台灣的合作夥伴包括台積電、日月光、矽品、力成、欣興、景碩、緯創、緯穎、英業達、台達電、營邦等。

5月21日，蘇姿丰宣布：超微將在台灣AI產業投資超過100億美元，用於加速建置AI基礎設施與提升先進封裝產能。

10月6日，蘇姿丰再度訪台時表示，由於AI市場需求暴增，相關投資計劃進展順利並決定繼續調高投資金額。

谷歌、蘋果、微軟等美國的科技巨頭，都在台灣供應鏈中深度布局。

比如，谷歌在台灣設立了美國總部以外全球最大的硬件與AI基礎建設研發中心。蘋果在台灣設有研發中心和技術實驗室，且其全球有四分之一的供應鏈廠商位於台灣。微軟在台灣設有數據中心與亞洲首座AI研發中心。這些美國科技巨頭都在台灣持續投資。

### **第四，台美在無人機方面的合作取得新突破。**

俄烏戰爭使無人機在現代戰爭中的作用變得異常關鍵。受烏克蘭的啟發，台灣在無人機方面也迅速趕上。

台灣從2022年起啟動無人機計劃。台灣無人機的產量從2024年的約1萬架增加到2025年的超過12萬架，並計劃到2028年年產18萬架。

美國國防科技公司安杜里爾（Anduril）創辦人拉奇（Palmer Luckey）在一個國際論壇上說，面對地緣政治挑戰，台灣建構不對稱作戰能力的進展速度，「比我們合作的絕大多數國家都快得多，其中也包括美國」。

台積電被稱為台灣的「護國神山」。台灣正在迅速崛起的無人機產業群，有望成為台灣的又一座「護國神山」。

美台在無人機方面的合作，從天空到水面，從短程到遠程，從「美國設計，台灣製造」到「共同設計，台灣製造」，正全方位展開。

10月13日，《華爾街日報》報導，在與台灣合作開發海空無人機的美國業者中，安杜里爾對台無人機合約已逾10億美元。

同日，美國國防科技公司Shield AI正式宣布：已與台灣合作夥伴漢翔航空工業共同完成首架V-BAT垂直起降監偵無人機的設計、生產、組裝、測試；該無人機已運抵台灣海巡署。未來數月內，將陸續交付12架V-BAT給台灣海巡署。

V-BAT屬於第三級（Group 3）無人飛行系統，採用涵道風扇設計，並搭載重油引擎，主要用於情報、監視與偵察，以及目標鎖定等任務。

10月2日，美國國防科技企業AEVEX的成長策略資深副總裁安德斯（Craig Anders）宣布：將與台灣中光電智能機器人公司合作生產VANDAL與ONYX兩款無人機。不久前這兩款無人機已在台東太麻里進行過實際飛行展示。另外，由AEVEX生產的LYNX無人船已由美方交給台灣的海軍陸戰隊操作。

9月中旬，台灣最大造船企業「台灣國際造船股份有限公司」宣布：與美國國防科技公司Havoc AI建立合作夥伴關係，共同推動自主無人水面載具在台灣的生產、技術合作與維護保養。

據美國軍事媒體Defense News報導，傳統上是美國出口武器給台灣，但在無人機領域，未來可能出現相反方向。

### **第五，台灣對美國的出口大幅增長。**

至2026年9月，台灣出口連續35個月正成長，寫下史上最長成長週期。據台灣財政部的數據，台灣9月出口872.2億美元，年增60.9%，創歷年單月新高；累計前9月出口達6615.5億美元，年增46.2%；全年出口值有望達到9000億美元。

1—9月，台灣對美國出口總額達到2077.8億美元，史上首次在同期突破2000億美元大關，提前刷新了全年的歷史紀錄。台灣對美國的出超（順差）達1005.9億美元，首次超越對中國大陸及香港的出超。

去年，美國就成為台灣最大的貿易出口國。今年美國更是台灣出口的第一大客戶。

### **第六，美籍華裔女子張婉瑩因涉監視台灣總統之子被FBI****抓捕。**

10月4日，居住在美國加州爾灣的34歲房產經紀人張婉瑩，準備搭乘前往上海的航班時，在洛杉磯機場被美國聯邦調查局（FBI）探員逮捕。她被指控充當未註冊的中共代理人，涉嫌監控在西雅圖工作的台灣總統賴清德之子賴廷與。

FBI局長帕特爾（Kash Patel）在社交平台X上表示：「外國對手請注意，美國不再是你們可以安全從事間諜活動的地方。有人在美國領土上為中共監視外國領導人的家人，然後試圖搭乘航班返回上海。調查局將追查任何威脅美國國家安全的目標，無論其藏身何處，都將繩之以法。」

## **二、為什麼美台關係會有上述六大進展？**

主要原因可能有三：

### **第一，共享的價值觀是連結台美最關鍵的基石。**

10月7日晚，美國國務卿盧比奧在希臘雅典的帕特農神廟前發表了長達26分鐘的演講。這是一個對西方文明「尋根」的演講，也是一篇在西方文明的源頭試圖復興西方文明的檄文。

那麼，西方文明的根本是什麼呢？就是對上帝的信仰，以及在此基礎上形成的自由、民主、法治、人權等價值觀。

盧比奧演講的核心是，呼籲美國及其盟友共同復興這些在漫長歲月中被塵封、被遺忘、被扭曲、甚至被一些人拋棄了的核心價值觀，回歸常識、理性與傳統。

10月10日，台灣總統賴清德在中華民國115周年國慶大典上，以「台灣山巔之城，地上的鹽，世上的光」為題發表演講。

「山巔之城，地上的鹽，世上的光」，出自《聖經‧新約‧馬太福音》，是耶穌對門徒的教導。其核心涵義是：人應以善行實踐信仰，堅守良善，並以自身的言行為他人帶來正面影響。

賴清德的演講，與盧比奧的演講相呼應，講的都是回歸對神的信仰，守護自由、民主、法治、人權的價值觀。

美國是自由世界的領袖，台灣是以美國為首的自由世界的重要組成部分。共享的傳統價值與普世價值，是把美台連結起來的最重要的基石。

### **第二，共同面臨中共的挑戰是美台攜手合作的動力。**

現在，美國面臨的最大對手，就是中共；台灣面臨的最大威脅，也是中共。

蘇共解散、蘇聯解體後，中共成了全世界唯一的最大的共產主義政黨、中共國成了全世界唯一的最大的共產主義國家。

上世紀90年代以來，中共利用以美國為首的西方國家對中共採取的綏靖政策，利用加入世界貿易組織的機會，利用西方的市場、資本、技術、金融、服務等，迅速成為世界第二大經濟體。

美國是世界第一大經濟體，中共是世界第二大經濟體。習近平上台後，認為中共的「底氣」足了，「東升西降」了，「時與勢」在中共一邊，「當今世界最大的亂源在美國」，「美國是我國發展和安全最大的威脅」，於是，開始在全球範圍內跟美國爭奪霸主地位。

2020年大瘟疫大爆發後，中共發起對美國的新冷戰。標誌性的事件有五：第一，1—2月，中共軍艦挺進太平洋中部的中途島軍演。第二，3月，宣布南海戰略核潛艇的「堡壘海區」建成。第三，6月，宣布對美國太空戰部署完成。第四，7月開始，從渤海到黃海到東海到南海到內地，發起40多年來最密集的軍演。第五，8月25日，《人民日報》發表批判美國的長文，中心思想是：美國最壞，「中共國」最好。

同一年，中共在暴力鎮壓香港反送中運動後，在香港強推「港版國安法」，提前27年終結了香港的「一國兩制」，以中共「一黨專政」取而代之。

同一年，中共在拿下資本主義的香港之後，立即將目標瞄準資本主義的台灣，在渤海、黃海、台海、南海發動了有史以來最密集的軍演，開始對台灣極限施壓，企圖以中共的一黨專政取代台灣的自由民主。

中共若拿下台灣，決不會止步。接下來，就是以台灣為據點，近處威脅日本、韓國、菲律賓等，更大範圍將突破美國在二戰後設立的防衛共產主義擴張的第一島鏈，進而直接威脅資本主義的美國，建立一個以中共為主導的「人類命運共同體」。

中共所謂的「人類命運共同體」是什麼？就是中共老祖宗馬克思講的「解放全人類」的另一種說法。

中共為什麼在拿下資本主義的香港之後，要拿下資本主義的台灣，並與資本主義的美國爭奪世界霸權呢？

因為中共的老祖宗馬克思仇恨資本主義、反對資本主義、必欲戰勝資本主義，最後要取代資本主義，建立社會主義、共產主義的一統天下。

台灣處在西方的自由民主與中共的專制極權對峙的最前沿。美國則在全球範圍內，從雅典，到羅馬，到美洲大陸，面對著中共無孔不入的滲透與顛覆。

守護台灣，就是守護美國，守護自由民主。

如何守護？

在投資、能源、無人機生產、科技、經貿、打擊中共間諜上，全面合作，深度融合，你中有我，我中有你，共同築起對抗共產主義的銅牆鐵壁，乃必然之道。

### **第三，世界第一強國與世界最強勁經濟增長體的強強聯手。**

美國是當今世界上的第一強國。美國強在哪裡？首先，美國人民享有信仰自由、言論自由、免於恐懼的自由、免於匱乏的自由；其次，美國的國父們給美國留下了一個防止專制獨裁極權的有效的分權與制衡的民主政治制度；再次，在自由民主的基礎上，美國有世界上最發達的科技，最強大的軍事實力，最具影響力的金融，最優秀的人才資源，最有消費能力的龐大的市場等。

台灣是當今世界上經濟增長最強勁的地區之一。

據國際貨幣基金組織（IMF）2026年10月發布的《世界經濟展望》報告，台灣2026年的實質GDP增長率預測被大幅上調至10.7%，這一增長率不僅在亞太地區高居榜首，也使台灣成為全球範圍內極為罕見的實現雙位數增長的經濟體。

這一增長速度遠超全球絕大多數主要經濟體。美國預測增長為2.3%，中國預測增長為4.5%，歐元區預測增長為1.1%，印度預測增長為7.0%。

台灣作為全球經濟增長最強勁的經濟體，自然願意與世界第一強國，實現強強聯手了。

## **結語**

現在總有人從川普與習近平關於台灣問題的談話中揣摩美台關係的走向。其實，美台關係不在於川普怎麼說，而在於美國政府與台灣政府實際怎麼做。

現在有一個說法，台灣產業角色正從單純的「Made in Taiwan」代工，轉向以戰略夥伴身分深度嵌入美方核心供應鏈，即「Made with Taiwan」。這個說法很有道理。

如今，美台正在投資、能源、貿易、科技、無人機、安全等各方面相互融合，形成一個共生共成、互利互惠、彼此守護的整體。

綜上，儘管仍有各種挑戰，美台合作的前景仍讓外界看好。

大紀元首發

资料照片：来自密歇根州的共和党众议员约翰·穆勒纳尔(John Moolenaar)在众议院中国问题特设委员会举行的听证会上向证人提问。(2023年2月28日)

美国国会众议院美国与中共战略竞争特设委员会主席约翰·穆勒纳尔(John Moolenaar)呼吁美国战争部扩大一份涉及研究安全的管控清单，将更多被指与中国国防科研体系存在关联的高校、实验室、科研机构及人才引进计划纳入其中，以防止美国纳税人资助的科研成果被中国政府或军方利用。

穆勒纳尔星期三(10月14日)公布了写给战争部长皮特·海格塞斯(Pete Hegseth)的[信函](https://chinaselectcommittee.house.gov/media/press-releases/moolenaar-calls-for-pentagon-to-update-its-list-of-pla-linked-institutions-and-talent-recruitment-programs)。他建议战争部在“第1286条清单”(Section 1286 List)中增加14家被特设委员会认定为中共“核心国防合作伙伴”的中国科学院下属研究所、62家实验室和国防实验室、58所大学、22项外国恶意人才引进计划，以及中国国家留学基金管理委员会(CSC)和获得该机构资助的研究人员。

穆勒纳尔说，扩大清单的目的是加强美国的研究安全，防止中国及其他外国对手利用战争部资助的科研成果。

**清单直接影响战争部研究经费**

“第1286条清单”依据2019财政年度《国防授权法》第1286条设立，用于识别美国政府认定对国家安全构成风险的外国科研机构、企业、个人和人才引进计划。

从2026财政年度开始，战争部不得为涉及清单内实体的基础研究项目提供资金。这项限制适用于研究拨款、合同及其他形式的资助，并禁止受资助机构与清单内实体共同开展研究或使用对方设备。研究人员如果与清单内机构的人员合作，也可能影响其获得联邦科研经费的资格。

战争部今年7月更新了清单，目前列有中国、俄罗斯和伊朗的130所高校和科研机构。战争部8月还要求30所美国高校审查其与外国机构的学术、资金和科研联系，并采取整改措施。

穆勒纳尔赞扬战争部近年来强化科研安全评估，并限制接受战争部资助的研究人员与美国政府管控清单上的机构合作。

“在这些努力中，战争部的‘第1286条清单’发挥着核心作用，”穆勒纳尔在信中说。“一个实体是否被列入清单，可能直接决定接受战争部资助的研究人员能否与该实体保持科研合作关系。”

他表示，随着列入清单产生的实际后果日益扩大，清单是否完整、准确也变得更加重要。

“这一框架能否发挥作用，不仅取决于对清单内实体施加的限制，也取决于战争部能否识别并认定符合相关标准的外国机构，”穆勒纳尔说。他警告，清单存在的覆盖缺口可能为接受战争部资助的研究人员和机构留下继续与中国相关组织合作的渠道。

**涉及军工、半导体、量子和人工智能**

穆勒纳尔说，特设委员会发现，一些尚未被列入清单的中国科研机构，与中国的国防科研和工业体系存在有记录的隶属、监管、协议或其他重要联系。

他要求战争部审查的机构包括中国科学院下属研究所，以及从事武器、航空航天、高超音速技术、半导体、水下系统、电子战等军事相关研究的实验室。名单还包括由中国国家国防科技工业局(SASTIND)共同管理或支持的高校。

人才引进计划部分则主要涉及量子技术和人工智能等关键及新兴技术领域。

穆勒纳尔说：“以下列出的几类机构尤其值得关注，因为它们与国防体系的关联已经得到美国政府或其他研究安全机构的记录和证实。”

据路透社报道，穆勒纳尔建议增加的58所高校包括清华大学。战争部目前尚未宣布是否接受他的建议；信中提到的机构也并未因为特设委员会的提名而自动受到限制。是否列入清单仍须由战争部依据相关法定标准进行认定。

近年来，美国国会和行政部门不断加强对外国政府参与美国科研项目的审查，重点包括隐瞒外国资金来源、参加外国人才计划、知识产权转移，以及敏感或军民两用技术可能流向外国军方等问题。

中国驻美使馆此前在回应战争部要求美国高校审查外国合作关系时，指责美方将国家安全概念泛化，并把正常的科学、教育和学术交流政治化。北京呼吁美国为两国学术与科研合作提供开放、公平和非歧视性的环境。这一表态并非针对穆勒纳尔最新信函作出。

**要求限制国家留学基金委受资助人员**

除了扩大机构名单，穆勒纳尔还要求战争部禁止任何接受中国国家留学基金管理委员会资助或其他经济支持的研究人员、研究生和博士后参与战争部资助的科研项目。

他主张，这项限制应在有关人员接受中方资助期间持续有效，无论他们是否被正式列为项目负责人、共同研究人员或其他具名参与者。

穆勒纳尔说，中国国家留学基金管理委员会不同于一般国际学生资助项目。该机构近年来因涉及学术自由、对留学生的监控、意识形态要求和潜在间谍活动等指控，在美国受到越来越严格的审查。

content:
La revista de prensa "Tribuna Libre" es una hemeroteca virtual, con acceso gratuito, que ofrece el texto completo de los principales artículos de opinión publicados en diversos medios de comunicación. Forma parte del [proyecto educativo y de investigación](https://www.almendron.com/asociacion.php) de la Asociación Cultural sin ánimo de lucro «Almendrón».

In this pool photograph distributed by the Russian state agency Sputnik, Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi (right) shakes hands with Chinese President Xi Jinping during a welcome ceremony before the start of the 18th BRICS summit in New Delhi on Sept. 12. Alexander Kazakov/Pool/AFP via Getty

Last month’s BRICS summit marked the pinnacle of an ongoing reset in China-India relations. Chinese President Xi Jinping made his first visit to India in almost seven years for the summit. That visit followed Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s trip to China last year—also his first in seven years—to attend the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) summit in Tianjin.

The partial renormalization of relations comes after the two countries’ border conflagration in 2020, which was the worst flare-up of hostilities between both countries in more than four decades. Steps taken to revive relations have included the resumption of direct flights and a relaxation of visa and investment restrictions. Even the intractable border issue has seen substantive progress, as noted by the meeting between Indian National Security Advisor Ajit Doval and Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi in August, which produced an eight-point [consensus](https://x.com/EOIBeijing/status/2092626800711225488) as part of their Special Representatives framework. The same month, trade along three border passes [resumed](https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-news/india-china-cross-border-trade-resumes-after-6-years-101785637096016.html) after a gap of six years.

On a global level, too, China’s and India’s leaders have had something of a meeting of minds on many issues to do with the international order. At the BRICS summit in India, the 140-point [New Delhi Declaration](https://www.mea.gov.in/bilateral-documents?dtl/41776/BRICS_New_Delhi_Declaration_Building_for_Resilience_Innovation_Cooperation_and_Sustainability_September_12_2026) made several references to the Trump administration’s disruptive foreign policies. These included the need for strengthening a “predictable and rules-based multilateral trading system”, condemning the “imposition of unilateral coercive measures that are contrary to international law”, and expressing “concern about ongoing conflicts in many parts of the world and the current state of polarization and fragmentation in the international order”.

Yet while engagement at the bilateral and global level continues to gain momentum, an overlooked area of engagement is the need for greater cooperation at the regional level. The recent flash floods in Nepal triggered by a glacial collapse near the Chinese border, for example, highlighted the need for a shared Himalayan water diplomacy framework.

After initial apprehension from Kathmandu to accepting foreign aid, China and India have emerged as key sources of humanitarian assistance following that disaster. However, this is being done in [parallel](https://foreignpolicy.com/2026/09/01/nepal-tibet-floods-china-india-disaster-response-border-dispute/) rather than in coordination.

Speaking at the U.N. General Assembly in late September, Nepali Prime Minister Balendra Shah [called](https://kathmandupost.com/national/2026/09/25/balendra-shah-un-speech-full-transcript-of-nepal-prime-minister-s-address-to-the-81st-un-general-assembly) for a Himalayan Climate Resilience Mechanism, led by Nepal, China, and India, to share satellite data and expertise to monitor glacial lakes and strengthen joint early-warning systems. Forums such as the International Centre for Integrated Mountain Development—[based](https://www.icimod.org/) in Nepal and comprising eight member states, including China and India—are well positioned to play such a role. Given the long-standing climate of mistrust in the bilateral relationship, projects will need to be assessed on a case-by-case basis and avoid disputed or sensitive territories. But this approach offers a “win-win” solution. It helps prevent India becoming further marginalized in its own neighborhood while facilitating a greater degree of transparency and accountability for an expanded roster of Chinese initiatives in the region.

Over the last decade, China has emerged as a leading trade, investment, and defense partner for most countries in South Asia. Beijing’s keen interest in the region is fueled by a combination of the need to maintain a stable periphery, seeking markets for its exports and investments, and securing alternative trade routes to overcome what then-Chinese President Hu Jintao referred to as a “[Malacca Dilemma](https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/full/10.1080/14799850802006555)”. From New Delhi’s perspective, Beijing’s interests in South Asia are also driven by latent efforts to challenge India’s position in the region, once referred to as a “[String of Pearls](https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/full/10.1080/09700160801886314)” strategy of strategic encirclement. To its credit, New Delhi has moved away from the era of viewing South Asia as its exclusive sphere of influence while demonstrating a growing willingness to partner with like-minded countries on development and infrastructure initiatives in South Asia. For example, it is working with [Japan](https://www.business-standard.com/economy/news/japan-pm-s-india-visit-northeast-high-on-agenda-during-modi-takaichi-talks-126063001011_1.html) through the Act East Forum on infrastructure projects in India’s geopolitically sensitive northeast. But New Delhi still maintains an aversion to an expanded Chinese role in South Asia, given the history of bad blood in the Sino-Indian relationship.

New Delhi’s futile attempts to keep China out of the region have prompted Beijing to develop its own regional initiatives that exclude India. The China-Pakistan Economic Corridor, established in 2015, was an early example of this, forming a key pillar of its Belt and Road Initiative. This has now been supplemented by newer initiatives, such as [trilateral](https://mofa.gov.pk/press-releases/inaugural-meeting-of-bangladesh-china-pakistan-trilateral-mechanism-held-on-19-june-2025?mission=chengdu) dialogues with Bangladesh and Pakistan as well as with Afghanistan and Pakistan.

China’s engagement with South Asia has also served to strengthen regional connectivity through infrastructure projects. An example is the [Colombo International Container Terminal](https://www.cict.lk/) in Sri Lanka, which is financed and operated through a joint venture between China Merchants Holdings and the Sri Lanka Ports Authority. In Bangladesh, China is also overseeing the modernization of [Mongla Port](https://today.thefinancialexpress.com.bd/public/print/china-backed-project-to-develop-mongla-port-as-regional-hub-experts-1746558248), the country’s second-largest seaport.

This engagement extends to a people-to-people level. When visiting Kathmandu recently, I was surprised to find a dedicated immigration line at the airport for Chinese nationals (alongside separate lines for Indian and Nepali nationals). China has been convening the [China-South Asia Expo](https://www.csa-expo.com/en/) trade fair in Kunming since 2013, and several Chinese academic institutions also maintain South Asia [institutes](https://www.siis.org.cn/researchEn/17.jspx). Beijing is even playing an increasingly active mediation role, as noted in the case of recent hostilities between Afghanistan and Pakistan. Beijing also claims to have played such a role during the brief India-Pakistan conflict in 2025 (although New Delhi has [disputed](https://www.timesnownews.com/india/had-no-role-government-sources-reject-chinas-mediation-claim-on-india-pakistan-ceasefire-article-153374297) this).

South Asia’s hub-and-spokes political geography—with India being the only country that shares a border with every other state in the region—makes India central to South Asia’s regional architecture. However, New Delhi’s often strained relations with its neighbors and China’s expanded role in the region have prompted some to [ponder a South Asian regional architecture without India](https://foreignpolicy.com/2025/10/20/india-region-bangladesh-pakistan/). Such views have been fueled by the fact that South Asia’s primary regional forum—the South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation (SAARC)—has not held a summit since 2014, following a breakdown in India-Pakistan relations. India’s resistance to working with Pakistan has been the primary obstacle to SAARC’s revival (although New Delhi argues that Islamabad’s support for terrorism is the original sin).

In reality, most countries in the region seek to maintain cordial relations with both China and India. Much is said about India’s commitment to [strategic autonomy](https://foreignpolicy.com/2025/11/26/india-end-strategic-autonomy/) in its foreign policy. However, other South Asian countries also have a long-standing tradition of pursuing a multialigned foreign policy. While a handful of countries are in the “China camp” (Pakistan) or “India camp” (Bhutan), most seek to engage both as a means of meeting their development needs while preserving their autonomy. In this context, regimes in the region remain averse to any push to choose between major powers or, worse, carve the region (or for that matter the world) into competing spheres of influence.

Indeed, historically, the smaller states of South Asia have sought to leverage the Sino-Indian rivalry to extract concessions from both countries. This has not always worked in practice, amid concerns about Beijing’s opaque lending practices; Sri Lanka’s Hambantota project, for instance, became synonymous with China’s “[debt trap](https://www.ft.com/content/e150ef0c-de37-11e7-a8a4-0a1e63a52f9c)” diplomacy. Greater China-India alignment in South Asia offers a means to alleviate these concerns.

When considering specific projects the two countries could work on together, water is one area of particular need.

As an upper riparian state, China should be included in discussions about shared river systems in South Asia. So far, these efforts have been largely bilateral: the Indus Waters Treaty between India and Pakistan and Ganga Water Treaty between India and Bangladesh, for example. Both of these happen to be in limbo, with New Delhi putting the former in abeyance following last year’s India-Pakistan hostilities, while the latter is due to expire in December. Still, a multilateral approach that includes China is required—particularly given the fact that most of the major river systems of South Asia originate in China.

India has direct interests in this given China’s construction of the world’s largest hydroelectric power project across a river (the Brahmaputra/Yarlung Tsangpo) that traverses both countries. And a recent agreement to resume sharing hydrological data between both countries, alongside reviving an expert-level mechanism on trans-border rivers, is a step in the right direction.

Another area of alignment is development. As with the response to the Nepal floods, both countries are often pursuing development initiatives in parallel. An example of this is the Koshi Corridor, a highway and power transmission project in eastern Nepal, with India’s Export-Import Bank providing a [line of credit](https://www.indembkathmandu.gov.in/commerce-wing-brief) to finance the electricity transmission line and China pledging to finance portions of the road project. Ideally, this should be an area of cooperation, especially given that the road project aims to [connect](https://peoplesreview.com.np/2026/05/19/nepals-shortest-india-china-route-biratnagar-kimathanka-track-opens/) India and China through Nepal.

title: Anatomy of a lie: how misinformation is spreading through US midterm campaigns
summary: W here is James Talarico? The question ricocheted around rightwing echo chambers before metastasising into a conspiracy theory – and a reminder of the persistent danger of disinformation in the [US midterm elections.](https://www.theguardia
content:
W here is James Talarico? The question ricocheted around rightwing echo chambers before metastasising into a conspiracy theory – and a reminder of the persistent danger of disinformation in the [US midterm elections.](https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/us-midterm-elections-2026)

The smear campaign began when Talarico, [the Democratic candidate](https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/mar/04/texas-primaries-democrats-texas) for the US Senate in Texas, was not seen in public for nine days. His campaign was slow to explain why. While nature abhors a vacuum, Donald Trump and social media seize on one and weaponise it.

On 30 September, Talarico spoke at a Hispanic Business Council event by video. He had been diagnosed with the flu at an urgent care facility in Dallas after “starting to feel kind of under the weather a few days ago”, he said, and would not appear in person because he had a fever and was still contagious.

On 7 October, the president held a rally in San Antonio, Texas, and claimed without evidence that “Tala-freako”, as he nicknames the Democrat, is vegan. [Trump asserted](https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/oct/08/donald-trumps-texas-rally-rocked-by-repeated-protests): “He’s sick because he’s been forced to eat meat for political reasons and he’s throwing up all over the place.”

On the same day, an X account with the username “Dan The Man, Always with a Plan” and a photo of “Trump 2028” cap tweeted without evidence: “He had a mental health crisis. That is what I heard from someone who would know inside information.”

On 8 October, Steve Bannon, a former White House chief strategist, stirred the pot further on his influential War Room podcast in an interview with former Trump fundraiser Caroline Wren, [who baselessly claimed](https://x.com/RealAmVoice/status/2108313243382952207?s=20): “I’m hearing that he checked himself into a mental institution – that he had a full-blown, like, mental breakdown.”

On the same day, Ken Paxton, the Republican running against Talarico, weighed in with [a social media post](https://x.com/KenPaxtonTX/status/2108250407277588546?s=20) that showed Talarico on a “Wanted” poster and said: “Jimmy appears to be having a full-blown mental Tala-freak-out on the national stage. My campaign has a simple request: proof of life.”

On 9 October, Spencer Pratt, a former candidate for mayor of Los Angeles, [offered his take](https://x.com/spencerpratt/status/2108553958696399249?s=20): “My sources are telling me Talarico is in a mental health facility. His campaign has stopped actively planning events in the vital homestretch of the campaign.”

Democratic Senate candidate James Talarico speaks during a campaign rally at the Cailloux theater on 31 August. Photograph: Brandon Bell/Getty Images

Right media sites swung into action. RedState, the Daily Wire, the Right Scoop, Twitchy and PJ Media all amplified the false claims. Elon Musk, the world’s richest man, put more toxins in the bloodstream with posts such as: “The Talarico campaign is hiding something big that voters ought to know about.”

Then, on 11 October, came the supposed coup de grâce. Conservative social media influencer Nick Sortor posted a 47-second audio clip on X that he said proved that Talarico had been discharged earlier in the week from [Lindner Center of Hope](https://lindnercenterofhope.org/), a mental health treatment centre in Mason, Ohio.

The call was placed by Rhein Amacher, a self-described “right-wing provocateur”. In the clip, a woman whom Sorter claimed was an employee there says it looked like Talarico “was just discharged this evening”. The online Maga faithful were jubilant.

But not for long. The Bulwark obtained the full phone call showing the purported employee had repeatedly denied any record of Talarico being at the centre. The timeline also did not add up. Amacher said he made the call to the mental health centre on Saturday evening, but Talarico was seen at the Austin City Limits music festival on Friday. On Saturday, he made an appearance at a Kacey Musgraves concert in Dallas.

The Lindner Center of Hope [wrote in an X post](https://x.com/LindnerCtrHope/status/2109430626562785517?s=20) on Sunday that Talarico “has never received treatment” from the facility. Talarico replied to the post, saying, “I’ve never even been to Ohio.” He included a tears of joy emoji.

JT Ennis, a spokesperson for Talarico, called Sorter’s claim “a lie designed to promote a pathetic conspiracy theory” in an X post and wrote that Talarico had been recovering from the flu at his home in Austin. Talarico has type 1 diabetes, placing him at higher risk for flu-related complications.

Even Maga followers began to acknowledge that the claim had collapsed. But if the episode appeared absurd, its implications for the midterms were serious.

[Reed Galen](https://x.com/reedgalen), a former Republican strategist and cofounder of the Lincoln Project, an anti-Trump group, said: “It was a bit wild but a good reminder to all of us how sophisticated, effective and efficient the rightwing/ bot/ Russian generated misinformation-disinformation machine is.

“This story came from some weirdos in Ohio or whatever but the point is that someone or something picked it up and amplified it to a point where – despite no evidence of reality – it became something that was an issue in the [Texas](https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/texas) Senate campaign.”

Galen added: “Even if Talarico wins, that in and of itself was a win for the tactic. If you have the ability and the willingness to do this stuff, it’s not gonna work every time, but if you do it a lot, sometimes you’re gonna have success, and sometimes those successes might be strategic in nature, not just tactical.”

Disinformation has been rampant in elections for at least a decade and 2026 is no different. NewsGuard, a company that tracks online misinformation, says it has identified and debunked [25 false claims](https://www.newsguardtech.com/special-reports/2026-elections-misinformation-tracker/) about the midterms that have gone viral on social media platforms.

Its list of false claims includes [Abdul El-Sayed](https://www.theguardian.com/profile/abdul-el-sayed), the Democratic candidate for US Senate in Michigan, having called for sharia law in the US during a 2022 speech; a Dominion Voting Systems whistleblower accusing US politicians of taking millions of dollars in bribes to rig the 2026 midterm elections; and Ken Paxton’s Senate campaign paying for a Texas billboard that says “Pedos Ain’t That Bad”.

Another example related to an image that purportedly showed Rob Sand, a centrist Democratic candidate for governor of Iowa, campaigning with the progressives Ilhan Omar and Tim Walz. NewsGuard found it was generated by artificial intelligence (AI).

Even as AI gives new tools to nefarious actors, defences have been weakened. Last year, US secretary Marco Rubio [shut down](https://www.reuters.com/business/media-telecom/us-state-department-closing-office-aimed-countering-foreign-disinformation-2025-04-16/) the state department’s Counter Foreign Information Manipulation and Interference office, accusing it of censorship and wasting US taxpayer money.

Major tech platforms – notably Musk’s X and Mark Zuckerberg’s Meta – have gutted trust, safety and factchecking teams, turning online spaces into a lawless wild west. Musk has [spent a record $366m](https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/oct/13/elon-musk-political-donor-midterm-elections) in ⁠the election cycle so far to help Republicans retain control of Congress.

[Richard Hasen](https://law.ucla.edu/faculty/faculty-profiles/richard-l-hasen), a professor at UCLA School of Law and election law expert, said: “When you’ve got Elon Musk owning one of the important social media platforms and being a vector for spreading the misinformation, and also when you’ve got the companies like Meta no longer doing the same kind of trust and safety work, it’s just an atmosphere where this kind of stuff can spread.”

But there is another, more optimistic perspective. While the Talarico rumours spread like wildfire in corners of the internet, they did not penetrate the mainstream media, and fizzled out once the reality became clear.

Hasen added: “The Talarico case shows the limits of being able to do this. This was something that was easily disproven and could have potentially even backfired, showing that the anti-Talarico forces are so desperate that they have to make up a false claim to try to boost a weak candidate.

“Every election now we’re hearing it’s going to be ‘the AI election’ and voters are going to be tricked. What I think is happening in part is that everyone’s on their guard. We all know that we can’t necessarily believe our eyes or our ears and things that a politician might appear to say or do might not necessarily be true, so that’s a little bit of a natural check.”

Hasen points out that candidates are better equipped to dismantle digital lies. To debunk the rumour, Talarico shared home security camera footage with the New York Times, establishing his presence at home. “Because we’re leaving digital footprints everywhere, that sometimes could be another way to debunk a rumour.”

[Tara Setmayer](https://www.tarasetmayer.com/), a former Republican communications director on Capitol Hill, also believes that the conspiracy theories have lost their novelty value. “The voters have become hip to this game,” she said. “There are too many other negative things going on in everyday American lives, so I don’t think these types of cheap attacks are going to resonate at this point.

“The difference between this election cycle and past election cycles is that, because it seems like we’ve been here before and we know how batshit crazy Maga can be, that mainstream media isn’t platforming the crazy as often,” said Setmayer._“_ They’re actually reporting it in a way with the healthy amount of scepticism that it deserves, so it’s dismissed off the top whereas in the past it was so novel.”

Setmayer added: “At this point now it feels like [Donald Trump](https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/donaldtrump) and Maga’s greatest hits: we’re really in the fat Elvis period of the Maga election campaign tactics and it’s obvious to everyone. The absurdity is finally breaking through even with some Republican voters, evidenced by how terrible Donald Trump’s numbers are and Republicans writ large.”

title: What’s Going On With China’s Military Exercises This Week? - Domino Theory
summary: Many in Taiwan have treated Chinese military exercises this week as significant, following President Lai Ching-te’s (賴清德) National Day speech. But analysis of the location and timing of the drills suggests they are more routine than they ar
content:
Many in Taiwan have treated Chinese military exercises this week as significant, following President Lai Ching-te’s (賴清德) National Day speech. But analysis of the location and timing of the drills suggests they are more routine than they are extraordinary.

“China launches 5-day military exercises after Taiwan’s National Day,” read one typical [headline](https://www.rti.org.tw/en/news?uid=3&pid=237144), from Radio Taiwan International. Reuters [described](https://www.reuters.com/world/china/taiwan-says-it-is-closely-monitoring-series-chinese-live-fire-drills-2026-10-12/) “a series of Chinese live-fire drills,” based on navigation restriction notices published by the China Maritime Safety Administration for five zones in different regions. These areas are all close to China’s coast and range from the Bohai Sea in the north to the South China Sea in the south.

The Chinese Communist Party’s decision to conduct live-fire drills immediately after the National Day address “does nothing to advance regional peace and will only heighten regional tensions,” said Chuang Jui-hsiung (莊瑞雄), head of the Democratic Progressive Party caucus, speaking at a [press conference](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eYyNoOU-StY) on Monday about a different National Day speech by opposition leader Han Kuo-yu (韓國瑜).

In [previous years](https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cvgd4yn45qlo), China has launched major military exercises around Taiwan after National Day, framing them as a response to perceived provocations in the president’s speech.

But is that actually what is happening here?

There are some problems with this theory.

As all the coverage acknowledges, these drills are neither around nor close to Taiwan. China has not publicly commented on the exercises this week, nor tied them to Lai’s speech.

The five drill areas described appear to be a partial snapshot of scheduled Chinese military activity at sea this week. A comprehensive review of the Maritime Safety Administration’s website by Domino Theory revealed a total of 12 relevant notices published before Monday. Four of them were for live-fire exercises, the remaining eight were for non-specified military training. The drills are of varying lengths of time, some even extending longer than seven days.

In September, 28 navigation restriction notices were published for live-fire exercises alone. It doesn’t appear that any of these were reported on as being unusual, despite there being broad crossover in the locations involved with the “five” this week.

“I don’t see anything in these notices that strikes me as particularly unusual or significant,” Ethan Connell for Taiwan Security Monitor, a group at George Mason University, told Domino Theory.

The Maritime Safety Administration regularly issues navigation warnings for live-fire exercises and military training, Connell said in a written response, adding “there isn’t much evidence that these five exercises are part of any larger, coordinated training or operation.”

Taiwan’s defense minister, Wellington Koo (顧立雄), told the legislature on Monday that the drills appear to be a “not particularly large,” routine exercise, adding that Taiwan must be cautious and will continue to monitor the situation, adding, “You can see that the timing was deliberately chosen to follow the October 10th National Day address.”

The drills “are likely a response to Lai’s speech, which is to be expected,” said Lyle Morris, a senior fellow at the Asia Society Policy Institute’s Center for China Analysis. “But nothing to panic about.”

The number of exercises is noteworthy, Morris said, but doesn’t rise to the level of something like the “[Joint Sword](https://dominotheory.com/china-announces-military-exercises-around-taiwan/)” drills from previous years. Those were among the exercises that took place around Taiwan.

Other analysts disagree about the timing.

“I would not interpret these as exercises targeting President Lai Ching-te,” said Chieh Chung (揭仲), a fellow at the Institute for National Defense and Security Research think tank in Taipei.

Chieh wrote to Domino Theory that [Lai’s speech](https://dominotheory.com/taiwan-intent-on-increasing-defense-spending/) had been uncontroversial this year, but pointed out: “Leaving observers to speculate whether the drills were triggered by Beijing’s displeasure with President Lai’s speech is enough for Beijing to achieve its objective.”

Lai’s only significant mention of China was to say it was engaged in authoritarian expansion, applying pressure “through military and gray-zone activities in an attempt to alter the status quo across the Taiwan Strait.”

“Most notices were issued before Lai’s speech, so the drills look routine,” said Ben Lewis, who runs the website [PLATracker](https://www.platracker.com/), which records Chinese military activity around Taiwan. Lewis doesn’t think that the drills are any more significant than they look. But he warned that a closure moving into the Strait or near Taiwan would change this view.

“The CCP disguises its intrusive actions under the pretexts of law enforcement and scientific research, attempting to expand its operational scope during non-conflict periods and create the illusion of de facto jurisdiction,” the Defense Ministry told Domino Theory, answering a question on whether the five drill areas were different in some way. “These moves severely undermine the international order and challenge our law enforcement authority within our waters.”

The Chinese military near Taiwan had been relatively quiet earlier this week, according to [data](https://x.com/MoNDefense/status/2109811367033143387?s=20) published by the Ministry of National Defense, although its data for [yesterday](https://x.com/MoNDefense/status/2110536140809719853?s=20) showed more activity, including a circumnavigation of Taiwan by an [uncrewed aerial vehicle](https://x.com/jointstaffpa/status/2110355583971053644?s=20), or UAV.

China has also this week deployed a carrier battle group into the Western Pacific, centered around the Liaoning aircraft carrier. Based on [information](https://x.com/jointstaffpa/status/2110317371932205415?s=20) published by the Japanese military, the battle group passed through the Okinawa archipelago and was located approximately 370 kilometers to the east of Taiwan on Wednesday.

Taiwan’s data for Chinese activity do not routinely show information about ship type and location, unlike the data for aircraft. Wednesday’s data do not appear to show any flights by Chinese naval aviation east of but close to Taiwan. Taiwan’s Defense Ministry said today that it wouldn’t comment on specifics of the carrier’s activity.

Jason Wang, the chief operating officer of geointelligence firm ingeniSPACE, said it was wrong to associate the drills with the National Day speech and that tying the two together helped with United Front narratives. “These drills were planned and should be seen in the context of raising overall readiness,” Wang said.

Experts contacted for this story did not think the five drill areas reported on this week are different or more significant than the other announced drills that have received less attention. Nor is there any obvious reason that attention should be placed on these when similar exercises last month were largely ignored.

Nonetheless, even if this week is not unusual, that may be its own problem. This high tempo of training is cause for concern in itself. China, said Wang from ingeniSPACE, is exercising more than it is resting.

title: Nutrition experts call for big food ban at biennial congress
summary: Nutrition experts have called for a ban of “big food” from future SA Nutrition Congresses following an alleged conflict of interest at this year’s event. From 7-9 October the Nutrition Society of South Africa (NSSA) and the Association for
content:
Nutrition experts have called for a ban of “big food” from future SA Nutrition Congresses following an alleged conflict of interest at this year’s event.

From 7-9 October the Nutrition Society of South Africa (NSSA) and the Association for Dietetics in South Africa (Adsa) hosted their biennial Nutrition Congress, a platform for researchers, healthcare professionals, policymakers, practitioners and other stakeholders to share and discuss current evidence and developments in nutrition.

This year companies Danone Southern Africa (Danone SA), Unilever South Africa and PepsiCo were exhibitors at the event, which nutrition experts said was a conflict of interest.

According to Tamryn Frank, a nutrition expert and senior lecturer at the University of the Western Cape’s School of Public Health, it is a conflict of interest for an event that aims to improve nutrition in South Africa to have companies like Danone, Unilever and PepsiCo, which produce and sell ultra-processed foods, sponsor it and exhibit at it. Frank added that there was increasing evidence that ultra-processed foods were linked to poor health outcomes like obesity and non-communicable diseases.

PepsiCo’s exhibition stand at the 2026 Nutrition Congress. (Photo: Supplied / Catherine Pereira-Kotze)

If the ultra-processed food industry was allowed to sponsor and exhibit at the Nutrition Congress, to the layman it created the impression that the congress endorsed these companies as part of a solution to SA’s nutrition crisis, Frank said.

Nutrition expert and consultant researcher at the South African Medical Research Council, Catherine Pereira-Kotze, noted that since South Africa was characterised by undernutrition and micronutrient deficiencies, together with overweight and obesity, and high levels of poverty, inequality, unemployment and various other social problems, families should not be spending the little they had on ultra-processed foods. Rather, families should be prioritising fruit, vegetables and whole foods in accordance with [national food-based dietary guidelines](https://www.fao.org/nutrition/education/food-dietary-guidelines/regions/countries/south-africa/en/).

“The term ‘healthwashing’ comes to mind where by being aligned with this event it indicates that they are part of the solution. Because if you see the Nutrition Congress’ logo alongside the sponsors or the logos of these ultra-processed food companies I think it gives the impression that they are healthy options,” said Frank.

To protest against the alleged conflict of interest, Frank, Pereira-Kotze and other nutrition experts shared protest slides during their presentations and created a petition.

### Nutrition experts take a stand

Concerned about the alleged conflict of interest, Frank created a slide to use in her presentation condemning the ultra-processed food industry’s involvement in the congress.The slide stated:

“I DO NOT SUPPORT THE ULTRA-PROCESSED FOOD INDUSTRY EXHIBITING AT THE CONGRESS

THIS IS A CONFLICT OF INTEREST”

Frank saw it fit to make this the third slide of her presentation as the second slide was a mandatory funding disclosure slide, she said. Frank shared the slide with other concerned speakers who also incorporated it into their presentations.

Zandile Kubeka, the Department of Health Deputy Director of Dietetics in the Child and Youth Health Directorate, shared a similar slide inspired by Frank’s during her presentation. The slide stated:

“THE DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH DOES NOT SUPPORT THE ULTRA-PROCESSED FOOD INDUSTRY EXHIBITING AT THE CONGRESS

THIS IS A CONFLICT OF INTEREST”

Kubeka also noted the presence of ultra-processed food industry sponsors and exhibitors at the Nutrition Congress, and raised concerns regarding potential conflicts of interest in relation to their participation, according to Department of Health spokesperson Foster Mohale.

To further protest against the alleged conflict of interest, Frank had created a [petition](https://awethu.amandla.mobi/petitions/ban-big-food-from-the-nutrition-congress)with the help of Amandla.mobi, she said.

The petition first called on the Nutrition Society of SA and the Association for Dietetics in SA to announce that no companies connected with ultra-processed foods would be allowed to sponsor or exhibit at future congresses or events. Second, they must issue an apology for allowing the ultra-processed food industry to participate in the congress.

### Safeguarding integrity

The Nutrition Society of SA and the Association for Dietetics in SA shared a collective written response by NSSA representative Elize Symington and Adsa president Maria van der Merwe in response to questions sent by Daily Maverick.

According to the Nutrition Society of SA, Danone, Unilever and PepsiCo complied with NSSA and Adsa’s criteria to participate.

All applications for participation as sponsors or exhibitors at the congress were accompanied by the information entities wanted to share and products to be exhibited, and an illustration of the exhibition stand, all of which had to be approved prior to the congress, it said.

It added that the congress organising committee also reviewed exhibition applications against healthy eating guidelines, compliance with applicable regulations, and alignment with the values and principles of the congress as guided by international consensus.

All congress exhibitors were allocated a stand in one of the exhibition areas to display the brands and products at a fee, and exhibition and sponsorship income was paid into pooled congress funds, according to the organisers.

Danone's exhibition stand at the 2026 Nutrition Congress. (Photo: Supplied / Danone SA)

Although the Nutrition Society of SA and the Association for Dietetics in SA recognised that commercial sponsorship of nutrition-related scientific and professional activities may create actual, potential or perceived conflicts of interest, they did not agree that participation under the safeguards described compromised the independence or integrity of the congress, they said.

For this congress, exhibitors and sponsors were screened and had no role in determining the programme or in the selection of abstracts or speakers, according to the organisers. Private sector participation did not constitute or imply endorsement of any exhibitor’s products or practices, and all speakers declared their affiliations and funding during presentations, they added. The congress’ commitment to open debate on this topic was demonstrated by the inclusion of two sessions specifically addressing conflicts of interest in the programme.

Feedback received this year, including differing perspectives from across the nutrition community, would form part of the host organisations’ ongoing review. Any future policy decisions would be guided by the best available evidence and made through the governance structures of the Nutrition Society of SA and the Association for Dietetics in SA, they said when asked if companies connected to the ultra-processed food industry would be excluded from future congresses as demanded in the petition.

### Exhibitors respond

According to Dudu Mthuli, Nutrition and Health Lead at Unilever Southern Africa, there was no conflict of interest. Unilever was involved only in hosting an exhibition stand and in no other elements of the congress, she said.

Unilever’s stand communicated how their brands fitted into healthy eating. Unilever applied to exhibit at the event, because they were committed to partnering with like-minded stakeholders in educational and sponsorship activities that supported their view of making nutritious, balanced diets accessible, affordable, and enjoyable through science and expertise, Mthuli said.

She added that Unilever’s registered dietitians and food scientists also used the opportunity to keep up to date with science as presented at the sessions.

Unilever’s exhibition stand at the 2026 Nutrition Congress. (Photo: Supplied / Catherine Pereira-Kotze)

Danone saw its participation in the congress “not as a conflict of interest, but as a confluence of interest”, according to Head of Corporate and Regulatory Affairs at Danone SA, Leanne Kiezer.

Danone SA participated in the Nutrition Congress as a presenter in the scientific programme and as an exhibitor, she said. The FoodSAMSA Project published the report [Inside our Food Environments South Africa 2025](https://foodsamsa.samrc.ac.za/FOODSAMSA%20Report%20WP2.pdf) that assessed the commitments and practices of 29 food companies in South Africa for supporting healthier food environments and improving population nutrition. The independent report ranked Danone SA as the leading food company assessed, with a score of 83/100 for its commitments and practices for supporting food environments and improving population nutrition, according to Kiezer.

She added that the Association for Dietetics in South Africa had invited Danone SA to submit an abstract to the Nutrition Congress scientific committee, to share the study results and to provide further detail on the commitments and practices that contributed to Danone SA’s score. Danone SA submitted an abstract that was independently reviewed by the congress’s scientific committee and accepted for an oral presentation as part of the scientific programme.

Danone SA also participated as an exhibitor, with a stand focused on sharing evidence on the health and nutritional benefits of yoghurt. The educational content was not brand or product specific and focused on yoghurt and its benefits from a category perspective, Kiezer said.

Danone SA believed that describing a food company or its portfolio through the single lens of “ultra-processed food” oversimplified the broader picture of nutritional quality, according to Kiezer. The overall nutritional profile of individual foods, and their contribution to dietary patterns, were also important considerations, she said.

Based on Danone SA’s assessment of total volumes sold in 2025, 74% passed the nutrient profiling calculator defined in draft Regulation 3337, while 71% would not carry warning labels under the current draft Regulation 3337 criteria, Kiezer claimed. These benchmarks provided important context on the nutritional quality of their portfolio, she said.

Daily Maverick contacted PepsiCo for comment, but had not received a response by the time of publication.**DM**
