 delivered to your inbox

Sign up for The Manila Times newsletters

By signing up with an email address, I acknowledge that I have read and agree to the [Terms of Service](https://manilatimes.net/terms-of-service "Terms of Service") and [Privacy Policy](https://manilatimes.net/privacy-policy "Privacy Policy").

Experts also point to slash-and-burn land-clearing practices that have changed the naturally fire-resistant landscape of Sumatra and Borneo.

The haze has drifted into neighboring Singapore, Malaysia and East Timor, which said it would shut schools nationwide for three days from Thursday, and as far afield as the Philippines.

The closures in East Timor were necessary “as a preventive measure to protect the health of students, teachers and other members of the educational community, given current air quality conditions,” the government said.

*   ![Image 1: Eala eyes fresh start at Ningbo Open](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/14/1259220.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Eala eyes fresh start at Ningbo Open](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/15/sports/eala-eyes-fresh-start-at-ningbo-open/2445560)

It urged families to keep children indoors and to use “respiratory protection” if going outside.

Singapore rolled out subsidies for haze-related medical treatment from Monday, a measure last activated in 2015, when similar blazes in Indonesia cloaked Southeast Asia in toxic smoke for weeks.

The city-state has also begun distributing N95 masks to eligible residents when pollution reaches very unhealthy levels.

Singapore’s National Trades Union Congress said on Monday that public transport workers and delivery riders could receive free N95 masks, but Agence France-Presse (AFP) found that uptake was slow.

*   ![Image 2: Pangilinan seeks reversal of ruling on Duterte’s dropped charges](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/14/1258438.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Pangilinan seeks reversal of ruling on Duterte’s dropped charges](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/14/news/pangilinan-seeks-reversal-of-ruling-on-dutertes-dropped-charges/2445025)

“It’s a little bit uncomfortable to wear a mask, and some orders we have to walk around blocks, or park outside,” a delivery rider, who gave his name only as Daniel, told AFP.

“With the mask, I will have to breathe heavier,” the 27-year-old said.

[![Image 3: BURNING UP Soldiers and firefighters work on containing a wildfire in Banjarbaru, South Kalimantan province, Indonesia, on Oct. 13, 2026. AFP PHOTO](https://manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/14/1259331.jpg)](https://manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/14/1259331.jpg)
BURNING UP Soldiers and firefighters work on containing a wildfire in Banjarbaru, South Kalimantan province, Indonesia, on Oct. 13, 2026. AFP PHOTO

*   ![Image 4: 44% expect Sara Duterte’s conviction in impeachment trial — survey](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/14/1258812.jpeg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[44% expect Sara Duterte’s conviction in impeachment trial — survey](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/14/news/44-expect-sara-dutertes-conviction-in-impeachment-trial-survey/2445251)

Homes razed,

diplomatic calls

Ong Kwang Wei, 57, who has asthma, said he wore an N95 mask outdoors and carried his inhaler and medication with him at all times.

He was accompanying his 88-year-old mother — also masked — for a health checkup after a recent bout of the flu.

“Once the flu kicks in, my asthma is exacerbated ... I get breathless, I cough, I get phlegm, so I need to use my inhaler,” Ong said.

In Indonesia, tens of thousands of people have sought treatment for respiratory illness linked to haze from fires burning in Borneo, South Sumatra and Papua regions.

On Sumatra island, a fire razed nearly 300 homes, forcing hundreds of people to evacuate, an official said on Tuesday.

Residents first spotted the fire approaching their village in Bangka Belitung province on Saturday and tried to put it out themselves with portable water pumps.

But the fire continued to smolder underground in peatland, and when the wind shifted, the flames moved toward their homes.

The local disaster agency said nearly 1,000 people fled the village.

“My house is gone,” Leni, a 55-year-old villager now staying at a shelter with her family, told AFP.

“There’s nothing left. I could only save myself and take my kids with me ... I panicked and didn’t have the time to grab anything,” said Leni, who, like many Indonesians, has one name.

President Prabowo Subianto on Monday ordered the government to mobilize maximum efforts, with officials saying more than 60,000 personnel had been deployed to combat fires on the ground.

But efforts so far, including cloud seeding and water-bombing, have had limited success.

The haze has prompted Malaysia to request a meeting of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (Asean), and on Tuesday Malaysian parliamentarian Syed Saddiq Rahman urged a “diplomatic protest.”

“We must send a diplomatic protest note, not just on behalf of Malaysia, but the Asean. You need to treat them as an outcast in the region,” he said.

title: BARMM coalition gets majority with 46 MPs
summary: **DAVAO CITY**— Not just 41 as earlier expected, but 46 Members of Parliament signed the coalition documents, which, in the words of Bangsamoro Interim Chief Minister Abdulraof Macacua, would pave the way for an inclusive government that br
content:
**DAVAO CITY**— Not just 41 as earlier expected, but 46 Members of Parliament signed the coalition documents, which, in the words of Bangsamoro Interim Chief Minister Abdulraof Macacua, would pave the way for an inclusive government that bridges political divisions and serves all BARMM communities.

In a press briefing in this city, Macacua said the coalition would prioritize unity among the Bangsamoro people after the region’s first parliamentary elections, stressing that the incoming government must serve constituents regardless of their political affiliations or electoral choices.

“After the formal assumption of the Government of the Day, we will pursue a program for the unity of all Bangsamoro,” Macacua said.

*   [More complaints filed vs Magalang mayor](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/12/regions/more-complaints-filed-vs-magalang-mayor/2443357)

Macacua described the coalition as broad and inclusive, reflecting the diversity of the region and the need for political leaders to work together beyond the divisions created during the election campaign.

Macacua emphasized that the responsibility of the new government would extend beyond those who voted for its members, encompassing every community, province and sector across the Bangsamoro region.

According to Macacua, the coalition would reach out to other groups, heal divisions and build a government capable of responding to the needs of the entire Bangsamoro population.

The commitment to inclusive governance comes as the newly elected Parliament prepares to organize the region’s first fully elected parliamentary government, marking a significant stage in BARMM’s transition from an interim administration.

*   ![Image 1: Marcos’ impeachment plot backfires](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/13/1258203.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)

[![Image 2: No Image](https://manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/14/1260105.jpg)](https://manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/14/1260105.jpg)

The 80-member Bangsamoro Parliament emerged from the Sept. 14 elections, in which no single political party secured the 41 seats needed to command a majority. The coalition arrangement is therefore central to efforts to establish a working parliamentary majority. The 46 lawmakers who signed the coalition documents exceed the 41-member threshold required for a majority in the 80-seat Parliament, providing the coalition with a numerical basis to organize the incoming government.

The Bangsamoro Federalist Party (BFP), chaired by Macacua, emerged as the largest party in the elections, securing 31 seats when party and district seats were combined, according to election reporting. The United Bangsamoro Justice Party and the BARMM Grand Coalition also secured substantial representation in the new legislature.

Macacua thanked the 46 elected lawmakers for their trust and commitment, as well as the national government for respecting BARMM’s institutions and political processes.

He said the coalition was prepared to move forward once Parliament convenes, with its members united by the objective of serving the Bangsamoro people.

The coalition’s formation comes at a crucial point in the region’s political transition, as elected lawmakers prepare to assume their responsibilities and determine the leadership and direction of the incoming parliamentary government.

The 80 newly elected members are scheduled to assume office on Oct. 30, when Parliament is expected to organize the new government and elect a chief minister.

title: Impeachment as democracy’s necessary check
summary: THE latest Pulse Asia survey, conducted from Sept. 17 to 24, places Sara Duterte at 50 percent in presidential preference for 2028. For those troubled by the allegations against her, this is a sobering reminder that electoral popularity and
content:
THE latest Pulse Asia survey, conducted from Sept. 17 to 24, places Sara Duterte at 50 percent in presidential preference for 2028. For those troubled by the allegations against her, this is a sobering reminder that electoral popularity and fitness for public office can travel in opposite directions.

A survey measures preference. It cannot certify honesty, reconcile financial records or absolve constitutional violations. Yet Duterte’s defenders treat her continuing popularity as though millions of supporters could collectively erase questions that demand documentary answers. When loyalty becomes a substitute for accountability, democracy risks becoming an elaborate mechanism for rewarding impunity.

This is why impeachment matters. It provides a constitutional means of protecting the republic when electoral judgment fails. The Senate can prevent irrational political allegiance from returning a demonstrably unfit official to power, provided it establishes impeachable wrongdoing through a fair examination of evidence. Popularity must never become immunity.

*   [Marcos’ impeachment plot backfires](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/14/opinion/columns/marcos-impeachment-plot-backfires/2444878)

Political theory gives us reasons to question the comforting assumption that voters reliably make informed, rational choices. Anthony Downs’ concept of rational ignorance explains why people may invest little effort in learning about politics. Acquiring information takes time, while one individual’s vote has an exceedingly small chance of deciding an election.

What makes sense for an individual can produce disastrous collective consequences. A citizen may find it easier to repeat a slogan than understand a financial disclosure. Multiply that shortcut across millions and an election can reward the candidate with the strongest emotional appeal rather than the strongest record of honesty.

Sign up for The Manila Times newsletters

By signing up with an email address, I acknowledge that I have read and agree to the [Terms of Service](https://manilatimes.net/terms-of-service "Terms of Service") and [Privacy Policy](https://manilatimes.net/privacy-policy "Privacy Policy").

Bryan Caplan goes further in “The Myth of the Rational Voter.” His concept of rational irrationality explains how voters can indulge comforting political beliefs because the personal cost of doing so appears negligible. People gain emotional satisfaction from believing what they want, while the consequences of misguided choices are shared by society.

Caplan’s principal evidence concerns economic policy. Applying his framework to unconditional loyalty toward a political personality is therefore an interpretation, rather than a finding about Duterte’s supporters. Nevertheless, the mechanism is recognizable. Admitting that one’s political idol has failed can be emotionally expensive. Dismissing inconvenient evidence can feel reassuringly cheap.

The resulting harm extends beyond the loyalist. Citizens who never supported that politician must also live under the administration that electoral devotion helps produce. Irrational voting carries a public cost. The satisfaction of defending an idol is privately enjoyed; the damage from installing an unfit leader is collectively endured.

*   ![Image 1: Eala eyes fresh start at Ningbo Open](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/14/1259220.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Eala eyes fresh start at Ningbo Open](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/15/sports/eala-eyes-fresh-start-at-ningbo-open/2445560)

Geoffrey Brennan and Loren Lomasky’s theory of expressive voting adds another explanation. Voting can function as an expression of identity, belonging, resentment or solidarity. A ballot may resemble cheering for a team. Supporting the candidate communicates who the voter is and which community the voter considers home.

This helps explain why damaging information can fail to weaken political allegiance. A supporter who experiences criticism of Duterte as an attack on personal identity may defend her more fiercely. The question shifts from whether she has answered the evidence to whether one’s political camp will be humiliated by conceding anything.

Christopher Achen and Larry Bartels, in “Democracy for Realists,” likewise challenge the picture of citizens calmly comparing policies before choosing leaders. They emphasize social identities and partisan attachments. Political loyalties can shape how people perceive facts, enabling the same conduct to appear unforgivable in an opponent and excusable in an ally.

These theories cannot establish that every Duterte supporter is irrational. Nor does one survey reveal what each respondent knows or believes. They do explain why counting preferences cannot settle questions of competence and integrity. Persistent refusal to confront substantiated wrongdoing deserves criticism, regardless of how numerous or enthusiastic its defenders become.

*   ![Image 2: ‘Our soldiers are not troublemakers’](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/14/1260179.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[‘Our soldiers are not troublemakers’](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/15/news/our-soldiers-are-not-troublemakers/2445870)

The argument for impeachment becomes stronger when supporters openly declare that no revelation could change their minds. Such loyalty abandons democratic scrutiny. It turns public office into a personal entitlement and makes constitutional accountability indispensable to the republic.

Constitutional democracy anticipates that popular judgment may falter. It distributes authority among institutions and imposes obligations that public enthusiasm cannot cancel. Article XI declares public office a public trust and identifies grounds for impeachment, including culpable constitutional violations, graft and corruption, and betrayal of public trust.

Impeachment is political because it addresses the abuse of public power through constitutionally designated political institutions. Its political character binds it to the protection of the republic. Alexander Hamilton’s discussion in “Federalist No. 65” links impeachment to violations of public trust and injuries to society, while warning against decisions governed by factional strength.

That warning applies directly to senators who might confuse Duterte’s survey numbers with a reason to excuse proven misconduct. Their obligation is to examine the charges, hear the defense and decide whether the evidence establishes constitutional grounds for conviction. Electoral calculations cannot discharge that obligation.

*   ![Image 3: 44% expect Sara Duterte’s conviction in impeachment trial — survey](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/14/1258812.jpeg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[44% expect Sara Duterte’s conviction in impeachment trial — survey](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/14/news/44-expect-sara-dutertes-conviction-in-impeachment-trial-survey/2445251)

Questions about asset declarations, unexplained wealth or the misuse of public funds require answers on their merits. If the evidence establishes impeachable wrongdoing, senators must act despite the respondent’s popularity. If it fails, they must decline to convict. The integrity of this check depends on principled judgment.

The Constitution permits impeachment judgments extending to removal and disqualification from public office. That power has a protective purpose: An official found culpable need not remain available for another electoral rehabilitation. Voters retain the right to choose among qualified candidates. Public support cannot compel institutions to disregard constitutionally established disqualification.

Senators are also vulnerable to irrationality, ambition and partisan attachment. Their election does not confer monopoly on wisdom. Robinhood Padilla is exhibit No. 1. This makes their conduct under oath especially consequential. They must demonstrate that constitutional responsibility can prevail over personal loyalty, anticipated electoral rewards and fear of offending a powerful political following.

The Senate can save irrational voters from making a mockery of democracy by enforcing accountability against proven abuses of public trust. Refusing that duty because an accused official remains popular would surrender constitutional government to political fandom.

Democracy deserves citizens willing to reconsider their loyalties and institutions willing to uphold their obligations. When voters will not confront proven unfitness, impeachment becomes a necessary check. Senators must have the courage to use it.

The author is a professor at the University of the Philippines Los Baños and vice chairman of the board of the People’s Television Network Inc.

# 病患進診間整疊「AI診斷」砸上桌要求照著治療 醫傻眼：當我得來速？

中時新聞網

醫師徐國峰表示，日前有病患帶著整疊AI診斷，要求照上面進行診治，讓他傻眼到不行。（示意圖：shutterstock／達志）

字級設定：[小](javascript:;)[中](javascript:;)[大](javascript:;)[特](javascript:;)

人工智慧世代到來，許多人遇到疑難雜症時，第一時間都是求助AI，但也有人把AI的話當成聖旨，甚至要求專業人士照AI做。近日專精於椎間盤突出與坐骨神經痛的醫師徐國峰分享自己遇到的奇葩案例，有位病患上門時，把整疊AI診斷砸到桌上，要求按照上面進行治療，讓他傻眼「當我得來速嗎」。

徐國峰日前在[臉書粉專發文](https://www.facebook.com/msnhsu/posts/pfbid0UfGzg8jR2zwEynjw41LHuz2ZQbNGKBd4HG3dSmMhzXw4QhKcxy1Ur2VLWrKTQF4Al?locale=zh_TW)「資料印了整整十五頁，結果只准林北回答一個好字？」表示近來有位初診患者一坐下來，就把整疊比論文還厚的A4紙砸到桌上，除了MRI報告外，還有10幾頁的ChatGPT對話紀錄，上面甚至用螢光筆與紅筆標好重點，讓他一時以為是大學指考衝刺筆記。

患者開口說「AI說我腳麻是因為椎間盤突出、椎管狹窄，加上第二級滑脫害的，你照這個方向處理就好」，當他詢問是小腿哪邊、走幾步會麻？下樓梯會不會踩空時，患者竟露出不耐表情，「上面不都寫了嗎，就是神經壓迫啊」，徐國峰解釋，需要敲反射、測肌力，確認症狀跟片子有沒有對上，話音未落，患者就不客氣打斷詢問「AI都交叉比對完了，你照上面處置很難嗎」。

徐國峰形容，當下心裡真的是有1萬隻「草泥馬」狂奔而過，花貴鬆鬆的掛號費進來是來看病還是點得來速的？直言真的很賭爛，對連人長什麼樣都不知道的伺服器代碼虔誠得像在拜北港媽祖，卻百般質疑眼前的活人醫師。徐國峰強調，自己也天天用AI，但脊椎這檔事從來就不是報告有名詞就代表抓到病因，感嘆AI很會說，但隔著螢幕有辦法檢測到患者肌肉萎縮嗎？敲得出膝反射嗎？連患者坐在診間翹二郎腿都看不到。

文末徐國峰表示，患者可以帶十頁資料來考試，也可以帶一百個問題來抬槓，但走進診間，請留一點空間縫隙，讓檢查跟專業說話，「身上的病痛，真的不會因為你辯贏了就自己痊癒，相信醫生，相信專業好嗎」，並貼出一張告示「已經在GPT獲得診斷的患者，請勿再向我們尋求意見，請改向Google查詢，但Threads真的不建議」。

title: A Louder Global South, an Unchanged Global Order?
summary: Today I would like to pick up where we left off last season and lay out the argument that will feature throughout this whole season. My claim is that the Global South has, in recent years, won a great deal of “voice” in global governance, b
content:
Today I would like to pick up where we left off last season and lay out the argument that will feature throughout this whole season. My claim is that the Global South has, in recent years, won a great deal of “voice” in global governance, but far less “authority”.

[![Image 1](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!ZS-6!,w_1456,c_limit,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2F94bca7fc-5dab-43a3-8f06-487c1739815b_1080x1350.png)](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!ZS-6!,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2F94bca7fc-5dab-43a3-8f06-487c1739815b_1080x1350.png)

Let me begin by complaining about my own vocabulary. I realize that this may be a strange way to open a new season!

The phrase is **“the Global South”**, which I have been using rather constantly in recent years. I use it in my lectures, in my published work, and on this podcast. Indeed, it is certainly being used much more today than at any point since the historic Bandung Conference of 1955 (1). Many countries are comfortable using it even though there are some, especially I would argue in the Global North, who question whether the Global South is any better than similar terms we have used in the past, such as “low-income countries”, “developing countries”, etc. (2). But although I am increasingly using the phrase, I am doing so with a sense of unease. Because I am, like perhaps many of you, am well aware of the numerous contradictions it entails.

As you may be aware, the Global South is sometimes used to signify a bloc in the sense of a group of countries that are acting together. Often because they have a common set of grievances (and claims) against the Global North. Sometimes it refers to a group of countries negotiating at a particular forum. At other times, it symbolizes a moral claim; meaning that many of these countries were colonized and typically bear the least responsibility for the current global climate crisis. And sometimes the Global South is simply a huge market to tap into (3).

Then there is the issue of which countries can be categorized as being part of the Global South. China is especially interesting here as it is projected to enter the high-income category either later this year or sometime next year (4). But while in the Global North there are voices claiming that this disqualifies China from claiming that they are a part of this group, Beijing itself is steadfast in its belief that it is firmly anchored in the grouping (5).

I could go on about the agreements and disagreements on this matter. But does this mean that we should we abandon the term?

I don’t think we should abandon it. Well, for a start, there is nothing better at the moment.

The term is often criticized for being imprecise. But its imprecision points to a gap between changing social or political realities. And rather than dismissing the phrase as vague, I think it actually illustrates how and to what extent something powerful is perhaps emerging.

But it certainly does mean that we need to be cautious about what we are claiming when we say that the Global South is rising. It may not be too controversial to claim that power has shifted and continues to shift. The more important question to address is whether rule-making authority has shifted.

So, what has actually changed?

In recent months, it appears to me that the donor–recipient relationship has collapsed, and, guess what, the Global South did not choose it!

Consider the facts. In 2025, official development assistance (ODA) fell by 23 per cent in real terms, down to around 174 billion dollars. It was actually the largest single-year aid contraction ever recorded, and the second consecutive year of decline. Foreign aid is now back to 2015 levels, the year the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) were adopted (6).

The United States is responsible for about 75 per cent of this decline. Particularly, aid to sub-Saharan Africa has fallen by 26 per cent (7). Another major power responsible for aid cuts is the United Kingdom. But there are also many others in Europe that have signaled or already undertaken drastic cuts.

The UN’s finances have also been in trouble for many years, and to make things worse core funding for the UN system has fallen by 27 per cent (8).

I think we should pay attention to how the aid era is not ending because the Global South wanted this to end right now. Rather, it is ending because the Global North appears to be walking away without any form of negotiations.

But, there is some good news. There has been an expansion of the institutional presence of the Global South.

The African Union is now a full member of the G20, and BRICS has expanded from 5 to 11 members, who together account for around 28 per cent of global GDP (9).

Between 2022 and 2025, the G20 was chaired by Indonesia, India, Brazil, and South Africa. These four consecutive presidencies had a major influence on what that group talked about and parts of the global economic agenda (10).

Consider another fact.

According to [Afrobarometer](https://www.afrobarometer.org/), which does the excellent public opinion work across the African continent, 62 per cent of Africans rate China’s influence positively. The corresponding figure for the US is 52 per cent and 50 for the EU (11).

But the really interesting aspect of this is that people who like what China is doing on the continent also tend to like the US and Europe (12).

This type of strategy is often termed as “hedging”. But the evidence shows that playing the field and having multiple sources of support and collaboration is precisely what people want.

Let me now return to the distinction between voice and authority that I mentioned at the beginning of this episode.

**Voice**, as I understand it, means being present in a forum or a meeting and being heard. It is also about ensuring that an issue or a set of issues a country’s leadership prioritizes appears on the meeting agenda.

**Authority,**by contrast, is about contributing to making a rule that other countries must abide by. Authority is also about ensuring that the rule will be respected by a large majority even against the wishes of a powerful state or a superpower.

So, my argument is that, at least as of now, the Global South has managed to achieve substantial voice. Indeed, a louder voice. It has articulated its demands and achieved considerable success in coordinating its position (on not all, but on some issues). But in terms of authority, the record is rather mixed.

**Let me offer four cases to illustrate this argument.**

**The G20**

In November 2025, the US boycotted the Johannesburg G20 summit. But despite American objection, the summit leaders adopted a final declaration text that focused on climate change mitigation, debt relief and initiatives that emphasized diversity and gender equality (13).

In many ways, this was the Global South exercising its “agency” and asserting its collective authority. And this authority held for a while. Until South Africa was disinvited from the Miami G20 summit that is scheduled for December 2026 (14).

Now, what happened in September of this year is the really interesting story. During the BRICS summit in New Delhi, eleven countries, two of which are permanent members of the UN Security Council, defended the South African position in the final BRICS declaration. The text mentioned that South Africa is a founding and full member of the G20 and that membership of the group can only change when all members agree. And that arbitrary revision of membership is inadmissible (15).

The BRICS summit’s support for the South African G20 position is an example of how a group of countries can agree on a text over a superpower’s objection. They declared that South Africa’s exclusion is illegitimate. However, what a group like the BRICS is still unable to do is to compel the US to invite South Africa to the Miami summit.

This is indeed an example of the exercise of authority over the agenda, but not over the final outcome.

Let us consider another case: **The UN tax convention**,which I believe is a really strong case.

The idea of an UN-led tax convention began as an African Group initiative in the General Assembly. The goal is to move international tax rules out of the OECD (the rich-country club) into the UN, where every country, irrespective of size or financial muscle, has one vote (16).

The OECD has not been supportive of this new convention, and the United States withdrew in February 2025. But the negotiations have been ongoing with the fifth session concluding in August with full draft texts of the framework convention and two protocols on the table. In November of this year, the sixth session will meet in Nairobi, and the final text will be discussed at the General Assembly by the end of 2027 (17).

The global coalition for this new tax convention has also widened with endorsement for it in from the BRICS. So, what began with the African Group now is supported by eleven countries that represent more than a quarter of the world economy (18).

This appears to me to be one of the clearest examples of rule-making that has moved out of a small and rich club and into a universal body because the Global South has insisted on it.

**The selection of the next UN Secretary-General is also going to test the voice and authority of the Global South.**

Seven candidates are officially still in the race, and all of them are either from Latin America, the Caribbean or Africa (19).

Whether one of these is actually confirmed is still uncertain as there are rumors that a consensus candidate will appear in the final stages.

This is more than likely as, according to a recent report, the [“Trump administration opposes all options for new UN chief”](http://(https//www.politico.com/news/2026/10/09/trump-un-chief-candidates-01115653)) (20).

What would be great is if it was someone from the Global South AND a woman!

A final example of voice and authority concerns the **IMF agreement on a quota increase under its Sixteenth General Review**. These quotas determine who actually decides things at the Fund. But this quota increase is frequently reaffirmed in declaration after declaration. In reality, reaffirmation is not enforcement (21)!

So far, then, we can conclude that there is a pattern that is emerging. The Global South has achieved major gains whenever rules are made in institutions built on sovereign equality (that is one country, one vote). Examples include the tax convention, General Assembly resolutions, etc.

But when rules are made in institutions built on weighted votes or great-power privilege (such as the Security Council, the IMF), the Global South has not achieved real gains. And the IMF quota system is an illustrative example.

So, how should we approach the next phase of global development?

**Firstly,** I think it is a mistake to view the Global South as one bloc.

Countries that agree on tax may not agree on climate finance. Those that agree on climate finance may not agree on Security Council reform. I think what we are seeing are the emergence of “issue coalitions”.

If you closely examine the text of the latest BRICS summit in New Delhi this year, there are several clues about how there is both support and disagreement within this grouping. For example, although the declaration mentions Chinese and Russian support for the aspirations of Brazil and India to “play a greater role” at the UN, note that the declaration does not mention “permanent membership” (22).

This does not mean that the BRICS summit was a failure. Far from it. But I think one lesson is that the Global North should not expect to negotiate with a unified “Global South”. Indeed, the Global South does not have an address. It does not have a secretariat. Its members do not always agree on a common position. And most importan

title: Regional Trade, Economic Strategy Draw Asian And African States Closer To BRICS – Analysis
summary: ## **Key Takeaways:** * Under India’s chairmanship the New Delhi BRICS summit adopted a declaration promoting local-currency trade, payment-system interoperability and reforms at the UN, IMF and World Bank, while Modi stressed that the expa
content:
## **Key Takeaways:**

*   Under India’s chairmanship the New Delhi BRICS summit adopted a declaration promoting local-currency trade, payment-system interoperability and reforms at the UN, IMF and World Bank, while Modi stressed that the expanded group of eleven members (nearly half the world’s population and 40 percent of global GDP) is non-Western rather than anti-Western.
*   The New Development Bank, now with over $32 billion in approved projects, and the Contingent Reserve Arrangement form the core of an alternative financial architecture that African members such as South Africa, Egypt and Ethiopia are using to pursue development while retaining ties with Western partners.
*   Rising Chinese trade and defence links with Central Asia illustrate the region’s diversification, yet the article notes that BRICS’s collective economic weight still outstrips its ability to act as a unified political bloc.

Perhaps, BRICS (Brazil, Russia, India, China and South Africa), with the new members and partner states, summit in New Delhi, on September 11 to13, produced a new round of significant declarations, adapting its collective policy towards an increasingly emerging architecture, while distinctively building an ‘Asian model’ of economic alliance. Under the chairmanship of India, the summit centered on creating a genuine reputation that has accumulated for nearly two decades. The timing was, particularly, notable. The most important strategic message was coined: “Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation, and Sustainability.”

Addressing the BRICS summit of leading developing nations in New Delhi, Indian Prime Minister, Narendra Modi, warned rising geopolitical tensions, could increasingly affect people worldwide, and called for deepening cooperation and strengthening support across the Global South. “The number of conflicts and tensions in the world is continuously increasing, and this is having an increasingly negative and far-reaching impact on the lives of ordinary people,” Modi said, alongside with leaders including Chinese President Xi Jinping, Russian President Vladimir Putin and South African President Cyril Ramaphosa. That was one of the main messages sent across the world. Founded in 2006 by Brazil, Russia, India and China, BRICS has expanded to 11 members representing about half the world’s population and a significant share of global economic output. It has sought greater representation for developing countries in global institutions and promoted alternative actions to Western-dominated financial systems.

## **Geopolitics: Is BRICS Challenging the West?**

BRICS leaders adopted the New Delhi Declaration, expressing indispensable concern relating to forging consensus over many strategic questions, backed greater use of local currencies in trade and stronger cross-border payment systems, while calling for cooperation on food security, energy, digital infrastructure, artificial intelligence and climate action. The declaration was a significant breakthrough, which holds competing positions on key regional and geopolitical issues–posed a complex diplomatic challenge amid ongoing conflicts and heightened geopolitical tensions. It emphasizes collective support for a multipolar world order and operational and structural reforms, at the United Nations, including its Security Council, as well as global financial institutions such as the World Bank (WB) and the International Monetary Fund (IMF).

The declaration demonstrated BRICS can move together and act on multilateral economic cooperation, and its sustainability in Global South. That makes the question whether India has used its presidency to drum home for BRICS grouping to become more capable of taking economic action, with reports indicating that India entered a particular moment with more than just diplomatic presence. For instance, during the financial year 2024-25, its total exports amounted, approximately, $825 billion, with services accounting for an estimated $387 billion. Few developing countries can match New Delhi’s economic leverage, which stems from its large domestic market, expansion of digital economy, and sustainable growth. Despite national preferences and differences between BRICS members, it is worthy to note that India is a major provider of digital public infrastructure, and its demography plays an increasingly important role in global consumption, production, and services. It therefore exemplifies BRICS members have to build economic prosperity by opening doors. This new phase must strategically focus on a broader economic leverage. And appropriately, India’s geography provides an additional layer of economic leverage, which serves as a classical example for other Asian countries.

## **Сorporate Economic Weight, Limited Collective Power**

While BRICS’s economic weight is enormous–its ability to wield it collectively is not, some analysts argued. However, experts’ arguments closely connected to BRICS operational successes and achievements should not only be measured by whether it can pose an alternative to multinational institutions, but also whether it could make any noticeable difference, in terms of using its natural resources to increase regional trade, raise economic production and improve distribution across the Global South. Several experts position portrays BRICS has offered its member countries alternative pathways for channeling trade and investment that serve the collective interests of member countries–largely national development and poverty alleviation.

Meanwhile, scholars have reminded that BRICS emerged after the 2008 financial collapse and the failures of the World Trade Organization’s (WTO) Doha Round–trade negotiations aimed at reforming the international trading system in favour of Global South countries. Why would the BRICS want to take on the global governance responsibilities of the G7 members? This has been the basic question among scholars until today. It is, however, believed that reforms and greater autonomy would be a greater concern for BRICS rather than overthrowing the unravelling liberal international order.

## **BRICS+ Financial Architecture**

The group is noticeably dominated by China, which has the largest share of the group’s GDP, accounting to about 70% of the organization total. The financial architecture of BRICS is made of the New Development Bank (NDB) and the Contingent Reserve Arrangement (CRA). These components were signed into a treaty in 2014 and became active in 2015. The New Development Bank (NDB), formally referred to as the BRICS Development Bank, is a multilateral development bank operated by the five BRICS states. It has non-members as contributors to the NDB.

The bank’s primary focus of lending is infrastructure projects with authorized lending of up to $34 billion annually. South Africa hosts the African headquarters of the bank. The bank has a starting capital of $50 billion, with wealth increased to $100 billion over time. Records show Brazil, Russia, India, China, and South Africa initially contributed $10 billion each to bring the total to $50 billion. As of 2020, it had 53 projects underway worth around $15 billion. By 2025, the bank had approved more than $32 billion for 96 projects.

In 2021, Bangladesh, Egypt, the United Arab Emirates and Uruguay joined the NDB. With India’s presidency in 2026, which was estimated to be a comprehensive and promising for BRICS, as India has outlined its framework of priorities, as it did during its G20 presidency several years ago. In close-coordination with members and partner-states within the BRICS, India has ensured the balance of multifaceted interests, and established mutual-trust in the multipolar world system. The goal of transforming into a full-fledged international organization must go beyond addressing current geopolitical challenges, the necessity to develop effective ways of engaging in global development to reflect multipolarity. Today, collectively, BRICS comprises more than a quarter of the global economy and nearly half the world’s population.

## **BRICS Advocates for Reforms at Financial Institutions**

Finance Ministers and Central Bank Governors of BRICS countries have called for reform of global developmental financial institutions ‌such as the International Monetary Fund and World Bank, seeking a ‌stronger voice for emerging market economies. “We will continue to strengthen coordination among BRICS members to make international financial ‌institutions more representative, transparent and accountable. With the growing share of emerging market and developing economies in ​global output and growth, reform of global economic governance remains a consistent BRICS priority,” Finance Chiefs of BRICS countries underlined in an official joint statement.

“We continue to have serious concerns with the unilateral imposition of trade and finance-related actions, including the raising of tariffs and non-tariff measures, which distort trade and are inconsistent with World Trade Organisation rules,” the statement said. “We ‌encourage the BRICS Payment Task Force to ​continue discussions, building ​on the ongoing work, to facilitate practical solutions for cross-border payments among BRICS countries, which are fast, low-cost, more accessible, efficient, transparent, and ​safe,” the statement said. While acknowledging the work done ​by the BRICS payment task force, the ​finance chiefs pushed for progress ​in ensuring greater interoperability of payment systems across member nations. It further noted India will ‌push for progress on linking digital currencies across BRICS countries.

## **BRICS-Africa Transiting from Diplomacy to Strategic Economy**

South Africa (2010), Ethiopia and Egypt (2024), as fully-fledged BRICS members, are seemingly changing policy which has always been strategic ambiguity, to a kind of assertive flexibility. South Africa, Ethiopia and Egypt are positioning also as leading African voices for the Global South while, at the same time, maintaining relationships with competing Western powers. In principles, Africa generally collaborates with the United States and Asian-Pacific partners while striking, to a certain degree, multifaceted ties with Russia, and operates within framework of BRICS domain.

South African Cyril Ramaphosa, Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed, and President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi of Arab Republic of Egypt held separate conversations on the current status and future prospects for their relations, and further discussed ways of strengthening BRICS strategic partnership in politics and security, economics and finance, and cultural and humanitarian ties, while exchanging divergent views on current international and regional issues that are of common significance to the global development. South Africa, Ethiopia and Egypt, however, plan to take new initiatives to improve and strengthen relations within BRICS.

The Asian economic architect is, strongly, being advocated for as BRICS new direction, and subsequently as non-Western dominated attention, according to the common statement by leaders of South Africa, Ethiopia and Egypt, while noting the significance of India’s role in hosting the 18th summit, and congratulated India for directing BRICS in shaping South-South alliance and the new economic order. As BRICS-African members, South Africa, Egypt and Ethiopia indicated high aspirations to build an alternative order to the West, wielding power to challenge Western hegemony. Now experiencing ‘reawakening’ from colonial yoke, Africa began throttling alternative pathways, and consistently signaling trade and investment that would serve the interests of the African member countries–largely focused on continental economic development, economic improvement and poverty alleviation.

**薄熙來前搭檔受查：重慶政壇「不倒翁」黃奇帆是誰？**

Published 2026年10月14日

中共中紀委在10月13日宣佈，74歲的黃奇帆涉嫌「嚴重違紀違法」，正接受紀律審查和監察調查。

黃奇帆的政途從上海走至重慶市，獲朱鎔基提攜參展浦東新區，大力提振重慶經濟，經濟政績亮眼。黃奇帆在薄熙來主政重慶期間任職市長，成為其緊密搭檔，然而歷經王立軍事件、薄熙來及孫政才兩任市委書記相繼落馬﹐惟他未受波及，被外界稱為重慶政壇「不倒翁」。

黃奇帆已退休九年，淡出政壇仍以學者身份高調評論經濟政策。他突然受查的消息，正值中共五中全會前夕，引發外界關注。

content:
_Katsuji Nakazawa 是日经新闻驻东京的高级职员和社论作家。他在中国担任记者七年，后来担任中国分社社长，并于 2014 年获得沃恩-上田国际记者奖。_

中国人民解放军的神经中枢——对中国军事部署做出最终决定的地方——仍然是空心的。

在军队内部进行了一系列大清洗后，监督解放军的最高军事机关中央军委已经没有可以指挥地面部队的军装军官了。

这种情况象征着中国国家主席习近平及其政府在准备本月晚些时候举行的一次重要党内会议时所面临的矛盾。

习近平还是中国共产党总书记、中央军委主席。中共二十届中央委员会第五次全体会议将于10月26日至29日在北京召开，会议的主题是“全面从严治党”。

2022年10月中国共产党第20次全国代表大会选举产生第20届中央委员会后，与解放军有关的矛盾逐渐暴露出来。自今年年初达到顶峰以来，这种情况没有改变。

9月21日，就在习近平访问美国并在白宫与唐纳德·特朗普总统举行会谈之前不久，宣布了一项重大决定。
公告称，中共中央政治局在当天的会议上决定，以“严重违纪违法”为由，给予张又侠、刘振立开除党籍和军籍处分。

张是中国人民解放军最高军官和中央军委副主席，刘是中央军委委员和中央军委联合参谋部参谋长。自共产党 2022 年全国代表大会以来，他们一直在习近平领导下监督解放军的行动，并自 1 月以来一直受到调查

罢免张和刘的决定预计将在即将举行的五中全会上正式批准。

最近的清洗使得中央军委只剩下两名委员，即习主席和去年升任的副主席张生民。 2022年共产党最后一次全国代表大会结束后，中央军委由七名委员组成。除张又侠和刘振里外，其他三名委员已被罢免。

张胜民是中央军委目前仅存的唯一一名军装军官，他的大部分职业生涯都在解放军的纪律检查和政治工作中度过。他不是军事行动专家。

中央军委现在没有人能够从专业角度为习近平的军事部署和其他行动决策提供建议。

那么，中央军委为何名存实亡呢？
究其原因，与解放军是共产党的军队，而不是担负保卫国家任务的国家军队有密切关系；解放军的首要任务是保护政党。

自2012年成为中国最高领导人以来，习近平多次强调“军队听党指挥”的口号。

解放军是共产党的军队，受党领导。事实上，解放军内部存在党委，这对于国家军队来说是不可想象的。

在中国，国家是党治国，而不是政府治国。

重要的是“坚持全面从严治党”的问题，这是这次全会的重要议题。

当习近平倡导“全面从严治党”

_Katsuji Nakazawa is a Tokyo-based senior staff and editorial writer at Nikkei. He spent seven years in China as a correspondent and later as China bureau chief and was the 2014 recipient of the Vaughn-Ueda International Journalist prize._

The nerve center of the People's Liberation Army -- where final decisions on Chinese military deployments are made -- remains hollowed out.

After a sweeping series of purges within the military, the Central Military Commission, the top military organ that supervises the PLA, has no uniformed officer who can command troops on the ground.

The situation symbolizes the contradictions that face Chinese President Xi Jinping and his administration as they prepare for a key party meeting later this month.

Xi is also general secretary of the Chinese Communist Party and chairman of the CMC. The Communist Party's 20th Central Committee will hold its fifth plenary session in Beijing on Oct. 26-29 under the theme of "full and rigorous Party self-governance."

The PLA-related contradictions have gradually come to light after the Communist Party's 20th national congress in October 2022, which elected the 20th Central Committee. The situation has not changed since peaking early this year.

On Sept. 21, shortly before Xi visited the U.S. for talks with President Donald Trump at the White House, a momentous decision was announced.

The Communist Party's elite Politburo decided at that day's meeting to expel Zhang Youxia and Liu Zhenli from the party and military for "serious discipline and law violations," according to the announcement.

Zhang was the PLA's top uniformed officer and CMC vice chairman, while Liu was a CMC member and chief of staff of the CMC's Joint Staff Department. They had overseen the PLA's operations under Xi since the Communist Party's 2022 national congress and had been under investigation since January

The decision to oust Zhang and Liu is expected to be formally approved at the upcoming fifth plenum.

The latest purges have left the CMC with only two members, Chairman Xi and Vice Chairman Zhang Shengmin, who was promoted to the post last year. The CMC consisted of seven members immediately after the Communist Party's last national congress, in 2022. Besides Zhang Youxia and Liu Zhenli, three others have since been ousted.

Zhang Shengmin, now the only remaining uniformed officer in the CMC, has spent much of his career in discipline inspection and political work within the PLA; he is not a military operations expert.

The CMC now has no one who can advise supreme leader Xi from a professional standpoint when he makes decisions on military deployments and other moves.

So how has the CMC come to exist in name only?

The reason is closely related to the PLA being the Communist Party's military, not a national army tasked with defending the state; the PLA's primary mission is to protect the political party.

Since becoming China's top leader in 2012, Xi has repeatedly stressed the slogan of "a military that follows the command of the Communist Party."

As the PLA is the military wing of the Communist Party, it is governed by the party. In fact, a party committee exists within the PLA, something unthinkable for a national army.

In China, the country is party-run, not government-run.

What is important here is the issue of "persistently advancing full and rigorous Party self-governance," which is high on the agenda at the upcoming plenum.

When Xi advocates "full and rigorous Party self-governance," he also has the PLA, the party's military, in his sights.

While China has seen an unusual concentration of power in Xi's hands, a different logic also operates within the vast Communist Party.

The logic is that, no matter what, one-party rule must be maintained; the system should remain unshaken even when Xi is no longer in power.

The PLA shares this commitment to preserving one-party rule. In this regard, the PLA does not merely protect the top CMC official at the time but the party as a whole.

Since the Communist Party's 20th national congress in 2022, numerous senior military officials have been purged, falling to the Xi administration's signature anti-corruption campaign.

The purges reveal a major contradiction between Xi's policies and the mindset mainstream uniformed officers have maintained for many years.

The military purges, carried out under the banner of fighting corruption, are also testing the political loyalty of generals and other senior military officers: Are they loyal not only to the Communist Party but also to Xi himself?

In Beijing in March, Xi delivered a speech at a plenary meeting of delegates from the PLA and the People's Armed Police Force. It came during the annual session of the National People's Congress, China's parliament.

The keyword in that speech was _er xin_, a term meaning disloyalty but which literally translates as "two hearts." By using the term, Xi implied disloyal generals and other military officers remained in the PLA.

"There must be no place in the military for those who are disloyal to the Party," Xi warned, "and there must be no hiding place for corrupt elements."

Xi's remarks meant that those disloyal to the party -- to Xi himself, really -- are "corrupt elements" and subject to his fierce anti-corruption campaign.

This issue also relates to the interpretation of the CMC's "chairman responsibility system," designed to concentrate final authority on military actions in Xi's hands.

Numerous senior military officials, including those close to Xi, have been ensnared in the supreme leader's anti-corruption campaign and punished. The purges have also dealt Xi a political blow.

In August, China announced that senior military officer Zhong Shaojun had been stripped of his status as a deputy to the NPC. Zhong had long served as director of the CMC's General Office, managing practical work at the commission under Xi.

Xi had sent Zhong into the PLA's nerve center to gather information about the situation there, then had no choice but to discard his prized pawn.

The massive military purges are not merely part of Xi's corruption crackdown; they are key to his efforts to control the PLA. Their outcome could affect the atmosphere at the Communist Party's 21st national congress in 2027.

Xi is poised to bid for a fourth five-year term as party chief at the party event next autumn, and taking full control of the powerful military is crucial to this.

On Sept. 21, the Politburo decided to revise and submit to the fifth plenum a draft decision on strengthening the party's internal governance, according to state-run Xinhua News Agency.

The question now is how much longer the CMC will remain hollowed out. Will the fifth plenum make any personnel changes to resolve the contradiction regarding the military structure, including the CMC?

The purges have left few PLA officers who hold the highest rank of _shangjiang_, general or admiral, whom Xi trusts.

To return the CMC to its 2022 seven-member structure, five new appointments are needed. Defense minister Dong Jun is supposed to be a candidate. His disgraced predecessor, Li Shangfu, was also a CMC member.

Dong, an admiral, assumed the defense portfolio at the end of 2023 and is in charge of China's military diplomacy. He was not promoted to the CMC at the fourth plenum of the Communist Party's 20th Central Committee last October.

If the current military structure is largely functioning, with Xi wielding firm command authority and, in effect, issuing orders directly to the PLA's lower echelons, he has the option to leave the CMC as is until the party's national congress next year. Whether Xi chooses to rebuild the CMC or leave it hollowed out could reveal how thoroughly he has consolidated his personal control.

_You can read it in_ _[Arabic here](https://alhurra.com/46433), and check out MBN’s flagship_[_Arabic-language Alhurra news platform_](https://alhurra.com/)_(English version_[_here_](https://alhurra.com/en/)_)._

_This week’s edition of the briefing is a joint effort by our new Iran reporter Tara Rad, who is writing under a pseudonym, and me._

_Here’s what you need to know: Iran’s security chief has warned that U.S.-linked technology sites across the region would be destroyed if war resumes. More than 30 countries, led by the U.S. and U.K., condemned Iran’s covert plots abroad. At home, the execution of musician and mountaineer Ali Sina Mostafavi and the arrest of human-rights lawyer Amirsalar Davoudi show no easing of the post-protest crackdown. Police in southeast Iran face a run of deadly attacks, and economic strain is showing. Some doctors now earn more driving passengers than treating patients, and the government is widening food aid to about 40 million people._

_Find out more below, and share your thoughts, analysis and predictions with me at [ailves@mbn-news.com](mailto:ailves@mbn-news.com). If you were forwarded the MBN Iran Briefing, please_[_subscribe_](https://alhurra.com/en/newsletter)_._

**QUOTE OF THE WEEK**

> The pulse of the American economy in this region runs through our part of the world … If war breaks out, many of these cables, data centers, artificial intelligence facilities, and numerous other sites will be destroyed.

_—_ _Supreme National Security Council secretary_[_Mohsen Rezaei_](https://www.presstv.co.uk/Detail/2026/10/11/778085/Exclusive--Rezaei-says-%E2%80%98Powers-greater-than-US-tried-to-conquer-Iran,-but-ended-up-in-dustbin-of-history%E2%80%99)

**TOP OF THE NEWS**

**Iran’s Security Chief Puts $2 Trillion of U.S.-Linked Tech Assets on its Target List**

Supreme National Security Council secretary Mohsen Rezaei [said](https://www.presstv.co.uk/Detail/2026/10/11/778085/Exclusive--Rezaei-says-%E2%80%98Powers-greater-than-US-tried-to-conquer-Iran,-but-ended-up-in-dustbin-of-history%E2%80%99) in a Press TV interview that if war resumes, Iran is ready to destroy what he said was more than $2 trillion in U.S.-linked technology assets in the region.

“Many of these cables, data centers, artificial intelligence facilities, and numerous other sites will be destroyed,” he said.

He also said that more than “30 million Iranians have registered in [the] ‘Janfada’ (Sacrifice for Iran) Campaign to take up arms in the event of U.S. aggression.” Iran has a population of over 90 million.

Speaking of Iranian threats on foreign targets, over 30 countries, including the U.S. and the U.K., signed a “[Joint Statement on Iran](https://www.gov.uk/government/news/joint-statement-on-iran-12-october)” that “condemn[s] in the strongest terms Iran’s use of violent attacks, including the acts of lethal plotting, arson, sabotage, cyber-attacks, and other hybrid activities against us and our partners.” The statement notes “the IRGC’s continued willingness to project hostile activity beyond its borders through covert networks and proxy actors” and mentions “the recent campaign of attacks across Europe targeting Jewish communities, Iranian journalists, and U.S. interests, claimed by Harakat Ashab al-Yamin al-Islamiya (HAYI).”

This came after an alleged terrorist plot against an RAF base at the end of September, [previously covered](https://alhurra.com/en/42956) in this newsletter. British Prime Minister Andy Burnham has [said](https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cjwyz59k5y75o): “There are strong indications that Iran played a part.”

The U.K. also [sanctioned](https://www.gov.uk/government/news/foreign-secretary-statement-on-iran-12-october) two Iranian nationals: the IRGC’s head of counterespionage operations and a man it calls the “facilitator” of a criminal network involved in several plots against Iranian dissidents.

Iran’s Foreign Ministry [rejected](https://fararu.com/fa/news/1009341/%D8%A8%DB%8C%D8%A7%D9%86%DB%8C%D9%87-%D9%88%D8%B2%D8%A7%D8%B1%D8%AA-%D8%AE%D8%A7%D8%B1%D8%AC%D9%87-%D8%AF%D8%B1-%D9%88%D8%A7%DA%A9%D9%86%D8%B4-%D8%A8%D9%87-%D8%A7%D8%AF%D8%B9%D8%A7%D9%87%D8%A7%DB%8C-%D8%A7%D9%86%DA%AF%D9%84%DB%8C%D8%B3-%D8%B9%D9%84%DB%8C%D9%87-%D8%A7%DB%8C%D8%B1%D8%A7%D9%86-%D8%A7%DB%8C%D9%86-%D8%B9%D9%85%D9%84%DB%8C%D8%A7%D8%AA-%D9%BE%D8%B1%DA%86%D9%85-%D8%AF%D8%B1%D9%88%D8%BA%DB%8C%D9%86-%D8%A7%D8%B3%D8%AA) the allegations as an “ugly conspiracy to advance the anti-Iran campaign and evade accountability for Britain’s participation in the American-Zionist military aggression against the Iranian nation.”

_Executed Wednesday: Ali Sina Mostafavi, Photo:_[_Iran Human Rights_](https://iranhr.net/fa/articles/9114/)_._

**More Executions and Arrests**

On Wednesday, Iran [executed](https://www.radiofarda.com/a/iran-judiciary-alisina-mostafavi-protester-executed/33876276.html) Ali Sina Mostafavi, a 38-year-old musician and mountaineer who had climbed Mt. Everest. He’d been detained after the protests in January of this year. The [judiciary’s website](https://www.mizanonline.ir/fa/news/4923653/%D8%AA%D8%B1%D9%88%D8%B1%DB%8C%D8%B3%D8%AA-%D9%85%D8%B3%D9%84%D8%AD-%D8%AF%D8%B1-%DA%A9%D8%B1%D9%85%D8%A7%D9%86-%D8%A8%D9%87-%D8%AF%D8%A7%D8%B1-%D9%85%D8%AC%D8%A7%D8%B2%D8%A7%D8%AA-%D8%A2%D9%88%DB%8C%D8%AE%D8%AA%D9%87-%D8%B4%D8%AF-%D8%B9%D9%85%D9%84%DB%8C%D8%A7%D8%AA-%D9%87%D8%A7%DB%8C-%D9%85%D8%B3%D9%84%D8%AD%D8%A7%D9%86%D9%87-%D8%B9%D9%84%DB%8C-%D8%B3%DB%8C%D9%86%D8%A7-%D9%85%D8%B5%D8%B7%D9%81%D9%88%DB%8C-%D8%B9%D9%84%DB%8C%D9%87-%D8%B4%D9%87%D8%B1%D9%88%D9%86%D8%AF%D8%A7%D9%86-%D8%A7%DB%8C%D8%B1%D8%A7%D9%86%DB%8C-%D8%AF%D8%B1-%D8%AD%D9%85%D8%A7%DB%8C%D8%AA-%D8%A7%D8%B2-%D8%B1%D8%B6%D8%A7-%D9%BE%D9%87%D9%84%D9%88%DB%8C-%D9%88-%D8%B1%DA%98%DB%8C%D9%85-%D8%B5%D9%87%DB%8C%D9%88%D9%86%DB%8C%D8%B3%D8%AA%DB%8C-%D8%AF%D8%B1-%D8%AC%D8%B1%DB%8C%D8%A7%D9%86-%D8%AC%D9%86%DA%AF-%D8%B1%D9%85%D8%B6%D8%A7%D9%86) called him “one of the armed elements of the American-Zionist enemy affiliated with the hated monarchist movement” and accused him of “communication with hostile media affiliated with the Zionist regime.”

The office of Reza Pahlavi, the exiled former crown prince of Iran, [posted](https://x.com/PahlaviComms/status/2110350868943880201) on X about his execution, describing Mostafavi as “a man full of life, with achievements, ambitions, and a future.”

In a separate development, a lawyer who went to court on Sunday to represent a client was himself [arrested](https://www.hra-news.org/2026/hranews/a-6dd984b1/).

Amirsalar Davoudi, a prominent Iranian human rights lawyer, was detained at the Revolutionary Court in Isfahan while representing Mahshad Kashani, who was imprisoned after the January protests. According to the head of the Isfahan judiciary, Davoudi was [charged](https://www.irna.ir/news/86291394/%D8%B9%D9%84%D8%AA-%D8%A8%D8%A7%D8%B2%D8%AF%D8%A7%D8%B4%D8%AA-%D8%A7%D9%85%DB%8C%D8%B1%D8%B3%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%A7%D8%B1-%D8%AF%D8%A7%D9%88%D8%AF%DB%8C-%D9%88%DA%A9%DB%8C%D9%84-%D8%AF%D8%A7%D8%AF%DA%AF%D8%B3%D8%AA%D8%B1%DB%8C-%D8%AF%D8%B1-%D8%A7%D8%B5%D9%81%D9%87%D8%A7%D9%86-%D8%A7%D9%86%D8%AA%D8%B4%D8%A7%D8%B1) with publishing false information online, incitement to violence intended to undermine national security, and propaganda against the system. The charges relate partly to [material](https://iranwire.com/en/news/158829-defense-lawyer-arrested-in-iran-after-publishing-wedding-audio-of-executed-prisoner/) he posted on Instagram.

One of those posts concerned his defendant Kashani and another detainee from the January protests named Alireza Sepahi. Davoudi had published an audio recording that he said documented the marriage of the two political prisoners shortly before Sepahi’s execution. Judicial authorities now dispute that account and describe the claim about the marriage ceremony as false. The [judiciary’s website](https://www.mizanonline.ir/fa/news/4923415/%D8%B9%D9%84%D8%AA-%D8%A8%D8%A7%D8%B2%D8%AF%D8%A7%D8%B4%D8%AA-%D8%A7%D9%85%DB%8C%D8%B1%D8%B3%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%A7%D8%B1-%D8%AF%D8%A7%D9%88%D8%AF%DB%8C-%D9%88%DA%A9%DB%8C%D9%84-%D8%AF%D8%A7%D8%AF%DA%AF%D8%B3%D8%AA%D8%B1%DB%8C-%D8%AF%D8%B1-%D8%A7%D8%B3%D8%AA%D8%A7%D9%86-%D8%A7%D8%B5%D9%81%D9%87%D8%A7%D9%86-%DA%86%D9%87-%D8%A8%D9%88%D8%AF) said that publishing the audio file “led to propaganda abuse by hostile media outlets.”

Sepahi was sentenced to death and later [executed](https://www.amnesty.org.uk/latest/iran-five-protesters-executed-in-one-week-after-torture-tainted-trials/) on Oct. 5.

Davoudi himself is no stranger to prison. He was arrested in 2018 after representing political prisoners and other defendants in sensitive cases and was originally sentenced to 30 years in prison and 111 lashes. His case has since gone through repeated reviews, retrials and appeals.

His latest arrest is not an isolated case.

On Oct. 8, the Human Rights Activists News Agency [reported](https://www.hra-news.org/2026/hranews/a-6eeb37ba/) that Bahareh Aghaei, another lawyer, had been sentenced to 20 years in prison by a Tehran revolutionary court. She was arrested following the January protests and remains in Qarchak Prison. Other human rights groups have said her case is linked to her support for the protests and families of people killed during them.

**Unrest on Iran’s Eastern Border**

A string of shootings, roadside bombs and security operations has put renewed focus on Sistan and Baluchestan, Iran’s southeastern province bordering Pakistan and Afghanistan.

On Oct. 5, gunmen attacked a police patrol on the road between Bampur and Iranshahr, [killing two officers](https://www.tasnimnews.ir/fa/news/1405/07/13/3714902) and wounding another, according to Iranian media. Three days later, another police officer was killed when armed men attacked a patrol near Nosratabad. The following day a police vehicle struck a roadside bomb near Zahedan, killing Nosrat Eftekhari, a deputy provincial police commander responsible for social and cultural affairs.

[Jaish al-Adl](https://www.tasnimnews.ir/fa/news/1405/07/13/3715187/%D8%AA%D8%B1%D9%88%D8%B1%DB%8C%D8%B3%D9%85-%D8%A8%D8%A7-%D9%86%D9%82%D8%A7%D8%A8-%D8%AF%D9%81%D8%A7%D8%B9-%D8%A7%D8%B2-%D9%85%D8%B1%D8%AF%D9%85-%D8%AC%DB%8C%D8%B4-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%B8%D9%84%D9%85-%DA%86%DA%AF%D9%88%D9%86%D9%87-%D8%AE%D8%B4%D9%88%D9%86%D8%AA-%D8%B1%D8%A7-%D8%B1%D9%88%D8%A7%DB%8C%D8%AA-%D9%85%DB%8C-%DA%A9%D9%86%D8%AF), a Sunni Baluch militant group active in southeastern Iran, claimed responsibility for the first attack, according to Iranian media. Iranian authorities routinely describe it as a terrorist group. But the Iranian reporting does not establish that the same group carried out all three attacks.

The state’s response has been swift. The day after the first attack, the Intelligence Ministry’s provincial office said security forces had [dismantled](https://www.mehrnews.com/news/6952673/%D9%88%D8%B2%D8%A7%D8%B1%D8%AA-%D8%A7%D8%B7%D9%84%D8%A7%D8%B9%D8%A7%D8%AA-%D8%B3%D9%87-%DA%A9%D8%A7%D9%86%D9%88%D9%86-%D8%B9%D9%85%D9%84%DB%8C%D8%A7%D8%AA%DB%8C-%D9%88%D8%A7%D8%A8%D8%B3%D8%AA%D9%87-%D8%A8%D9%87-%DA%AF%D8%B1%D9%88%D9%87%DA%A9-%D9%87%D8%A7%DB%8C-%D8%AA%D8%B1%D9%88%D8%B1%DB%8C%D8%B3%D8%AA-%D9%85%D9%86%D9%87%D8%AF%D9%85) three armed cells, killing two people and arresting ten. The ministry alleged those detained had received military, bomb-making and assassination training outside Iran before entering the country.

On Sunday, authorities announced the arrest of three people in Chabahar and Dashtiari whom they linked to Jaish al-Adl. Officials said they had identified a safe house and seized weapons and ammunition.

A day later, the regime [executed Omar Dorostaran](https://www.tasnimnews.ir/fa/news/1405/07/20/3720921). Authorities described him as a key Jaish al-Adl operative who supplied weapons, safe houses and logistical support to attack teams. His case, however, was based on earlier attacks in Rask and Chabahar and predates this month’s violence.

title: Jacinta Ngobese-Zuma reported to IEC for xenophobic smear on Rise candidate Aziz Ally
summary: March and March leader Jacinta Ngobese-Zuma, as well as Operation Dudula, the anti-migrant party contesting the local government election, have attacked Rise Mzansi’s Johannesburg Ward 58 councillor candidate Aziz Ally because they thought
content:
March and March leader Jacinta Ngobese-Zuma, as well as Operation Dudula, the anti-migrant party contesting the local government election, have attacked Rise Mzansi’s Johannesburg Ward 58 councillor candidate Aziz Ally because they thought he was Somali.

Ally is South African.

“We have submitted a complaint to the IEC as of today. We have not laid a criminal charge,” said Rise Mzansi’s Johannesburg mayoral candidate Lukhona Mnguni on Wednesday, 14 October.

March and March social media influencers and office-bearers have said that her arrest for “Islamophobia” is imminent, but it may relate to the IEC complaint by Rise instead.

Operation Dudula also earlier attacked a Somali community activist, who is documented and legally in South Africa, when they saw a photograph and a video of him putting up posters in the area, which is South Africa’s most migrant-rich, with 23 communities from different parts of the world calling it home. He was helping Ally.

An Operation Dudula social media post of a documented Somali community activist supporting Aziz Ally’s campaign. (Photo: Supplied / Facebook)

Both anti-migrant organisations unleashed a volley of lies about both men.Ngobese-Zuma said that foreigners were actively running for office and voting for each other to take over South Africa.

On 7 October, Operation Dudula entered this post on Facebook. It reads: “A Somali national is campaigning for the Rise Mzansi party. He says people must vote for Aziz Ally in Ward 58 to get a better life.”

Then Ngobese-Zuma followed, mistaking Ally for a Somali national too.

 Community activist Aziz Ally, right, on an inspection in Ward 58. (Photo: Supplied / Aziz Ally)

He is, in fact, South African and was born in KwaZulu-Natal. Ally is part of a group of dedicated Ward 58 community activists who are up night and day dealing with daily water and power cuts as well as regular fires, like [the one reported here](https://www.dailymaverick.co.za/article/2026-10-08-mayfair-fire/) by Jamie Ho.

Mayfair has regular fires and no water and electricity on most days. For years, Ally has documented and reported overcrowding, which leads to unsafe living conditions, as [Daily Maverick reported here](https://www.dailymaverick.co.za/article/2025-05-19-we-warned-you-joburg-ignored-years-of-alerts-before-four-mayfair-toddlers-died-in-fire/).

Ally decided to contest the election on 4 November to attempt to bring better governance to a ward long recognised as one of Johannesburg’s most troubled. People from across the African continent, as well as India, Pakistan and Bangladesh, have settled in Ward 58, in which, like Yeoville, Berea and Hillbrow, among other nodes, infrastructure has largely collapsed due to overcrowding.

March and March and Operation Dudula have tried to protest in the area, [but the tight-knit community](https://groundup.org.za/article/mayfair-immigrants-put-their-faith-in-south-africas-police-to-protect-them/) has kept a lid on violence and often sent agents provocateurs scurrying away.

Community activist Aziz Ally in action in Ward 58, Johannesburg. The councillor candidate does everything from reporting illegal scrap dealers to helping people to register complaints with the City about illegal planning and development. (Photo: Supplied / Aziz Ally)

Rise Mzansi has filed a complaint with the IEC over active disinformation and breach of the Electoral Code of Conduct.

It has brought a complaint against both Ngobese-Zuma and Thomas Mabaso, the host of “The 360 Experience with Thomas Mabaso” podcast, whom the party says amplified the disinformation.

The prohibited conduct included the reckless disregard for verifiable facts (Ally is South African; his Somalian activist aide is documented); fuelling hostility and xenophobia; and undermining electoral integrity by falsely claiming that the electoral system is allowing non-citizens to run as candidates.

Rise Mzansi has implored the IEC to investigate the posts and videos by Ngobese-Zuma and Mabaso; to direct their immediate takedown and correction; and to refer the matter for sanction under its Disinformation Code and the Municipal Electoral Act.

“She said ‘Aziz’ is not a South African name and that I must be Ethiopian or Somalian,” Ally told Daily Maverick.

He was scared after the attacks.

“I didn’t leave the house. It’s a diverse ward; you must unite people,” he said, explaining that he worked with all communities and regularly with the documented Somali migrant who was also attacked.

He said his friend was often part of community clean-ups and patrols.The Ward 58 community has its ups and downs, but it is largely united and offers a way of co-existing and partnership.

“I started campaigning in September, and all was going well. It really broke me. I don’t have motivation any more,” said Ally. **DM**

# DEFENSE/Ex-U.S. national intelligence director praises Han Kuang reforms

10/14/2026 01:27 PM

[](jsvscript:)[](jsvscript:)[](javascript:void(0))[Listen](javascript:)

Dennis Blair, director of national intelligence under former U.S. President Barack Obama. CNA file photo

Taipei, Oct. 14 (CNA) Dennis Blair, director of national intelligence under former U.S. President Barack Obama, on Wednesday praised Taiwan's decision in recent years to transform its large-scale annual military exercises into a whole-of-society defense effort.

Speaking virtually at a security conference in Taipei, Blair told the audience that Taiwan's decision to transform the Han Kuang exercises from "a purely military one" into what he described as a "nation-defensive exercise" was a great decision.

By doing so, Taiwan would be "making sure that all of the capabilities of Taiwan are mobilized and brought to bear," said Blair, a former U.S. Navy admiral who commanded U.S. forces in the Pacific before retiring in 2002.

He argued that Taiwan's all-out effort to demonstrate its determination to defend itself would help convince like-minded countries and regional partners to come to its aid in an emergency.

"And of course, helping Taiwan is very much in the interests of all seafaring nations."

"After all, if Taiwan can be bullied into giving up parts of its sovereignty, then Japan, the Philippines, Vietnam, Malaysia, Korea, all of the countries of the world have to wonder, the region has to wonder about whether they are next," he said.

Two Clouded Leopard armored vehicles advance through the streets during a military exercise in the annual Han Kuang exercises. CNA photo Aug. 13, 2026

The annual Han Kuang exercises have served as Taiwan's primary war games since 1984, testing the country's combat readiness in the event of a possible Chinese invasion.

Originally involving only military personnel from all branches of the armed forces, the exercises have in recent years been expanded to incorporate whole-of-society defense resilience drills to promote active civil-military operations.

Blair also suggested in his address that Taipei should continue its efforts to monitor maritime activities and enforce laws in waters under its jurisdiction, as China continues to send civilian and government vessels into Taiwan's waters.

Beyond these monitoring and enforcement efforts, he argued that Taiwan needs an active campaign of diplomacy and public outreach, similar to what the Philippines has undertaken in its disputes and confrontations with China in the South China Sea.

"The objective is to convey the message that Chinese claims and operations are both illegal and inept. In order to win and retain world attention, Taiwanese public diplomacy needs to be inventive and fresh. Taiwan cannot allow China to establish a new normal in the international public perception."

Blair made the remarks remotely during the 2026 International Conference on Sea Lane Security, organized by Taiwan's Ocean Affairs Council.

At the opening of the one-day conference, Lii Wen (李問), deputy secretary-general of Taiwan's National Security Council, thanked like-minded partners for jointly voicing opposition to China's destabilizing actions in the East China Sea, Taiwan Strait and South China Sea.

He called for greater international and regional cooperation to strengthen early-warning capabilities and for international partners to maintain their maritime presence through measures such as freedom of navigation operations and regional cooperation to combat maritime crime.

(By Joseph Yeh)

title: 穆勒纳尔促战争部扩大“1286清单”，限制与更多中国高校及实验室合作
summary: 美国国会众议院美国与中共战略竞争特设委员会主席约翰·穆勒纳尔(John Moolenaar)呼吁美国战争部扩大一份涉及研究安全的管控清单，将更多被指与中国国防科研体系存在关联的高校、实验室、科研机构及人才引进计划纳入其中，以防止美国纳税人资助的科研成果被中国政府或军方利用。 穆勒纳尔星期三(10月14日)公布了写给战争部长皮特·海格塞斯(Pete Hegseth)的[信函](https://chinaselectcommittee.house.gov/media/press-
content:
美国国会众议院美国与中共战略竞争特设委员会主席约翰·穆勒纳尔(John Moolenaar)呼吁美国战争部扩大一份涉及研究安全的管控清单，将更多被指与中国国防科研体系存在关联的高校、实验室、科研机构及人才引进计划纳入其中，以防止美国纳税人资助的科研成果被中国政府或军方利用。

穆勒纳尔星期三(10月14日)公布了写给战争部长皮特·海格塞斯(Pete Hegseth)的[信函](https://chinaselectcommittee.house.gov/media/press-releases/moolenaar-calls-for-pentagon-to-update-its-list-of-pla-linked-institutions-and-talent-recruitment-programs)。他建议战争部在“第1286条清单”(Section 1286 List)中增加14家被特设委员会认定为中共“核心国防合作伙伴”的中国科学院下属研究所、62家实验室和国防实验室、58所大学、22项外国恶意人才引进计划，以及中国国家留学基金管理委员会(CSC)和获得该机构资助的研究人员。

穆勒纳尔说，扩大清单的目的是加强美国的研究安全，防止中国及其他外国对手利用战争部资助的科研成果。

**清单直接影响战争部研究经费**

“第1286条清单”依据2019财政年度《国防授权法》第1286条设立，用于识别美国政府认定对国家安全构成风险的外国科研机构、企业、个人和人才引进计划。

从2026财政年度开始，战争部不得为涉及清单内实体的基础研究项目提供资金。这项限制适用于研究拨款、合同及其他形式的资助，并禁止受资助机构与清单内实体共同开展研究或使用对方设备。研究人员如果与清单内机构的人员合作，也可能影响其获得联邦科研经费的资格。

战争部今年7月更新了清单，目前列有中国、俄罗斯和伊朗的130所高校和科研机构。战争部8月还要求30所美国高校审查其与外国机构的学术、资金和科研联系，并采取整改措施。

穆勒纳尔赞扬战争部近年来强化科研安全评估，并限制接受战争部资助的研究人员与美国政府管控清单上的机构合作。

“在这些努力中，战争部的‘第1286条清单’发挥着核心作用，”穆勒纳尔在信中说。“一个实体是否被列入清单，可能直接决定接受战争部资助的研究人员能否与该实体保持科研合作关系。”

他表示，随着列入清单产生的实际后果日益扩大，清单是否完整、准确也变得更加重要。

“这一框架能否发挥作用，不仅取决于对清单内实体施加的限制，也取决于战争部能否识别并认定符合相关标准的外国机构，”穆勒纳尔说。他警告，清单存在的覆盖缺口可能为接受战争部资助的研究人员和机构留下继续与中国相关组织合作的渠道。

**涉及军工、半导体、量子和人工智能**

穆勒纳尔说，特设委员会发现，一些尚未被列入清单的中国科研机构，与中国的国防科研和工业体系存在有记录的隶属、监管、协议或其他重要联系。

他要求战争部审查的机构包括中国科学院下属研究所，以及从事武器、航空航天、高超音速技术、半导体、水下系统、电子战等军事相关研究的实验室。名单还包括由中国国家国防科技工业局(SASTIND)共同管理或支持的高校。

人才引进计划部分则主要涉及量子技术和人工智能等关键及新兴技术领域。

穆勒纳尔说：“以下列出的几类机构尤其值得关注，因为它们与国防体系的关联已经得到美国政府或其他研究安全机构的记录和证实。”

据路透社报道，穆勒纳尔建议增加的58所高校包括清华大学。战争部目前尚未宣布是否接受他的建议；信中提到的机构也并未因为特设委员会的提名而自动受到限制。是否列入清单仍须由战争部依据相关法定标准进行认定。

近年来，美国国会和行政部门不断加强对外国政府参与美国科研项目的审查，重点包括隐瞒外国资金来源、参加外国人才计划、知识产权转移，以及敏感或军民两用技术可能流向外国军方等问题。

中国驻美使馆此前在回应战争部要求美国高校审查外国合作关系时，指责美方将国家安全概念泛化，并把正常的科学、教育和学术交流政治化。北京呼吁美国为两国学术与科研合作提供开放、公平和非歧视性的环境。这一表态并非针对穆勒纳尔最新信函作出。

**要求限制国家留学基金委受资助人员**

除了扩大机构名单，穆勒纳尔还要求战争部禁止任何接受中国国家留学基金管理委员会资助或其他经济支持的研究人员、研究生和博士后参与战争部资助的科研项目。

他主张，这项限制应在有关人员接受中方资助期间持续有效，无论他们是否被正式列为项目负责人、共同研究人员或其他具名参与者。

穆勒纳尔说，中国国家留学基金管理委员会不同于一般国际学生资助项目。该机构近年来因涉及学术自由、对留学生的监控、意识形态要求和潜在间谍活动等指控，在美国受到越来越严格的审查。

Your phone isn't just for posting stories and playing music. That little computer in your pocket has more power than entire governments had 20 years ago. Like the ancient Abhaya Mudra - the fearless hand gesture that banishes fear and offers protection from the "Evil Eye" - we're transforming these devices into something that helps communities meet the coming challenges with a sense of fearlessness, rooted in Free Collaboration and Privacy.

**Abhaya started as disaster recovery - how do communities rebuild communication when the towers are down and the power's out?** But we realized something profound: the same tools that help neighborhoods coordinate after a hurricane are exactly what we need when authoritarians try to silence us. Like the protective Abhaya Mudra, this system creates a shield against the "evil eye" of surveillance while becoming a helpful digital companion that guides and empowers our communities.

Drawing inspiration from Buckminster Fuller's vision of global cooperation for humanity's benefit, Abhaya is designed as the foundation for communities to work together toward a more equitable future. The ecosystem operates through five interconnected elements:

**The Five Core Components:**

• **Tor + Mobile based Mesh Networks**: Messages that flow around censorship like water

• **Mesh Based Distributed Storage**: Truth that lives everywhere so it can't be destroyed

• **Mesh Based Distributed Computation Service**: AI-capable shared processing power for communities to solve their own challenges

• **Sensor/Peripheral IO**: User Controlled Eyes and ears embedded in the network

• **Mesh Federation**: Connecting local networks into unstoppable global resistance

**History demonstrates the need**

_"The ultimate measure of a man is not where he stands in moments of comfort and convenience, but where he stands at times of challenge and controversy."_ - MLK Jr.

Iranian women shared videos of police brutality when the state blocked social media. Puerto Ricans coordinated mutual aid through amateur radio when Maria destroyed the grid.

• Android & iOS Development
