Taipei, Oct. 17 (CNA) Taiwanese made 2.492 million trips to China in the first eight months of this year, up 19.63 percent from a year earlier, even as the government kept its orange travel warning in place for China, Hong Kong and Macau.

China was the second most popular overseas destination for Taiwanese travelers after Japan, according to the latest statistics from the Tourism Administration. Trips to China have exceeded 300,000 every month since March, with March recording the largest year-on-year increase at 32.34 percent.

Taiwan has maintained the orange warning for China, Hong Kong and Macau since June 27, 2024. Orange is the second-highest warning level in Taiwan's four-tier travel advisory system and advises the public to avoid nonessential travel to the affected destinations.

The Mainland Affairs Council (MAC) said the increase in trips to China was part of a broader rise in outbound travel, which grew 15.24 percent year-on-year over the same period.

It attributed the trend partly to Taiwan's economic growth and rising stock prices, which have boosted people's wealth and made people more willing to spend on overseas travel.

The MAC urged people planning to visit China to carefully assess the risks and keep up with official travel safety updates, citing changes to China's national security laws and entry-exit regulations.

Huang Cheng-tsung (黃正聰), an associate professor in Providence University's Department of Tourism, told CNA that the rise was in line with overall growth in outbound travel, and that business trips may also have contributed.

Hung Pu-chao (洪浦釗), director of the Center for Global Strategy and Democratic Resilience at the University of Taipei, said some Taiwanese travelers may judge the risks based on previous visits.

However, past trouble-free trips do not guarantee the same experience in the future, he warned, citing cases in which Taiwanese have been questioned, detained or had their freedom of movement restricted in China.

Hung said the government faces challenges in communicating travel risks, as the orange warning has been in place for more than two years and may have limited influence on people who need to travel across the Taiwan Strait.

He called for more specific information tailored to travelers' backgrounds and purposes, including guidance on seeking help if they are questioned or prevented from leaving.

(By Lee Ya-wen and Lee Hsin-Yin)

content:
中新社台北10月16日电 中选会周五表示，台湾即将举行的地方选举市县议会席位竞选，包括新党候选人游智彬在内的10名候选人被判定为不合格。

CEC在一份新闻稿中表示，在10名被取消资格的议会候选人中，有5名正在竞选直辖市议会席位，5名正在竞选县或市议会席位。

正在竞选台北市议员的尤出生于中国福建省。中委会表示，他原本是中国大陆居民，并提交了他于2025年4月放弃大陆户口的证明。

根据《台湾地区与大陆地区人民关系条例》及相关选举法规定，像游这样情况的人，必须在提交放弃大陆户籍证明后，已在台湾地区登记为居民满10年。

CEC 表示，你们没有满足这一要求。

此外，该委员会表示，四名被取消资格的市议会候选人因刑事定罪或刑期未服满而被裁定不符合资格。
他们是新北市的林正峰，因洗钱罪被定罪；台中人郑伯其，被判诈骗罪；曹暐国，台南人，因枪支弹药法被定罪；桃园市的萧湘瀚，因妨碍公务罪等罪名尚未服刑完毕。

被取消资格的五名县市议员候选人分别是：云林县钟任明、嘉义县何博伦、花莲县周骏宥、金门县石永城、基隆县张芳丽。

中央选举委员会表示，候选人号码将于10月23日在地方选举委员会办公室抽签。候选人的财务披露信息也将在网上公布，自候选人名单最终确定之日起一年内。

台湾2026年地方选举定于11月28日举行，也被称为“九合一”选举，因为台湾22个市县的选民将投票选出竞选九个不同地方政府职位的候选人，包括市长、县长、市县议员。

（吴树伟、李心音撰）

结局/ASG

【原文 English Original】
Taipei, Oct. 16 (CNA) A total of 10 candidates running for city and county council seats in Taiwan's upcoming local elections have been ruled ineligible, including New Party candidate You Zhi-bin (游智彬), the Central Election Commission (CEC) said Friday.

Of the 10 disqualified council candidates, five were running for special municipality council seats and five for county or city council seats, the CEC said in a news release.

You, who is running for a Taipei City Council seat, was born in Fujian Province, China. The CEC said he was originally a resident of mainland China and submitted proof that he had relinquished his mainland household registration in April 2025.

Under the Act Governing Relations Between the People of the Taiwan Area and the Mainland Area and relevant election laws, people in You's circumstances must have been registered as residents in Taiwan for at least 10 years after submitting proof that they had relinquished their mainland household registration.

You had not met this requirement, the CEC said.

In addition, four disqualified city council candidates were ruled ineligible because of criminal convictions, or sentences that had not been fully served, the commission said.

They were Lin Cheng-feng (林正峰) of New Taipei, convicted of money laundering; Cheng Po-chi (鄭伯其) of Taichung, convicted of fraud; Tsao Wei-kuo (曹暐國) of Tainan, convicted under the law governing firearms and ammunition; and Hsiao Hsiang-han (蕭湘瀚) of Taoyuan, whose sentence for offenses including obstruction of official duties remained uncompleted.

The five disqualified county and city council candidates were Chung Jen-ming (鍾任明) of Yunlin County, Ho Po-lun (何博倫) of Chiayi County, Chou Chun-yu (周駿宥) of Hualien County, Shih Yung-cheng (石永城) of Kinmen County and Chang Fang-li (張芳麗) of Keelung.

The CEC said candidate numbers will be drawn at local election commission offices on Oct. 23. Candidates' financial disclosure information will also be published online for one year from the date the candidate lists are finalized.

Taiwan's 2026 local elections, slated for Nov. 28, are also known as the "9-in-1" elections because voters in Taiwan's 22 cities and counties will cast ballots for candidates vying for nine different local government posts, including city mayors, county magistrates, and city and county councilors.

(By Wu Shu-wei and Lee Hsin-Yin)

# Taiwan plans U.S. industrial parks with private funding, government aid

10/16/2026 04:15 PM

[](jsvscript:)[](jsvscript:)[](javascript:void(0))[Listen](javascript:)

[Link](javascript:)[Whatsapp](javascript:)[Reddit](javascript:)[Line](javascript:)[Email](javascript:)

To activate the text-to-speech service, please first agree to the privacy policy below.

Minister of Economic Affairs Kung Ming-hsin. CNA file photo

Taipei, Oct. 16 (CNA) Taiwan's government plans to develop industrial parks in the United States based on a model in which private businesses provide the funding while the government offers assistance, with each park costing US$2 billion to US$4 billion, the Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA) said Friday.

The government will work with the Taiwan Electrical and Electronic Manufacturers' Association (TEEMA) to promote the initiative, the MOEA said.

The comments followed a [Bloomberg](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-10-16/taiwan-to-fund-4-billion-texas-complex-for-ai-nvidia-partners) report published earlier Friday that Taiwan plans to develop industrial parks in the United States to build a comprehensive supply chain supporting Nvidia Corp. and other artificial intelligence (AI) hardware makers.

Screenshot from Bloomberg

In an interview with Bloomberg earlier this week, Minister of Economic Affairs Kung Ming-hsin (龔明鑫) said the proposed parks would help smaller suppliers that support Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. (TSMC) and AI server makers such as Foxconn Technology Group establish operations in the United States.

Kung added that the government is planning more than one site in the United States, with the initiative set to start with a complex in Texas.

He also told Bloomberg that Taiwan's government would support suppliers seeking to operate in the parks by offering loan guarantees and helping them coordinate with U.S. federal and local officials on matters such as visas and land.

Asked about the report which said land has already been secured in Texas for an industrial park, the MOEA said it would provide details at a later date.

Hon Hai Precision Industry Co. (Foxconn) Chairman Young Liu (劉揚偉), who also chairs TEEMA's Supervisory Committee, said recently that potential locations for overseas science parks included Arizona and Texas, as well as Mexico, Poland and India.

The parks are intended to help small and medium-sized Taiwanese businesses expand into overseas markets and connect with local government agencies and companies to foster supply chain cooperation, Liu added at the time.

(By Tseng Yun-ting and Ko Lin)

title: Leave forms, bags of cash link Hawks member to alleged ‘crime syndicate’
summary: Last year, a member of the Hawks allegedly booked leave on two occasions to travel to Nelson Mandela Bay so he could join other members of a kidnapping syndicate to abduct two women for ransom. Around the same time, he spent his share of th
content:
Last year, a member of the Hawks allegedly booked leave on two occasions to travel to Nelson Mandela Bay so he could join other members of a kidnapping syndicate to abduct two women for ransom.

Around the same time, he spent his share of the ransom money on a luxury car, which was parked at a house in Motherwell where the police found close to R200,000 in marked bills used to pay the ransom, as well as a firearm that was used in the [assassination of Gqeberha prosecutor Tracy Brown](https://www.dailymaverick.co.za/article/2025-08-02-gqeberha-prosecutor-gunned-down-outside-her-home-in-planned-hit-emphasises-high-stakes/).

These were among allegations levelled against Xolani Busakwe at the Gqeberha Magistrates’ Court on Thursday, where State advocate Marius Stander led evidence opposing his formal bail application.

Busakwe, a member of the Hawks’ Digital Forensic Investigation Unit, sat in the dock with slumped shoulders as Stander outlined the State’s case that he is allegedly linked to a criminal syndicate responsible for Brown’s death and at least two kidnappings for ransom – all in the space of three months last year.

He faces a string of charges including kidnapping, human trafficking, extortion and robbery with aggravating circumstances, as well as charges under the Prevention of Organised Crime Act.

His co-accused, Simthembile Xungu, David Mthembu, Buhle Mbini, Andile Mathumbu, Unathi Mayi and his brother Ayabulela Busakwe face similar charges, while some have also been charged with murder and conspiracy to commit murder in relation to the hit on Brown.

 Ayabulela Busakwe (left) and Simthembile Xungu will remain behind bars until the start of the trial. (Photo: Riaan Marais)

According to an affidavit prepared by the Hawks and read into the court record by Stander, Busakwe was a police officer stationed at the Gqeberha Local Criminal Records Centre before he was transferred to the Directorate for Priority Crime Investigation (Hawks) head office in Pretoria, where he was assigned to the Digital Forensic Investigations Unit in 2024.

In June 2025, Busakwe submitted a leave request and planned to visit his home in Motherwell. It was during this time that cellphone records place him in the vicinity of the Markman Fresh Produce Market where [Lindsay Knowlden was kidnapped](https://www.dailymaverick.co.za/article/2025-06-25-abducted-held-captive-for-4-days-lindsay-knowlden-reunited-with-family/).

Cellphone records also placed Mthembu, Mbini and Mathumbu in the same location and indicated continuous communication between the four men around the time of the kidnapping.

It was also revealed that the last known live location of Knowlden’s cellphone was Mathumbu’s home address in Motherwell.

Lindsay Knowlden was kidnapped from the Fresh Produce Market in Markman Industrial in June 2025. (Photo: Deon Ferreira / Facebook)

A ransom amount of R1.25-million was paid for Knowlden’s release. The following day, Busakwe and his brother contacted a used car dealership in George, Western Cape, to negotiate the cash purchase of a BMW to the tune of R155,000.

The two brothers, along with a friend, Lungile Jika, travelled to the dealership a few days later with a plastic bag full of cash to complete the transaction. However, the deal was delayed when the salesman became suspicious.

The car was subsequently purchased via an electronic fund transfer and registered in Jika’s name.

Stander said it was the State’s case that the Busakwes, along with Mthembu, Mbini and Mathumbu, orchestrated Knowlden’s kidnapping, and that the BMW was purchased with a portion of the ransom money.

Between 11 and 14 August 2025, Busakwe was scheduled to testify in a court case in Nelson Mandela Bay, and the police booked his flights between Pretoria and Gqeberha. The day after his flights were confirmed, he booked leave for the days leading up to the court dates, claiming he would be in Nelson Mandela Bay due to a family bereavement.

On 11 August, [Theresa Minnie was kidnapped outside her home in Kariega](https://www.dailymaverick.co.za/article/2025-08-12-hawks-mum-on-arrests-after-numerous-nelson-mandela-bay-kidnappings/). A ransom of R1.1-million was paid to secure her release. However, before the payment was made, the Hawks marked the cash with a fluorescent powder.

Theresa Minnie was kidnapped from her home in Kariega, Eastern Cape, on 11 August 2025. (Photo: Facebook)

The suspects were subsequently tracked, and in the week following the kidnapping, Ayabulela Busakwe and Mathumbu were arrested and found in possession of large sums of cash, including banknotes marked with the fluorescent powder.

Stander also indicated that during questioning, Ayabulela Busakwe made a partial confession that a “Xolani” was involved in the kidnapping, effectively fingering his brother as an accomplice.

Further investigation led the police to an address where the accused allegedly stashed some of their loot. The police found R197,000 marked with the fluorescent powder, as well as a firearm that has since been positively linked to the murder of prosecutor Tracy Brown.

Gqeberha prosecutor Tracy Brown was gunned down at her Young Park, Gqeberha home on 31 July, 2025. (Photo: Supplied / Facebook)

A witness also told the police that Ayabulela Busakwe parked a BMW at the address, but that his brother later came to fetch the vehicle.

Xolani Busakwe missed his flight from Gqeberha to Pretoria on 14 August. It is the State’s case that he waited in Nelson Mandela Bay until he was certain that Minnie’s ransom had been paid before driving the BMW, purchased with Knowlden’s ransom money, back to Pretoria.

The vehicle has since been located in Pretoria and is the subject of an asset forfeiture application.

Stander also indicated that Busakwe faces charges of theft and defeating the ends of justice in a separate case. During the search of his residence, police uncovered 12 dockets related to a 2022 investigation at the Local Criminal Record Centre at Mount Road police station in Gqeberha, where Busakwe had previously been stationed.

The State submitted that it would be in the interests of justice for the court to deny Busakwe bail, mainly because of his familiarity with police systems and some of the witnesses, and he could easily interfere with the investigation and possibly tamper with evidence.

The case was postponed until Friday for closing arguments by the State and defence. Busakwe is scheduled to return to court alongside his co-accused next week. **DM**

Where is Mauritius?

15 October 2026

Mauritius has[imposed](https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cm4g1rnj5qweo "https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cm4g1rnj5qweo")an overnight curfew following violent protests over water shortages and the rising cost of living, marking the island's worst unrest in decades.

Demonstrations escalated after a woman was shot and injured by police at a roadblock. The circumstances of the shooting were not clear, but the officer has since been arrested and remanded in custody.

Protesters burned tyres, blocked roads and vandalised police stations and public infrastructure, prompting school and public transport closures.

The British embassy in Mauritius cautioned its citizens about the possibility of further demonstrations, advising them to steer clear of protests and large gatherings. The French embassy also urged French nationals in the country to remain vigilant.

Prime Minister Navin Ramgoolam warned that those responsible would face consequences.

Analysts warn that unrest could return if water shortages persist until the rainy season in December.

title: Belize PM Briceño seeks deeper cooperation with Taiwan, invites investment - Focus Taiwan
zh_title: 伯利兹总理布里塞尼奥寻求与台湾深化合作并邀请投资 - 聚焦台湾
summary: By Zachary Lee, CNA staff reporter Belize Prime Minister John Briceño has called for deeper cooperation with Taiwan through investment, technology exchanges, and people-to-people ties, saying that he hopes those links will contribute to his country's development.周三，布里塞尼奥在曼谷接受中央社专访时，热情评价了伯利兹与台湾的密切关系，并强调了在虾养殖技术和实用技术交流等领域的潜在合作潜力。 ## 伯利兹寻求台湾投资和技术 66 岁的 Briceño 表示，伯利兹的年轻人口是
content:
中央社记者 Zachary Lee

伯利兹总理约翰·布里塞尼奥呼吁通过投资、技术交流和人文联系与台湾深化合作，并表示希望这些联系将为伯利兹的发展做出贡献。

周三，布里塞尼奥在曼谷接受中央社专访时，热情评价了伯利兹与台湾的密切关系，并强调了在虾养殖技术和实用技术交流等领域的潜在合作潜力。

## 伯利兹寻求台湾投资和技术

66 岁的布里塞尼奥表示，伯利兹的年轻人口是技术合作的优势。

“我们有一群年轻人，他们从大专到大学，学得很快。所以这些都是我们可以合作的领域，”他强调说。

布里塞尼奥表示，在人工智能开发领域，与台湾的合作不一定要从最先进的技术开始，而是可以专注于满足伯利兹需求的实用解决方案。

“例如，虾类养殖技术是台湾可以做出贡献的领域之一，”他说。

他还强调了人文交流的价值，称在伯利兹工作的台湾学生可以帮助加强两国之间的关系。

目前，有六名台湾交换生在伯利兹政府部门和其他领域工作。
伯利兹领导人表示，对伯利兹来说，吸引商业投资和建设技术能力是扩大经济机会和提高生活水平的更广泛努力的一部分。

## 伯利兹呼吁更多地考虑小国

布里塞尼奥作为伯利兹财政部长兼世界银行小国论坛主席出席在曼谷举行的国际货币基金组织和世界银行集团 2026 年年会。

他在接受中央社采访时表示，国际金融机构需要考虑到小国有限的行政能力和资源。

他举例说，他的国家在参与世界银行资助的项目以帮助小农增强应对气候变化的能力时面临挑战。

布里塞尼奥表示，当伯利兹完成冗长的申请程序时，已接近截止日期，他不得不请求世界银行延长期限。

## Other challenges faced by small countries

布里塞尼奥说，气候变化是影响小国的问题之一。布里塞尼奥说，目前，加勒比岛国和该地区其他沿海国家正在应对大量涌入的褐马尾藻，这威胁到旅游业的主要经济命脉，并呼吁采取区域解决方案。
总理表示，在伯利兹，鉴于税基有限，另一个重大挑战是为其分布广泛的约 42 万人口提供基本基础设施和服务。

“我们必须不断地思考如何在提供基本服务、供水、供电以及教育和保健方面找到平衡，”他说，并解释说伯利兹有 196 个小社区。

布里塞尼奥说，政府必须平衡居民的需求与有限的资源，同时保持财政可持续性。

## 伯利兹重申支持台湾

布里塞尼奥重申，作为台湾的长期伙伴，伯利兹致力于发展与台湾的关系，并表示中国最近对伯利兹外交部长实施制裁

【原文 English Original】
By Zachary Lee, CNA staff reporter

Belize Prime Minister John Briceño has called for deeper cooperation with Taiwan through investment, technology exchanges, and people-to-people ties, saying that he hopes those links will contribute to his country's development.

In an exclusive interview with CNA in Bangkok on Wednesday, Briceño spoke warmly of Belize's close ties with Taiwan and highlighted areas such as shrimp farming technology and practical technology exchanges for potential cooperation.

## Belize seeks Taiwanese investment and technology

Briceño, 66, said Belize's young population was an advantage for technology cooperation.

"We have a young population, and they go to junior college on to university, and they learn quickly. So these are areas where we can collaborate," he emphasized.

In the field of AI development, cooperation with Taiwan does not necessarily have to begin with the most advanced technologies, but instead could focus on practical solutions that meet Belize's needs, Briceño said.

"For example, shrimp farming technology is one area where Taiwan could contribute," he said.

He also emphasized the value of people-to-people exchanges, saying that Taiwanese students working in Belize could help strengthen ties between the two countries.

Currently, there are six Taiwanese exchange students working in government ministries and other fields in Belize.

For Belize, attracting business investment and building technological capacity are part of a broader effort to expand economic opportunities and improve living standards, according to its leader.

## Belize calls for greater consideration of small states

Briceño is attending the 2026 Annual Meetings of the International Monetary Fund and the World Bank Group in Bangkok as Belize's finance minister and chair of the World Bank's Small States Forum.

In his interview with CNA, he said international financial institutions need to take into account the limited administrative capacity and resources of small countries.

He cited as an example the challenge his country faced in participating in a World Bank-funded project to help small farmers strengthen their resilience to climate change.

Briceño said that by the time Belize had completed the lengthy application procedure, it was close to the deadline, and he had to ask the World Bank to extend the timeframe.

## Other challenges faced by small countries

Climate change is one of the issues affecting small nations, Briceño said. Currently, Caribbean island nations and other coastal countries in the region are dealing with a massive influx of brown sargassum seaweed, which threatens tourism -- a major economic lifeline, Briceño said, calling for regional solutions.

In Belize, another significant challenge is providing basic infrastructure and services to its widely dispersed population of about 420,000, given its limited tax base, the prime minister said.

"We have to constantly see how we can find that balance in providing basic services, access to water, access to electricity, and access to education and health," he said, explaining that Belize has 196 small communities.

The government must balance residents' needs against its limited resources while maintaining fiscal sustainability, Briceño said.

## Belize reaffirms support for Taiwan

As a long-standing partner of Taiwan, Belize is committed to its relations with Taiwan, Briceño reaffirmed, saying China's recent sanctions against Belize's Minister of Foreign Affairs and Foreign Trade Francis Fonseca will not change that position.

Belize is an independent country with the right to decide which countries it maintains relations with, Briceño said, condemning China's sanctions as unreasonable, unnecessary, wrong and illegal.

That move by China will only serve to strengthen Belize's resolve to support Taiwan, he said.

"We strongly believe in the right to self-determination," he said, arguing that Taiwan's strengths in the economy, technology, artificial intelligence, health care, education and climate research warrant recognition by the United Nations and other international organizations.

Briceño, who began his second term as prime minister in 2025, said he wants Belize to remain a free and democratic country with a vibrant economy capable of providing for its people.

Enditem/pc

title: Alaska LNG deal may boost Taiwan's energy resilience: U.S. scholar - Focus Taiwan

summary: 中新社华盛顿10月14日电 一位美国学者周三表示，台湾拟从阿拉斯加管道项目购买液化天然气(LNG)的协议可能会增强台湾的能源弹性，并缩小与美国的贸易顺差。史汀生中心高级研究员迈克尔·坎宁安（Michael Cunningham）对中央社表示，该协议可能会提高台湾作为美国出口市场的重要性，让华盛顿更有动力确保台湾的安全。他表示：“到 2050 年代，台湾仍将至关重要。”他补充说，预计该项目的出口不会开始
content:
中新社华盛顿10月14日电 一位美国学者周三表示，台湾拟从阿拉斯加管道项目购买液化天然气(LNG)的协议可能会增强台湾的能源弹性，并缩小与美国的贸易顺差。

史汀生中心高级研究员迈克尔·坎宁安（Michael Cunningham）对中央社表示，该协议可能会提高台湾作为美国出口市场的重要性，让华盛顿更有动力确保台湾的安全。

他表示：“到 2050 年代，台湾仍将至关重要。”他补充说，预计该项目的出口要到 2031 年才会开始。

坎宁安在回复中央社询问其对此问题看法的电子邮件时表示，“如果这项协议得以实现，将有助于增强台湾的能源弹性”并减少对美国的贸易顺差——这是华盛顿的优先事项。

据财政部统计，2025年，台湾对美国的贸易顺差约为1501亿美元。

周二，美国总统特朗普在阿拉斯加的一次集会上表示，台湾已同意在20年内购买计划中的阿拉斯加液化天然气管道项目30%的天然气产量，并为该项目额外投资44亿美元。他后来在其真相社交平台上的一篇帖子中重申了这一说法。
继他宣布这一消息后，台湾经济部周三证实，台湾国有企业中油集团将在阿拉斯加项目上投资至多44亿美元，并在投产后每年采购600万吨液化天然气。

经济部表示，长期购买和投资计划将使台湾的天然气供应多元化，并增强其能源弹性。

该部门表示，阿拉斯加液化天然气项目还将通过直接跨太平洋向台湾运送货物来减少运输和地缘政治风险。

经济部表示，如果该项目按计划进行，最早可能在 2032 年开始为台湾国内天然气供应做出贡献。

华盛顿哈德逊研究所高级研究员赖利·沃尔特斯表示，台湾对阿拉斯加液化天然气项目的承诺将有助于确保该管道的盈利能力。

沃尔特斯表示，该协议还将有助于台湾对美国做出更广泛的投资承诺，并指出台湾仍需要获得2000亿美元的信贷才能完成与华盛顿的战略投资协议。

（侯绮琳、柯琳）

【原文 English Original】
Washington, Oct. 14 (CNA) A proposed deal for Taiwan to purchase liquefied natural gas (LNG) from an Alaska pipeline project could strengthen Taiwan's energy resilience and narrow its trade surplus with the United States, an American scholar said Wednesday.

Michael Cunningham, a senior fellow at the Stimson Center, told CNA that the deal could increase Taiwan's importance as a market for U.S. exports, giving Washington greater incentive to ensure Taiwan's security.

"Taiwan will remain critically important into the 2050s," he said, adding that exports from the project are not expected to begin until 2031.

"If this deal materializes, it will help strengthen Taiwan's energy resilience" and reduce its trade surplus with the U.S. -- a priority for Washington, Cunningham said in an email response to CNA's request for his views on the issue.

In 2025, Taiwan recorded a trade surplus of approximately US$150.1 billion with the U.S., according to Ministry of Finance statistics.

On Tuesday, U.S. President Donald Trump said at a rally in Alaska that Taiwan had agreed to purchase 30 percent of the natural gas output from the planned Alaska LNG pipeline project over 20 years and invest an additional US$4.4 billion in the project. He later reiterated the claim in a post on his Truth Social platform.

Following his announcement, Taiwan's Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA) on Wednesday confirmed that the state-owned CPC Corp., Taiwan will invest up to US$4.4 billion in the Alaska project and purchase 6 million metric tons of LNG annually once production begins.

The long-term purchase and investment plan will diversify Taiwan's natural gas supplies and strengthen its energy resilience, the MOEA said.

The Alaska LNG project would also reduce transportation and geopolitical risks by sending shipments to Taiwan directly across the Pacific, the ministry said.

If the project proceeds as planned, it could begin contributing to Taiwan's domestic natural gas supply as early as 2032, according to the MOEA.

Riley Walters, a senior fellow at the Hudson Institute in Washington, said that Taiwan's commitment to the Alaska LNG project would help to ensure the pipeline's profitability.

The deal would also contribute to Taiwan's broader investment commitments to the U.S., Walters said, noting that Taiwan still needs to secure US$200 billion in credit to complete its strategic investment agreement with Washington.

(By Elaine Hou and Ko Lin)

Enditem/pc

14 October 2026

[New Zimbabwe (London)](http://newzimbabwe.com/ "Visit New Zimbabwe (London)")

CABINET has approved the implementation of a US$650 million floating solar power project on Lake Kariba, despite lingering concerns over the stalled Gwanda Solar Project, which was awarded to late businessman Wicknell Chivayo's company, Intratrek Zimbabwe.

The latest initiative comes amid questions over the lack of progress on the Gwanda project, which was approved in 2015 as a 100-megawatt solar power plant intended to help ease Zimbabwe's electricity shortages.

The tender was awarded to Chivayo and his engineering firm, Intratrek Zimbabwe. In April 2016, the Zimbabwe Power Company paid the company US$5 million upfront, but more than a decade after the project was approved, no meaningful progress has been made at the site.

With no clear steps to recover the upfront payment or compel Intratek to deliver, cabinet has now announced plans to implement another major solar power project.

Details of the Lake Kariba initiative were presented by Agriculture, Mechanisation and Water Resources Minister Dr Anxious Masuka during a post-Cabinet briefing.

"The Nation is informed that in December 2023, His Excellency the President Cde E.D. Mnangagwa, directed relevant Government Ministries to facilitate private sector investment for a 600 MW Floating Solar Power Plant on Lake Kariba.

"The Project was intended to augment hydropower generation in the country, stabilize power output, preserve water during the day through solar generation, and to enhance climate resilience and long-term sustainability of the Kariba power generation system," he said.

Masuka said the project is valued at US$650 million and will be implemented through a partnership between the Zimbabwe Electricity Transmission and Distribution Company (ZETDC), which will be the sole off-taker of the electricity generated, and GreenGrid Energy Private Limited, formerly known as Sunspire, as the developer.

"At full capacity, the plant is expected to provide power for 3 million people and create 1,000 direct jobs in Kariba. Progress recorded to date includes the completion of grid and technical studies; land survey and environmental impact assessment processes; regulatory licensing; and the negotiation of the Project's commercial agreements," he said.

According to Masuka, the Power Purchase Agreement and Transmission Connection Agreements were signed in 2025, while technical, regulatory and preparatory work was completed in July 2026.

Nigerian soldiers

13 October 2026

[Premium Times (Abuja)](http://premiumtimesng.com/ "Visit Premium Times (Abuja)")

By Yakubu Mohammed

_The listing places pressure on the Nigerian government to address concerns over child recruitment and demonstrate compliance with international standards on the protection of children in armed conflict._

The United States has placed Nigeria on its 2026 list of countries whose governments are identified as having armed forces, security forces or government-supported militias that recruit or use child soldiers, exposing the country to restrictions on certain US military assistance and equipment sales.

The designation, contained in the US State Department's 2026 Trafficking in Persons (TIP) Report, means Nigeria could face restrictions on specific security assistance and commercial licences for military equipment from 1 October, unless the restrictions are waived or an applicable exception is granted by US President Donald Trump.

Keep up with the latest headlines on [WhatsApp](https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VaIdDi8Bqbr263erhw1K "https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VaIdDi8Bqbr263erhw1K") | [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/company/allafrica/ "https://www.linkedin.com/company/allafrica/")

Nigeria is among 14 countries included on the 2026 Child Soldiers Prevention Act (CSPA) list, alongside Afghanistan, Burma, the Central African Republic, the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Ethiopia, Iran, Russia, Rwanda, Somalia, South Sudan, Sudan, Venezuela and Yemen.

Under Section 402 of the CSPA, the US government identifies foreign governments whose armed forces, police, other security forces or government-supported armed groups allegedly recruit or use child soldiers. The latest determinations cover 1 April 2025 to 31 March 2026.

The law prohibits certain forms of assistance to listed governments, including International Military Education and Training, Foreign Military Financing and Excess Defence Articles. It also restricts the issuance of licences for direct commercial sales of military equipment, subject to applicable exceptions and presidential waivers.

The restrictions could have implications for Nigeria's military cooperation with Washington, particularly in areas involving training, financing and the acquisition of US military equipment.

The State Department said its determination draws on multiple sources, including observations by US government personnel, United Nations agencies, international organisations, civil society groups and local and international media reports.

Under the CSPA, a child soldier includes anyone under 18 who is compulsorily recruited into government armed forces or security forces, as well as children recruited or used in hostilities by armed forces distinct from a state's military.

The definition also covers children serving in support roles, including as cooks, porters, messengers, medics, guards or victims of sexual exploitation.

Nigeria's inclusion on the list comes amid longstanding concerns about the recruitment and exploitation of children in the country's conflict zones, particularly in the North-east, where Boko Haram and the Islamic State West Africa Province (ISWAP) have abducted and recruited children for combat and support roles.

title: Lai calls for progress on unsigned Taiwan-Canada trade framework - Focus Taiwan
zh_title: 黎智英呼吁未签署的台加贸易框架取得进展 - 聚焦台湾
summary: 中新社台北10月14日电 赖清德总统14日表示，希望台湾与加拿大尚未签署的贸易合作框架能取得进展，并呼吁加强双边经济和产业合作。黎智英在台北总统府会见加拿大议员时表示，希望台加贸易合作框架安排（TCFA）能够在他们的支持下向前推进。代表团由自由党议员、加拿大-台湾议会友好小组和众议院主席朱迪·斯格罗（Judy Sgro）率领。
content:
中新社台北10月14日电 赖清德总统14日表示，希望台湾与加拿大尚未签署的贸易合作框架能取得进展，并呼吁加强双边经济和产业合作。

黎智英在台北总统府会见加拿大议员时表示，希望台加贸易合作框架安排（TCFA）能够在他们的支持下向前推进。

该代表团由自由党议员朱迪·斯格罗（Judy Sgro）率领，她也是加拿大-台湾议会友好小组和下议院国际贸易常设委员会的主席。

根据加拿大外交部全球事务部 9 月份对议会的回应，拟议的 TCFA 旨在加强双边贸易和经济合作，尽管其文本已于 2025 年 3 月最终确定，但仍未签署。

该部表示，该框架仍在考虑签署，但没有提供时间表。

赖表示，台湾在半导体、信息和通信技术方面的优势，加上加拿大在人工智能（AI）、能源和关键矿产方面的优势，使得两国经济在人工智能推动全球产业转型的过程中“高度互补”。
他表示，这些优势为“双边合作提供了广泛机遇”，并补充说，近年来双方在贸易、技术、供应链和海上安全等领域扩大了合作。

黎智英表示，台湾是加拿大在亚洲的第六大贸易伙伴，希望双方“发挥各自优势，推动更多实质性合作”，为两国产业和人民创造新机遇。

据台湾国际贸易管理局统计，2025年双边商品贸易额达48.9亿美元，同比增长5.6%。

在周三的会议上，黎智英还感谢加拿大立法者的支持，并引用了一项跨党派议会动议，反对他所说的中国歪曲联合国大会第2758号决议的行为，以及Sgro和下议院国际贸易常设委员会为推进TCFA所做的努力。

在黎智英之后发表讲话时，斯格罗表示，加拿大和台湾享有“强劲且不断发展的关系”，并列举了在贸易、投资、教育、科学、创新、文化和旅游方面的合作。

她说，牢固的关系“不仅通过正式协议建立，还通过持续对话、相互尊重和个人联系”建立。

不过，代表团团长在发言中并未具体提及TCFA。
第六次访问台湾的斯格罗表示，代表团的目的是加深议会对话并更好地了解印度-太平洋地区，她称该地区“对加拿大未来的繁荣与安全越来越重要”。

她说：“请知道，加拿大是朋友和伙伴，加拿大将与台湾站在一起。”

（赖阳光）

结局/AW

【原文 English Original】
Taipei, Oct. 14 (CNA) President Lai Ching-te (賴清德) on Wednesday expressed hope for progress on a proposed trade cooperation framework between Taiwan and Canada that remains unsigned, as he called for closer bilateral economic and industrial cooperation.

During a meeting with Canadian lawmakers at the Presidential Office in Taipei, Lai said he hoped the Taiwan-Canada Trade Cooperation Framework Arrangement (TCFA) would move forward with their support.

The delegation was led by Judy Sgro, a Liberal Party lawmaker who is also chair of the Canada-Taiwan Parliamentary Friendship Group and the House of Commons Standing Committee on International Trade.

The proposed TCFA, aimed at strengthening bilateral trade and economic cooperation, remains unsigned despite its text having been finalized in March 2025, according to a September response to Parliament by Global Affairs Canada, the country's foreign ministry.

The ministry said the framework is still being considered for signature but provided no timetable.

Lai said Taiwan's strengths in semiconductors and information and communications technology, alongside Canada's advantages in artificial intelligence (AI), energy and critical minerals, make their economies "highly complementary" as AI drives global industrial transformation.

He said those strengths presented "extensive opportunities for bilateral cooperation," adding that the two sides had expanded cooperation in trade, technology, supply chains and maritime security in recent years.

Noting that Taiwan is Canada's sixth-largest trading partner in Asia, Lai said he hopes both sides would "build on their respective strengths and promote even more substantive cooperation" to create new opportunities for their industries and people.

According to Taiwan's International Trade Administration, bilateral merchandise trade totaled US$4.89 billion in 2025, up 5.6 percent from a year earlier.

During Wednesday's meeting, Lai also thanked Canadian lawmakers for their support, citing a cross-party parliamentary motion countering what he described as China's distortion of United Nations General Assembly Resolution 2758, as well as efforts by Sgro and the House of Commons Standing Committee on International Trade to advance the TCFA.

Speaking after Lai, Sgro said Canada and Taiwan enjoy "a robust and growing relationship," citing cooperation in trade, investment, education, science, innovation, culture and tourism.

She said strong relationships are built "not only through formal agreements, but also through sustained dialogue, mutual respect, and personal connections."

However, the delegation leader made no specific mention of the TCFA in her remarks.

Sgro, who is visiting Taiwan for the sixth time, said the delegation aimed to deepen parliamentary dialogue and better understand the Indo-Pacific, a region she described as "increasingly important to Canada's future prosperity and security."

"Please know that Canada is a friend and a partner," she said, adding that "Canada will be standing next to Taiwan."

(By Sunny Lai)

Enditem/AW

title: Nigeria: NAFDAC Bursts Trade Fair Complex Den of Fake Energy Drinks, Wine, Whisky 'Manufacture'
summary: The National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control, NAFDAC, has uncovered a suspected counterfeit drinks production facility at Zamfara Plaza, BBA Trade Fair Complex, along the Badagry Expressway, Ojo, Lagos State. The Agency
content:
The National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control, NAFDAC, has uncovered a suspected counterfeit drinks production facility at Zamfara Plaza, BBA Trade Fair Complex, along the Badagry Expressway, Ojo, Lagos State.

The Agency arrested two suspects allegedly involved in the illegal operation.

The suspects, identified as Okafor and John, were arrested during an enforcement operation in a two-storey building where equipment and materials allegedly used to repackage and produce counterfeit alcoholic and energy drinks where discovered.

The raid, according to NAFDAC, followed credible intelligence and surveillance on suspected counterfeiters operating within the Trade Fair International Market.

Keep up with the latest headlines on [WhatsApp](https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VaIdDi8Bqbr263erhw1K "https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VaIdDi8Bqbr263erhw1K") | [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/company/allafrica/ "https://www.linkedin.com/company/allafrica/")

Speaking during the operation, the Assistant Director of the Investigation and Enforcement Directorate of NAFDAC, Mr Kunle Ojo, said the agency caught some of the suspects in the act and recovered drums, filters, packaging materials, a heating device and other equipment allegedly used in the illicit production process.

"Gentlemen of the press, as you can see today, when we came, we caught some red-handed producing all kinds of alcoholic drinks," Ojo said.

"What we have discovered today is a lot, and it's mind-boggling. We are here to protect the lives of many Nigerians."

Ojo said the agency intensified its enforcement activities ahead of the festive season, when demand for alcoholic and other beverages typically rises.

He warned that the circulation of counterfeit drinks posed a serious public health concern, urging suspected manufacturers to abandon the illegal trade.

"You are killing Nigerians in order to make money, which is not good," he said, appealing to those involved to stop the activities.

The NAFDAC official disclosed that the agency would investigate the source of the products, the raw materials used and the individuals allegedly financing or directing the operation.

"Where are they getting the products from? Where are they getting their raw materials? Who is employing them to do this kind of dangerous activity?"

He added that the agency would evacuate the recovered materials and products to its warehouse for further action, including destruction in accordance with applicable procedures.

"Those people that we have arrested today will be dealt with administratively and definitely will face the law," Ojo said.

Ojo also appealed to Nigerians to support the agency by providing credible information about suspected counterfeit production facilities.

"If you see something, say something," he said, assuring informants that their identities would be protected.

**Confession**

One of the arrested suspects, Okafor, who identified himself as a drinks dealer in the market, in an interview with Vanguard at the scene said: "I deal on drinks. I change the bottle of the drink. It's not that the bottle is not good. It's the drink in there, because the other one is already damaged. So that's why we are putting it to the next bottle," he said.

Also speaking during the operation, Mrs. Christiana Obiazikwor, Deputy Director, NAFDAC Public Relations, said the agency routinely carried out surveillance, seizures, arrests and destruction of unregistered and counterfeit products, despite public criticism that it was not doing enough to tackle the menace.

"NAFDAC is still at work. We are on the streets. We are in the markets. We are everywhere," she said.

Obiazikwor explained that enforcement teams often conducted operations without publicity to avoid alerting suspected offenders or triggering confrontations.

She said the agency decided to take journalists along on the latest operation to demonstrate its activities and reassure Nigerians that it remained committed to protecting public health.

"Most of the things they do, we don't publicise them so that we don't raise alarm," she said, adding that enforcement officers continued to visit suspected production and distribution points.

She urged members of the public to report suspected counterfeit production and distribution directly to NAFDAC rather than merely posting allegations on social media.

"There's no point going to social media to create fear. Report to NAFDAC and we'll do the needful."

Obiazikwor assured informants that the agency would protect their identities, urging Nigerians to provide credible information that could assist investigations.

Speaking, the Assistant Director, Head Public Relation, Investigation & Enforcement, Mrs. Victoria Jennifer Akudu, explained that the raid was part of the agency's routine efforts to uncover illegal manufacturing activities and protect consumers.

"Every day, our people are in the field. Our enforcement department, they are on the field trying to uncover this. And they do a lot," Akudu said.

She explained that the agency routinely confiscated products, carried out seizures and destroyed offending goods, adding that the latest operation was intended to demonstrate the work being done by enforcement officers.

"This is just a routine activity of our enforcement directorate," she said.

Akudu further disclosed that the suspected operators had allegedly moved from an earlier location after enforcement action, prompting officials to continue tracking their activities.

"We have confiscated and sealed off the place. They moved to another place. This time around, we passed through the back door. And that is how we are able to get them," she said.

She urged Nigerians to report suspected counterfeit products directly to NAFDAC rather than allow rumours and unverified claims to create unnecessary public fear.

Akudu assured the public that the agency remained committed to its responsibilities, stressing that its enforcement teams were continuing operations against suspected manufacturers and distributors of illegal products.

"I will ask Nigerians not to fear. We are alert and we are alive. We are doing our statutory function the way it should be," she said.

NAFDAC officials said the operation formed part of continuing efforts to remove counterfeit, adulterated and unregistered products from the Nigerian market.

The agency reiterated that consumers could be exposed to serious health risks when drinks were repackaged under the labels of established brands without proper quality controls or verification of their contents.

title: China’s Next Frontier: How Beijing Is Challenging Washington in Outer Space
zh_title: 中国的下一个前沿：北京如何在外太空挑战华盛顿
summary: 8月19日上午，中国航天事业跨越了一个重大门槛。中国航天公司蓝箭航天在中国西北部发射一枚火箭后不久，其助推器（将火箭推入轨道所需的部件）成功分离并返回地球。这是中国公司首次在陆地上回收火箭，六周前，中国首屈一指的国有航天承包商在南海进行了首次火箭回收。这些事件标志着中国可重复使用火箭发射的曙光——这种能力将释放巨大的潜力。
content:
8月19日上午，中国航天事业跨越了一个重大门槛。中国航天公司蓝箭航天在中国西北部发射一枚火箭后不久，其助推器（将火箭推入轨道所需的部件）成功分离并返回地球。这是中国公司首次在陆地上回收火箭，六周前，中国首屈一指的国有航天承包商在南海进行了首次火箭回收。这些事件标志着中国可重复使用火箭发射的曙光，这种能力将释放中国蓬勃发展的航天工业的巨大潜力。

华盛顿对这些事态发展的反应一直很冷淡。美国的发射次数和在轨卫星数量仍然是其他国家的两倍多。但中国正在迎头赶上。 2020年至2025年间，中国企业每年发射的火箭数量增加了一倍多，从39枚增加到92枚。中国实体已申请了数十万颗通信卫星的许可证，中国航天公司也在激增。其中许多，例如蓝箭空间，相对较新，但已经具有创新性。
这一进展具有经济和军事意义。中国公司可能很快就会与美国公司展开竞争，为全球大片地区提供卫星互联网等天基服务。与此同时，中国人民解放军将太空优势视为赢得未来战争的关键，正在开发一系列太空能力以及一套可以攻击卫星的武器。这对依赖太空进行通信、态势感知和导航以及进行精确打击和接收导弹警告的美军构成了严重风险。

中国作为太空强国的发展应该给美国敲响警钟。冷战结束后，华盛顿开始认为其在太空的主导地位是理所当然的。它再也无力这样做了。随着北京航天工业的进步，其成本优势将使美国公司的竞争变得更加困难，而中国的军事能力将增加太空成为未来冲突战场的风险。美国无懈可击的太空力量时代即将结束，华盛顿别无选择，只能适应。

### 爆炸！
中国的太空计划可以追溯到 20 世纪 50 年代，当时中国领导人毛泽东发起了中国人民解放军现代化和推动技术创新的努力。 1970年，中国发射了第一颗卫星，20世纪80年代，中国将空间技术研究列为国家重点。但中国太空计划的分水岭发生在 1990-91 年海湾战争期间，当时美军对天基资产的熟练运用使得规模相对较小但技术先进的联盟在短短几天内击败了伊拉克军队。卫星使美军能够在困难的沙漠地形中航行，为指挥官提供更快、更准确的战场信息，并使士兵能够在长距离内无缝协调。北京尚未意识到自己落后了多少，立即采取行动追赶。

在接下来的几年里，解放军的条令强调先进技术（尤其是卫星）对于战争的重要性日益增加。 2000年，中国军方开始开发自己的卫星导航服务，称为北斗，这样就不必依赖美国的运营

【原文 English Original】
On the morning of August 19, China’s space industry crossed a major threshold. Shortly after the Chinese aerospace company LandSpace launched a rocket in northwestern China, its booster—the part needed to thrust the rocket into orbit—successfully detached and landed back on earth. It was the first time a Chinese firm recovered a rocket on land, and it came six weeks after the country’s first-ever rocket recovery, carried out in the South China Sea by China’s premier state-owned space contractor. These events mark the dawn of China’s reusable rocket launch—a capability that will unlock enormous potential in the country’s booming space industry.

Washington’s response to these developments has been muted. The United States still conducts more than twice as many launches and has more satellites in orbit than any other country. But China is catching up. Between 2020 and 2025, the number of rockets launched annually by Chinese companies more than doubled, from 39 to 92. Chinese entities have applied for licenses for hundreds of thousands of communications satellites, and Chinese space companies are proliferating. Many of them, such as LandSpace, are relatively new but already innovative.

This progress has both economic and military implications. Chinese companies could soon compete with U.S. firms to provide vast swaths of the globe with space-based services such as satellite Internet. Meanwhile, the People’s Liberation Army (PLA), which sees space superiority as essential to winning future wars, is developing a range of space capabilities as well as a suite of weapons that can attack satellites. This poses a serious risk to the U.S. military, which depends on space for communications, situational awareness, and navigation, as well as for conducting precision strikes and receiving missile warnings.

China’s development as a space power should be a wake-up call for the United States. After the end of the Cold War, Washington began to take its dominance in space for granted. It can no longer afford to do so. As Beijing’s space industry advances, its cost advantages will make it much harder for U.S. companies to compete, and China’s military capabilities will increase the risk that space becomes a battlefield in future conflicts. The era of unassailable U.S. space power is ending, and Washington has no choice but to adapt.

### BLASTOFF!

China’s space program dates to the 1950s, when Chinese leader Mao Zedong initiated efforts to modernize the PLA and boost technological innovation. In 1970, China launched its first satellite, and in the 1980s, it made space technology research a national priority. But the watershed moment for China’s space program occurred during the 1990–91 Gulf War, when the U.S. military’s adept use of space-based assets allowed a relatively small but technologically advanced coalition to defeat Iraq’s army in just a few days. Satellites allowed U.S. forces to navigate difficult desert terrain, gave commanders information about the battlefield with greater speed and accuracy, and enabled soldiers to coordinate seamlessly across long distances. Beijing, which had not realized just how far behind it was, leaped into action to catch up.

In the years that followed, PLA doctrine emphasized the growing importance of advanced technology, especially satellites, for warfighting. In 2000, the Chinese military began developing its own satellite-powered navigation service, called BeiDou, so that it would not have to rely on U.S.-operated GPS. In 2015, the PLA created the Strategic Support Force, a now defunct organization that consolidated China’s space, cyber, and electronic warfare missions, with the aim of accelerating the country’s space progress. That same year, a Chinese government white paper identified outer space as a critical national security domain. China has since created spacecraft for communications; navigation; and intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance that would have been unimaginable to PLA officials who observed Desert Storm.

Encouraging commercial space activity has become one of China’s main tools for expanding its space program. In 2014, Beijing opened parts of the space sector to private investment, and more than 400 Chinese commercial space companies have since sprouted. Beijing and provincial governments have provided commercial space firms with financing through state-backed investment funds, subsidized factory upgrades and rocket launches, and given private companies access to government test facilities and technologies. In 2025, commercial space missions accounted for 54 percent of China’s national total, and commercial satellites made up 84 percent of Chinese spacecraft placed in orbit. China’s broad space-industrial ecosystem, composed of commercial companies, state-owned enterprises, research institutes, and universities, has allowed the country to eliminate its dependence on GPS and paved the way for the development of new domestic remote sensing and satellite communications companies.

In reusable rocket technology, the U.S. company SpaceX has enjoyed an enormous advantage, conducting five out of every six launches in the United States. But China’s two controlled recoveries of rocket boosters in July and August suggest that it could be a real competitor to the United States within a decade. Reusable rockets drive down the cost and increase the speed of space launches significantly; should China master the technology, it could develop large satellite constellations much more easily.

Reusable launches will also allow China to develop space-based Internet capabilities to compete with SpaceX’s dominant Starlink network, an extensive satellite Internet system with connectivity that rivals many land-based networks and which has been crucial for Ukraine in its defense against Russia. Although Chinese companies are still in the early stages of developing this technology, they are scaling fast. The entities operating the Guowang and Qianfan satellite constellations, which intend to compete with Starlink, plan to launch nearly 30,000 communications satellites over the next decade or so. These systems are currently much smaller than Starlink, which has more than 11,000 satellites in orbit, but they could eventually become legitimate alternatives. Qianfan already has trial agreements with Brazil, Kazakhstan, Malaysia, and Turkey for the use of its satellite network.

### ROCKET SCIENCE

China’s commercial space development has gone hand in hand with a growing ability to use space to support its military modernization. Beijing has spent decades studying the U.S. military’s use of satellites, and it is now developing its own national security–related space capabilities. According to the Pentagon, China operates more than 500 satellites that can conduct intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance missions, in addition to its satellite-enabled positioning system, allowing the PLA to locate and track U.S. and allied forces around the world. PLA strategists have identified Defense Department space assets as valuable targets because the U.S. military depends on them for nearly every step of what it calls the “kill chain”: finding, aiming at, and striking targets, and then assessing the results.

To exploit U.S. dependence on satellites, Beijing is investing in antisatellite weapons. Since 2007, when it conducted its first successful test of an antisatellite missile, China has developed other tools, including electronic warfare and directed-energy weapons, which can interfere with satellite signals or damage sensors without physically destroying satellites. Chinese spacecraft can also execute increasingly sophisticated maneuvers: in 2022, a Chinese satellite called Shijian-21 attached itself to a defunct Chinese satellite and moved it into a different orbit. Such an action could be benign—it could be used to repair and refuel satellites or remove debris—but it could also enable Chinese platforms to manipulate other spacecraft, including U.S. military satellites. Beijing’s ability to take down U.S. satellites could pose an especially serious challenge for the U.S. military in East Asia, where, in the case of conflict, China would be much less dependent on space-based assets than the United States.

China’s space rise is already influencing broader international security dynamics. During Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine, in 2022, Chinese firms provided satellite imagery of the battlefield that helped Russian forces conduct military operations. Throughout the war in Iran, Chinese entities have also supplied Tehran with satellite imagery, including images of a base in Jordan that Iran struck in July, resulting in the deaths of three American service members. As China’s commercial space sector expands, so could these relationships, giving more countries and nonstate actors without advanced space programs access to their benefits. Such expanded access could be used during natural disasters or other emergencies to save lives. But it could also provide adversaries with the ability to more effectively target U.S. and allied forces across the globe.

### MISSION CRITICAL

As China’s space power grows, Washington has moved to protect some of its satellite networks. The U.S. Space Force has diversified the placement of some of its most sensitive assets and increased procurement of new satellites. Such investments are useful but insufficient to address the United States’ vulnerabilities. Given the capabilities that China already has or will develop soon, there are now many possible scenarios in which the U.S. military would have to operate when satellite communications are denied or degraded, GPS signals are jammed, and intelligence from orbit is restricted.

The U.S. military should invest in nascent technologies, such as inertial navigation systems and quantum sensors, which could one day help its forces move with precision without GPS. It should also invest in emerging alternatives to satellites, such as high-altitude relays, which include drones or balloons that operate closer to Earth and can link communications networks; laser-enabled communications, which use light to transmit information and are difficult to disrupt; and mesh networks, which automatically reroute signals around nodes that have been destroyed, making communications more resilient. Mechanisms for delegating decision-making will be even more essential than in the past, as the danger of disconnection increases.

Washington should also increase its efforts to foster a more competitive domestic launch industry. The United States leads the world in space launches largely because of SpaceX. Although the company is an enormous asset, its near monopoly is a risk. If technical failures or damage to launch infrastructure were to interrupt SpaceX’s operations, the United States’ ability to launch satellites would be severely curtailed. This year, SpaceX announced plans to retire the Falcon 9, its main reusable rocket. The Falcon 9 will eventually be replaced by Starship, a new high-capacity rocket that will carry more satellites into orbit with each launch. But the beginning of the phase-out has already created a launch shortage that threatens the continued development of the U.S. space economy. To mitigate this risk, Washington should continue awarding government contracts to more companies.

> SpaceX is an enormous asset to the United States, but its near monopoly is a risk.

title: Japan Wants to Sell Air Defense, Maritime Surveillance Systems to Philippine Forces - USNI News
zh_title: 日本希望向菲律宾军队出售防空和海上监视系统 - USNI新闻
summary: 日本陆上自卫队的03型中程地对空导弹。日本陆上自卫队照片菲律宾马尼拉——日本希望向菲律宾出售防空、海上监视和反无人机系统，以加强其在南海和吕宋海峡的军事力量。周三，在日本自卫队成立 72 周年纪念日期间，拟议的中短程防空系统销售计划得到了强调。该提案代表了东京对马尼拉长期安全援助的新阶段，并且是在两国加强防务关系之后进行的。
content:
日本陆上自卫队的03型中程地对空导弹。日本陆上自卫队照片

菲律宾马尼拉——日本希望向菲律宾出售防空、海上监视和反无人机系统，以加强其在南海和吕宋海峡的军事力量。

周三，在日本自卫队成立 72 周年纪念日期间，拟议的中短程防空系统销售计划得到了强调。该提案代表了东京对马尼拉长期安全援助的新阶段，也是两国通过最近的联合训练和后勤协议加强防务关系之后的结果。

在成立周年纪念活动中，日本三菱电机公司和东芝公司展示了他们的防空系统。其中包括03型中程地对空导弹、11型近程防空系统和91型单兵便携式防空系统。日本自卫队正在积极使用所有这些系统。
菲律宾武装部队正在寻求为其下一个现代化计划采购数十套地对空导弹系统，以满足菲律宾空军、陆军和海军陆战队的防空需求。日本国防工业代表告诉 USNI 新闻，[最近修订的国防出口指南](https://www.trade.gov/market-intelligence/japan-defense-export-policy) 使得向菲律宾出售和转让这些日本制造的防空系统成为可能。

日本军事分析家稻叶义博告诉美国海军学院新闻网：“这些系统共同可以保护城市地区、关键基础设施和军事设施。通过整合这些系统，日本可以建立一个分层的防空网络，能够在多个层面上反击中国的空中攻击。”

2026 年 10 月 14 日，在日本自卫队成立 72 周年纪念活动期间，日本三菱电机公司和东芝公司展示了他们的防空系统。菲律宾国防部照片

稻叶表示，虽然东京正在扩大其国内导弹生产能力，但目前的扩张努力旨在加强日本自卫队的远程打击计划，可能不足以满足出口需求。
“扩大的导弹产能可能仍不足以满足出口需求。尽管如此，即使在向日本自卫队的导弹交付完成后，出口对于维持扩大的生产基地也至关重要，”稻叶说。

马尼拉尚未建立能够保护其广阔领空或拦截弹道导弹威胁的防空网络。菲律宾的主要对手中国部署了大量巡航导弹、弹道导弹和高超音速导弹，可以从各种地面、海军和空中平台向菲律宾基地发射。

除了防空提案外，日本公司还展示了天基和沿海雷达海上监视系统。其中一次演示中，日本卫星星座正在监测黄岩岛，这是一个[有争议的南海海洋地物](https://news.usni.org/2026/09/11/combat-patrol-scarborough-shoal)，也是菲律宾和中国之间各种对峙和冲突的发生地。展示了从固定站点到移动雷达的各种海上监视雷达，其中包括一种可以跟踪最远 75 海里目标的系统。

【原文 English Original】
Japan Ground Self-Defense Force’s Type 03 medium-range surface-to-air missile. JGSDF photo

MANILA, Philippines — Japan wants to sell air defense, maritime surveillance and counter-drone systems to the Philippines amid its push to bolster forces in the South China Sea and Luzon Strait.

The proposed sale of medium and short-range air defense systems was highlighted Wednesday on the sidelines of the 72nd founding anniversary of the Japan Self-Defense Force. The proposal represents a new phase in Tokyo’s longstanding security assistance to Manila and follows enhanced defense ties between the two countries through recent joint training and logistics agreements.

During the founding anniversary event, Japanese firms Mitsubishi Electric Corporation and Toshiba showcased their air defense systems. These included the Type 03 medium-range surface-to-air missile, Type 11 short-range air defense system and Type 91 man portable air defense system. All of these systems are in active use by the JSDF.

The Armed Forces of the Philippines is looking to procure dozens of batteries of surface-to-air missile systems for Philippine Air Force, Army and Marine Corps air defense requirements under its next modernization program. [Recently revised defense export guidelines](https://www.trade.gov/market-intelligence/japan-defense-export-policy) have made the sale and transfer of these Japanese-made air defense systems to the Philippines possible, a Japanese defense industry representative told USNI News.

“Together, these systems can protect urban areas, critical infrastructure and military installations. By integrating these systems, Japan can establish a layered air defense network capable of countering Chinese aerial attacks at multiple levels,” Yoshihiro Inaba, a Japanese military analyst, told USNI News.

Japanese firms Mitsubishi Electric Corporation and Toshiba showcased their air defense systems Oct. 14, 2026, on the sidelines of the 72nd founding anniversary of the Japan Self-Defense Force. Philippines Department of National Defense photo

While Tokyo is expanding its domestic missile production capabilities, the current expansion effort is aimed at strengthening the JSDF’s long-range strike plans and may prove inadequate for export demands, Inaba said.

“The expanded missile production capacity may still be insufficient to meet export demand. Nevertheless, exports will be essential to maintaining the expanded production base even after deliveries of missiles to the JSDF have been completed,” said Inaba.

Manila has yet to operate an air defense network capable of protecting its vast air space or intercepting ballistic missile threats. China, the Philippines primary adversary, fields a vast array of cruise, ballistic and hypersonic missiles that can be launched against Philippine bases from a variety of ground, naval and air platforms.

Alongside the air defense proposals, Japanese firms presented space-based and coastal radar maritime surveillance systems. One of these presentations saw a Japanese satellite constellation monitoring Scarborough Shoal, a [contested South China Sea maritime feature](https://news.usni.org/2026/09/11/combat-patrol-scarborough-shoal) that is the site of various standoffs and clashes between the Philippines and China. Various maritime surveillance radars ranging from fixed sites to mobile radars were showcased, including one system that could track targets up to 75 nautical miles away.

Since the 2010s, Japan has funded 17 Coast Guard cutters and sold four air surveillance radars to the Philippine Air Force. In 2023, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs launched the [Official Security Assistance program.](https://news.usni.org/2023/11/09/japan-grants-security-assistance-to-the-philippines-looks-to-enhance-military-cooperation) Under this program, the Philippines has received maritime patrol infrastructure, radar maintenance support and coastal surveillance systems. The Philippines and Japan are also [engaged in talks](https://news.usni.org/2026/06/03/philippines-progresses-japanese-destroyer-transfer-talks-receives-american-cutter-at-shangri-la) regarding the transfer of five Japan Maritime Self-Defense Force Abukuma-class destroyers. The transfer is set to occur within the next two to three years.

Beyond the potential for air defense transfers, Inaba said he expects future security assistance to the Philippines to include unmanned systems and transport vessels.

Last month, Japan launched the first of a series of British-designed high speed landing craft. Tokyo wants to use these vessels for the rapid insertion of troops and supplies across its Ryukus island chain, which covers a strategic strait near Taiwan.

“Such landing craft would be essential for transporting troops and supplies in support of the defense of the South China Sea,” said Inaba.

title: Underground railway set to reshape old Tainan, revive historic station - Focus Taiwan
zh_title: 地下铁路将重塑旧台南，复兴历史车站 - 聚焦台湾
summary: 中新社台南10月15日电 台南台南地下列车将于周六开始运行，标志着台南城市景观重塑迈出了重要一步，也为台南百年火车站作为了解当地历史文化的门户开辟了新的可能性。几代人以来，这条铁路一直是贯穿台湾最古老城市台南的重要南北交通走廊。但其轨道、平交路口、地下通道和立交桥也将城市分割开来，使得东部和西部地区之间的交通更加困难。据工信部称
content:
中新社台南10月15日电 台南台南地下列车将于周六开始运行，标志着台南城市景观重塑迈出了重要一步，也为台南百年火车站作为了解当地历史文化的门户开辟了新的可能性。

几代人以来，这条铁路一直是贯穿台湾最古老城市台南的重要南北交通走廊。但其轨道、平交路口、地下通道和立交桥也将城市分割开来，使得东部和西部地区之间的交通更加困难。

据交通部称，全长8.23公里的地下路段将取消23个铁路道口及相关建筑物，改善行人和骑自行车者的通行，同时缓解交通瓶颈。

该项目于2009年9月获得内阁批准，由铁路局牵头，历时约17年才实现第一阶段通车。据该局称，在此期间，成本从预计的 330 亿新台币增加到 412.6 亿新台币（13 亿美元），整个项目目前计划于 2031 年 3 月完工。

转型将不仅仅限于交通运输。交通部表示，一旦现有轨道被拆除，计划将原来的铁路走廊变成一条约30米宽的绿道，并设有步行道、自行车道和景观区，连接新车站、社区、学校和公共设施。
## 历史车站的新角色

国立成功大学建筑学荣休教授、车站修复和再利用计划审查委员会成员傅朝卿表示，该项目还提供了一个重新思考台南车站角色的机会，台南车站是该市最知名的地标之一。

该车站的历史建筑于 1936 年重建，并于 1998 年被指定为国家纪念碑。该车站于 1900 年日本殖民统治期间（1895-1945 年）首次开放。它将保留在新地铁站旁边，而不是被新地铁站取代。

傅说，车站与台南的城市布局紧密相关。它面向车站环岛和历史悠久的市中心的位置决定了人们进入和游览城市的方式。

铁路规划者最初考虑在更北的地方建造一个新车站，将历史建筑抛在后面，傅反对这一提议，因为这可能会切断车站与市中心的长期关系。

采用的设计将新车站置于地下并毗邻历史建筑，使两者共存。其低矮的水平轮廓和宽阔的天篷使旧车站在视觉上更加突出，而下沉的广场和连接的走道将两个设施连接起来。
台铁表示，旧车站还可以发挥更重要的文化和商业作用，并补充说，正在讨论的计划包括咖啡馆、便餐选择、当地纪念品、阅读空间和展览。

## 连接交通和遗产

成大城市规划系特聘教授陈彦仲表示，铁路迁入地下也为保留和诠释车站周围的历史风貌提供了机会。

台南已有400多年的历史，曾是台湾的省会，保留了历史悠久的铁路设施和车站周围的其他历史遗迹，包括站台、转盘、仓库和车站等。

【原文 English Original】
Tainan, Oct. 15 (CNA) Trains are set to begin running underground in Tainan on Saturday, marking a major step in reshaping the southern Taiwan city's urban landscape and opening up new possibilities for its century-old railway station to serve as a gateway to local history and culture.

For generations, the railway has served as a vital north-south transportation corridor through Tainan, Taiwan's oldest city. But its tracks, level crossings, underpasses and overpasses have also divided the city, making travel between its eastern and western districts more difficult.

According to the Ministry of Transportation and Communications (MOTC), the 8.23-kilometer underground section will eliminate 23 railway crossings and related structures, improving access for pedestrians and cyclists while easing traffic bottlenecks.

Approved by the Cabinet in September 2009 and led by the Railway Bureau, the project will have taken about 17 years to reach its first-stage opening. In that period the cost rose from a projected NT$33 billion to NT$41.26 billion (US$1.3 billion), with the full project now scheduled for completion in March 2031, according to the bureau.

The transformation will extend beyond transportation. Once the existing tracks are removed, there are plans to turn the former railway corridor into a greenway about 30 meters wide, with walking and cycling paths and landscaped areas linking new stations, neighborhoods, schools and public facilities, the MOTC said.

## A new role for a historic station

The project also offers an opportunity to rethink the role of Tainan Station, one of the city's most recognizable landmarks, said Fu Chao-ching (傅朝卿), an emeritus professor of architecture at National Cheng Kung University (NCKU) and a member of the review committee for the station's restoration and reuse plan.

First opened in 1900 during Japanese colonial rule (1895-1945), the station's historic building was rebuilt in 1936 and designated a national monument in 1998. It will remain in place alongside the new underground station rather than be replaced by it.

Fu said the station is closely tied to Tainan's urban layout. Its position facing the station roundabout and the historic city center has shaped how people enter and navigate the city.

Railway planners initially considered building a new station further north, leaving the historic building behind, a proposal Fu opposed because it risked severing the station's long-standing relationship with the city center.

The adopted design instead places the new station underground and next to the historic building, allowing the two to coexist. Its low, horizontal profile and broad canopy give visual prominence to the old station, while a sunken plaza and connecting walkways link the two facilities.

The old station could also take on a more prominent cultural and commercial role, Taiwan Railway Corp. said, adding that plans under discussion include cafes, light meals options, local souvenirs, reading spaces and exhibitions.

## Connecting transport and heritage

The railway's relocation underground also presents an opportunity to preserve and interpret the historic features around the station, said Chen Yen-chung (陳彥仲), a distinguished professor in NCKU's Department of Urban Planning.

With a history of more than 400 years, Tainan was once the capital of Taiwan and retains historic railway facilities and other remnants of the past around the station, including platforms, a turntable, warehouses and sections of the old city wall.

Chen said future development should balance preservation with new uses, allowing the station to serve as a starting point for understanding Tainan's history and culture.

He said rather than simply passing through the station to transfer to other forms of transportation, visitors could encounter the city's past there before continuing to historic areas such as the old city center and Anping.

"Restrictions should not be seen as limitations. They can instead become opportunities to create a distinctive urban character," Chen said.

The project has also revealed traces of Tainan's earlier history beneath the modern city. According to the city's Cultural Affairs Bureau, construction teams uncovered 20 archaeological sites containing remains dating from prehistoric times to the Qing dynasty and Japanese colonial period.

The discoveries directly impacted the project's construction schedule, with archaeological investigations and preservation work adding about two years to the original timetable, the Railway Bureau said.

According to the Tainan City government, there were also design changes to preserve archaeological remains, either by relocating them for safekeeping or reinforcing them in place.

However, the transformation will take time. After trains begin running underground, the existing tracks and structures still need to be removed, roads restored and pedestrian facilities improved before the full benefits can be realized.

Two additional underground commuter stations, Linsen and South Tainan, are scheduled to open in 2029 and 2030, respectively.

The longer-term challenge will be to ensure that the land freed up by the project becomes useful public space, encourages renewal along the corridor and helps reconnect communities, Chen said.

For Tainan, the railway's move underground could ultimately reshape more than the city's transport network. Whether the former railway corridor becomes a meaningful public space, and whether the historic station can draw visitors into the city's wider cultural landscape, will help determine how far the project succeeds in reconnecting Tainan with its past as well as its future.

(By Chiu Chu-yin, Chang Jung-hsiang, Huang Chiao-wen and Lee Hsin-Yin)

title: “Secure and controllable”: How Beijing is writing Europe out of its systems
summary: In June 2025, a Chinese state-owned utility put out a tender covering the replacement of the control systems for 67 wind turbines at the Kangbao wind farm in Hebei. The turbines were not broken or outdated. The problem was their controllers
content:
In June 2025, a Chinese state-owned utility put out a tender covering the replacement of the control systems for 67 wind turbines at the Kangbao wind farm in Hebei. The turbines were not broken or outdated. The problem was their controllers, which were imported from Europe. The tender warned not only of high costs and long procurement cycles, but also of a risk of being “controlled by foreign forces”. The prescribed solution was replacement with domestically produced technology.

The Kangbao case is not unusual. A [new study](https://www.osw.waw.pl/designed-out/) by the Centre for Eastern Studies (OSW) of the Chinese wind sector analysed more than 1,600 publicly available procurement documents and found nearly 300 calling for foreign equipment to be replaced. European manufacturers and component suppliers are among those named in the notices as risks to be removed.

The analysis shows that Beijing’s drive to make its energy infrastructure “self-reliant, safe and controllable” is security-focused and discriminates against foreign suppliers, including European ones. And while European suppliers are written out of Chinese critical energy infrastructure, Chinese companies push for expansion in Europe.

It is widely known that China’s leadership under Xi Jinping strives for China to be less reliant on technology imports, especially in critical infrastructure. OSW’s findings describe how this is being done and how European firms are affected. They show a coordinated effort, more than a decade in the making, to identify foreign technological dependencies that could become vulnerabilities, build domestic alternatives and gradually remove the foreign technology itself.

The findings should reassure Europeans already moving towards a more restrictive approach. Reciprocity used to mean asking Beijing to open its market, follow rules and stop discriminating. This notion no longer fits the reality. Europeans need to re-evaluate their understanding of security in critical infrastructure, and to shift what they mean by “reciprocity”: not waiting for China to match Europe’s openness, but matching China’s protective measures.

## China’s path to technological self-reliance and control

The OSW research shows that as early as 2012 Chinese State Council documents warned that core information technologies depended on other countries. The 2015 National Security Law made the development of “self-reliant and controllable” critical technologies a national-security objective. In 2016, Xi Jinping described having core technologies controlled by others as China’s “greatest hidden danger”.

What followed was a three-stage process: creating alternatives, ensuring demand and replacing vulnerabilities. The 14th Five-Year Plan called for manufacturing to become “self-reliant and controllable, safe and efficient”. The 15th Five-Year Plan extended this into industrial-control software, precision bearings, motors, control systems and energy equipment—all areas where European companies retain important capabilities.

At the same time, Beijing has understood that diversification away from non-Chinese inputs could not just be ordered. Someone had to buy the alternatives to ensure the investments were worthwhile. Regulation securing that demand followed: operators were required to prioritise “secure and trustworthy” products; acceptable technologies for electricity systems were set out in official whitelists; and state-owned enterprises were obliged to support indigenous technological innovation.

The last stage is across-the-board substitution, and the OSW study shows the concrete manifestation of this in the energy sector. Since 2022, major state-owned energy utilities have translated the policy approach into their own procurement requirements. Their objections to imported systems are partly practical—poor reliability, slow spare-part delivery—and partly political: not “secure and controllable” and vulnerable to control by “foreign forces”.

In the wind sector, the campaign focuses on systems used to operate and control power assets. The technologies being targeted point to perceived risks of remote disruption and loss of control over power generation stemming from foreign presence in software, databases and other connected elements of critical infrastructure.

## Use China’s risk map to identify Europe’s vulnerabilities

The EU should treat China’s localisation agenda as a guide to how Beijing assesses strategic risk. China does not seek to localise every technology at once. Instead, it sets short- and long-term localisation objectives, and concentrates resources on selected capabilities and parts of the technological stack. Those choices therefore offer a window into which dependencies Beijing considers most dangerous. It is a playbook from which the EU can take inspiration as it weighs its [own trade-offs](https://ecfr.eu/publication/trust-and-trade-offs-how-to-manage-europes-green-technology-dependence-on-china/?amp)—which dependencies are worth the cost of removing and which are not.

The useful lesson is in the prioritisation: where Beijing is prepared to accept foreign dependence, where it seeks to reduce it and where it is willing to spend heavily to eliminate it. The Chinese leadership’s focus on the threat of remote disruption and loss of control to foreign actors over power generation points, in reverse, at the strategic vulnerability that Chinese technologies with remote access create in Europe.

When Beijing judges a technology sensitive enough to demand domestic control, European authorities should ask themselves what vulnerability it is seeking to close and whether Europe faces an equivalent exposure through Chinese suppliers. Europe should pay as much attention to what Chinese companies are eliminating from their own critical systems as to what Beijing wants to sell abroad.

## Decide on high-risk suppliers at EU level

Designating high-risk suppliers and third countries, and imposing mitigation measures, should sit at the EU level. Information and communications technology (ICT) risks cross national borders. In energy, disruption to grid infrastructure or generation assets can have cascading effects beyond the country where it originates, as the [2025 Iberian blackout](https://ecfr.eu/article/a-brighter-future-why-upgrading-the-grid-is-vital-for-europes-competitiveness/?amp) demonstrated. EU-level mitigation measures close the loophole that fragmented implementation creates: a supplier judged to pose an unacceptable security risk in one member state must not be able to simply shift its business to another.

EU-level designations also take the political pressure off individual member states. The [5G Toolbox](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/library/eu-toolbox-5g-security), the European Commission’s non-binding framework for mitigating cyber-security risks in telecommunications infrastructure, is the lesson in what happens otherwise. Five years after its adoption, only [13 of the EU’s 27 member states](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:52026SC0156) had imposed restrictions on high-risk suppliers, though 22 had the legal powers to do so. Parts of Europe’s 5G infrastructure remain dependent on high-risk vendors, with Germany the most prominent example. Eight years after the debate about these vulnerabilities started, about [60%](https://www.lightreading.com/6g/huawei-5g-deal-defended-by-deutsche-telekom-boss-as-6g-ban-looms) of its radio access network is still provided by Chinese vendors. The share of European vendors present in China’s critical advanced communication systems has since fallen to [less than 3%](https://www.techtimes.com/articles/324592/20260815/nokia-closes-china-rd-hub-5g-world-splits-rival-supply-chains.htm).

## Radically rethink reciprocity

> **“**Beijing criticises the revised Cybersecurity Act as unfairly targeting Chinese companies, while its own procurement notices explicitly name European companies as supply-chain risks to be removed from critical infrastructure.”

Beijing’s [complaints](https://ec.europa.eu/info/law/better-regulation/have-your-say/initiatives/14578-The-EU-Cybersecurity-Act/F33393498_en) about Europe’s risk mitigation actions should be met with a plain and pragmatic observation: China does the same, more extensively and less transparently. Beijing [criticises](https://www.chinadaily.com.cn/a/202604/20/WS69e619c4a310d6866eb44785.html) the revised Cybersecurity Act as unfairly targeting Chinese companies, while its own procurement notices explicitly name European companies as supply-chain risks to be removed from critical infrastructure. Its grounds go well beyond technical faults or security incidents: a supplier’s foreign origin is itself disqualifying under a top-down localisation drive.

Under the revised Cybersecurity Act, whether a third country itself excludes EU-origin products from critical infrastructure should be considered when the EU assesses non-technical cyber risks. The EU should stress its own “[legitimate right](https://english.mofcom.gov.cn/News/SpokesmansRemarks/art/2026/art_6ba67ba24946452099098f1c83e3f408.html)”, in Beijing’s own phrase, to protect critical infrastructure, and use the evidence of China’s localisation drive to address asymmetric procurement conditions through the [International Procurement Instrument](https://ecfr.eu/publication/brussels-holdem-european-cards-against-trumpian-coercion/?amp). Trust cannot be a one-way street. Chinese companies should not compete freely for EU public contracts while European firms face systematic exclusion or replacement in China.

Europe is facing a less integrated world: supply chains are already concentrated in a few places, while global technology and energy systems are fragmenting. Openness itself is no longer a virtue, but increasingly a vulnerability. Those trends are not going to reverse any time soon. By eliminating European exposure in its own energy infrastructure, the Chinese leadership has set the tone. It is on Europe to take the message.

_The European Council on Foreign Relations does not take collective positions. ECFR publications only represent the views of their individual authors._

# Hang Seng Index falls below 24,000 as tech shares weigh

Hong Kong shares fell sharply by noon on 15 October, with the Hang Seng Index dropping 1.47 per cent to 23,955 points. The decline was led by tech shares, as the Hang Seng Tech Index slid 2.94 per cent and mainland indices also fell.

[![Image 4: Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)

 By [Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk), Editor in Chief

 15 Oct 2026 at 12:08 HKT · 1 min read
