Hong Kong shares saw losses widen by the midday break on Thursday, weighed down by tech shares. The benchmark Hang Seng Index dropped 358 points, or 1.47 per cent, to 23,955 points by noon, according to The Standard.

The half-day market turnover was HK$113.7 billion. The Hang Seng Tech Index slid 2.94 per cent to 4,051 points at noon, underscoring the drag from technology stocks.

In the mainland, the Shanghai Stock Exchange Composite Index decreased 1.98 per cent to 3,692 points, and the Shenzhen Stock Exchange Component Index declined 2.78 per cent to 11,773 points.

# Taiwan shares plunge over 1,500 points Thursday morning

10/15/2026 11:22 AM

CNA photo Oct. 15, 2026

Taipei, Oct. 15 (CNA) Shares in Taiwan tumbled more than 1,500 points at one point Thursday morning, as heavy losses on other major Asian markets and Wall Street triggered a sell-off amid renewed inflation concerns, dealers said.

As of 11:14 a.m., the Taiex, the Taiwan Stock Exchange's benchmark index, had dropped 1,612.82 points, or 3.32 percent, to 47,013.01, dealers said.

The plunge was led by large-cap technology stocks after higher-than-expected U.S. inflation data led investors to anticipate a more hawkish monetary policy from the U.S. Federal Reserve, dealers said.

On Wednesday, the U.S. consumer price index (CPI) data for September showed that inflation rose 3.7 percent, higher than the market forecast of 3.6 percent, fueling expectations of a Fed rate hike, dealers said.

Following the release of the CPI data, sell-off occurred on U.S. markets Wednesday, and Asian markets followed suit Thursday morning, with tech stocks in focus, as concerns mounted that AI-related developers would face higher financing costs if interest rates continued to rise, dealers said.

In Taipei, the electronics index had fallen 3.63 percent as of 11:14 a.m., pulling the Taiex sharply lower.

Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. (TSMC), which accounts for more than 40 percent of the market's total capitalization, was down 2.01 percent at NT$2,440.00 (US$75.54).

Memory chip supplier Nanya Technology Corp. plunged 9.16 percent to NT$436.50, while smartphone IC designer MediaTek Inc. dropped 5.92 percent to NT$4,210.00.

Among other tech stocks, iPhone assembler and AI server maker Hon Hai Precision Industry Co. was down 1.85 percent at NT$238.50, while power-management solutions provider Delta Electronics Inc. fell 8.40 percent to NT$1,635.00.

(By Pan Chih-yi and Frances Huang)

title: A true story of how China took off--now almost completely forgotten and ignored
summary: In my 2026 book, Statism with Chinese Characteristics, I compare the era since 1978 to a treadmill—more actions than progress on meaningful, substantive reforms. In particular, I identified a pivotal change in the early to mid-1990s that cr
content:
In my 2026 book, Statism with Chinese Characteristics, I compare the era since 1978 to a treadmill—more actions than progress on meaningful, substantive reforms. In particular, I identified a pivotal change in the early to mid-1990s that created this dynamic.

The following is part 2 of an excerpt of my book published on the website of Cambridge University Press at https://doi.org/10.1017/9781009680646.002.

**1.2 What Can We Learn from China’s Takeoff?**

Getting details right yields right lessons about China’s takeoff and its subsequent experiences. This is a book of factual details, not of novel perspectives, and I approached the subject matter like a historian. Sadly, it is not fashionable to be a historian on the Chinese economy compared with being an armchair theorist. There was a time when economists theorized TVEs as a bulwark against the “private pillaging of public assets” even though the true underlying ownership of TVEs was private in the first place. Statist financial controls were justified on the ground of information asymmetry and broader public welfare functions of the state even though the period of steepest poverty reduction occurred during an era of financial liberalization.

I draw four lessons from the facts and data that I have reviewed. One is that the baseline effect is huge and we need to get it right. Second, what I call “directional liberalism” contributed to the incentive effect of Chinese entrepreneurs. The third is that politics and economics are complements rather than substitutes. The fourth is that rural China makes, and it can break, China.

These are not the lessons the Chinese leaders since 1989 have drawn. They believe, with rising vigor of conviction, that the power of the state in building infrastructure, scaling technology, and developing cities created China’s miracle. I believe that this view gets China wrong, and it has led to many of the ills of the Chinese economy, such as its macro imbalances, overcapacity, slowing personal income growth relative to GDP growth, poor productivity performance, and a gaping hole in the human capital of rural China.

**1.2.1** Incentives and Baseline Effects

Economist Steven Radelet had a memorable quip about China’s rapid turnaround. “In 1976,” he said, “Mao single-handedly and dramatically changed the direction of global poverty with one simple act: he died.”[7](https://www.cambridge.org/core/product/identifier/9781009680646%23bp7/type/BOOK_PART#fn20)

This is true. His death set off reforms that launched China’s economic takeoff. But there is another side of the story. Mao also made a lasting contribution to poverty alleviation while he was alive. His disastrous policies had kept so many people poor. About two-thirds of the poverty reductions China achieved in the 1980s was attributable to the correction of Mao’s economic mismanagement (Ravallion [Reference Ravallion2021](https://www.cambridge.org/core/product/identifier/9781009680646%23rl1/type/BOOK_PART#r248)). In 1976, the level of poverty was incredibly high relative to China’s economic potentials. Given that gap, reasonable and common-sensical policies produced immediate and sizable gains and progress.

China lifted so many people above poverty because there were so many poor people in the first place. This is a baseline effect. We should use more of this baseline thinking in our analysis of Chinese reforms. What was the political baseline in 1978? How did that political baseline affect the psychology of China’s would-be entrepreneurs? We do not have data but the following conjecture is eminently plausible: A would-be Chinese entrepreneur in 1978 did not view and assess her political world from the perspective of a Westministerian system of checks and balances. She compared China in 1978 with China in 1976. Once we get this basic scenario straight, so much of the “surprise” about why Chinese entrepreneurship boomed without Western institutions is superfluous. The absence of Western institutions is irrelevant to our inquiry because it was irrelevant to the cognitive horizon of our entrepreneur in question.

Her political baseline was the Cultural Revolution from 1966 to 1976, the totalitarian world of Mao Zedong. Now we ask, “Did the Chinese political system circa 1978, as arbitrary and as absent of the rule of law compared to a Westministerian system, mark a substantial _marginal_ change from the Cultural Revolution?” The answer is a resounding “yes,” and that is the answer that mattered to her perceptions of risks and rewards of going into business.

The Cultural Revolution was a tough period for private businesses, to put it mildly. The ideology was antagonistic toward capitalism. Private businesses were strictly forbidden and in urban China all vestiges of capitalism – known at the time as “the tail of capitalism” – were wiped out. (There was some leeway in rural China, an important point to which I will return later.) Anyone who went into private business faced instantaneous risks of being arrested and of being persecuted.

Now imagine a change from being imprisoned instantaneously to a situation in which imprisonment was no longer instantaneous. Economists often tout security of property as a precondition for economic growth, but security of property presupposes security of the person holding the property, the proprietor. We often gloss over this distinction between the security of the proprietor and the security of the property itself. China did not then, or ever, have a strong protection of property rights but soon after the Cultural Revolution China moved quickly toward establishing security of the proprietor. One would think not getting arrested has an impact on incentives.

If we do not get the baseline right, we also cannot correctly calibrate the impact arising from the departures from the baseline. Two explanatory camps of Chinese growth do not sufficiently take into account that baseline. One holds that China took off because the policy changes were modest. This is the premise of the gradualist school. You start the reform slowly by taking small, incremental steps and then initial successes feed back into the policy process to produce another round of reforms. Modesty is a virtue.

Another theory holds that the Western model of economic growth is all wrong, with its fixation on rights and the rule of law. Look at China. It is an antithesis to democracy, and it thrived without the rule of law. It must be the case, this theory deduces, that China has figured out a unique “playbook,” the one rooted in China’s own tradition, culture, and institutions.

Both ideas ignore the baseline of China in the late 1970s. Modesty is in the eye of a beholder. A reallocation of profit retentions, an approach used to contract out farmland, may appear modest to us in an ivory tower, but against the backdrop of extreme antagonism toward capitalism this change was nothing short of radical. The “modesty” view is glaringly incongruous with the tale of eighteen households in Xiaogang village writing their pledge in blood. Also, the method required some remnants of capitalistic practices, which only existed in the countryside, and signals that policy and political changes were here to say.

The idea that Chinese boom violated the basic cannons of economics would have us believe that in 1978 a would-be Chinese entrepreneur contemplating to go into business was flipping through the pages of the American constitution and asking agonizingly, “Do I have Western property rights security?” That is just not a realistic representation of that entrepreneur’s frame of mind. Her likely question was, “Do I have more personal security in 1978 than in 1976?” The answer is yes because she, as a proprietor, became more secure. It was that directional change that explains China’s entrepreneurial response. While Polity IV may lump them close to each other, to the hundreds of millions of the Chinese, there was a world of difference between Mao Zedong and Deng Xiaoping.

**1.2.2** Directionally Liberal Model

Entrepreneurship boomed at a time when China lacked even a hint of constitutional democracy, a phenomenon that has produced a cottage industry of books and articles all eagerly pontificating how growth can happen under – or is even facilitated by – an autocratic system.

This is the China Model in its most essential elements. It asserts that Chinese growth came from its own unique brand of political economy that is neither a central planning system nor a conventional market economy. The foundation of that model is a meritocratic autocracy that is smart, strategic, and always focused on the long term. China boomed precisely because it did not reform its politics and rule of law is dismissed as a Western fixation that has no economic utility for China.

This conceptualization of Chinese growth model is implicitly conditioning the decision framework of Chinese entrepreneurs on the level of political institution rather than on its movement. There is an easy way to demonstrate the flaw with this approach: It is unable to explain why Chinese entrepreneurs sprang into action under Deng whereas they are retreating today under Xi Jinping.

For my approach, it is easy. Deng was moving China away from Mao’s totalitarianism, whereas Xi is moving China toward it. Let me frame this statement in rule-of-law language: Chinese entrepreneurship boomed when the country was moving _toward_ the rule of law; it is now retreating because the country is moving _away_ from it. The rule of law matters tremendously but we need a dynamic framework to capture its relevance and importance.

China was not, and never has been, a democracy. This is true, but the reformist leaders made several moves very early on with a clear intention of signaling an improvement in property rights security. They did not do so through constitutional reforms but through enhancing the legal and political security of entrepreneurs. In the 2008 edition of this book, I coined the term “directional liberalism” to explain why the private sector surged forward immediately after the Cultural Revolution.

Two things can be true at the same time. One is that China is not a liberal democracy; it has never been even at its most liberal moment, and it may never be. The other is that China can, at a particular time (e.g., the 1980s), move in a liberal direction. In my account, the trajectory of reforms is correlated with that movement rather than with the static characteristics of Chinese system at a particular moment in time. China boomed, in GDP but also in personal income, when it had a directionally liberal model of growth.[8](https://www.cambridge.org/core/product/identifier/9781009680646%23bp7/type/BOOK_PART#fn21)

The operative variable here is the _movement_ of politics rather than a given position of politics. The directionality of politics matters, not its level. Economic agents may still invest and expand their businesses even if China does not have the rule of law but that requires two conditions. One is that the investment returns have to be abnormally high in order to compensate for the risks of not having the rule of law. This condition is especially important to foreign investors, who have a menu of choices when they make investments. A combination of low returns and absence of the rule of law is the reality of Xi’s China today.

The other condition is that China is moving in the direction of the rule of law. This distinction between direction and level clarifies so much muddled thinking about Chinese institutions and Chinese growth. During the entire reform era, China was never in the vicinity of a democracy. Its Polity score is stuck stubbornly at −7. From this shabby level of political liberalism, Xi is taking China backward, moving the country away from that of Deng Xiaoping in the direction of Mao Zedong. Is it any surprise that entrepreneurs are not investing and foreign businesses are leaving?

**1.2.3**

# Russia, Iran and China use AI to amplify disinformation ahead of midterms

Foreign influence networks are using generative AI tools to produce fake videos, fake journalists and fake accounts before the November vote

Share

[](https://x.com/intent/tweet?url=https%3A%2F%2Fcryptobriefing.com%2Frussia-iran-china-ai-disinformation-midterms%2F&text=Russia%2C+Iran+and+China+use+AI+to+amplify+disinformation+ahead+of+midterms)[](https://www.linkedin.com/sharing/share-offsite/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fcryptobriefing.com%2Frussia-iran-china-ai-disinformation-midterms%2F)[](https://www.facebook.com/sharer/sharer.php?u=https%3A%2F%2Fcryptobriefing.com%2Frussia-iran-china-ai-disinformation-midterms%2F)

[Add us on Google](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=cryptobriefing.com "Add Crypto Briefing as your preferred source to see more of our stories on Google.")

by [Diego Almada Lopez](https://cryptobriefing.com/team/diego-almada-lopez/)

10 hours ago

Russia, Iran and China are using generative AI to push disinformation at American voters ahead of the US midterm elections, Bloomberg reported on October 14, 2026.

The midterms are scheduled for November 3, 2026. That leaves less than three weeks for platforms, AI companies and US officials to figure out how much of this content is out there, and who it is aimed at.

## Who is doing what

According to the research findings, all three governments’ affiliated networks have turned to mainstream generative AI products, including [OpenAI](https://cryptobriefing.com/markets/openai/)’s ChatGPT and [Anthropic](https://cryptobriefing.com/markets/anthropic/)’s Claude.

Intelligence assessments from US agencies and independent analysts indicate the goal is not a single knockout blow. Instead, the operations aim to widen political divides, chip away at public trust in the election process and inflame tensions that already exist.

**Russia** is the most visible actor. A Russian-linked network known as Matryoshka, also tracked as Operation Overload and Storm-1679, has been spreading AI-manipulated videos since early September 2026.

Its output includes deepfakes of celebrities criticizing Democratic figures. It has also produced fabricated news clips styled to look like they came from established outlets such as CNN.

**Iran** has taken a different partisan angle. Iran-associated networks have used AI-generated material to push anti-Republican messaging, and some of them have posed as US activists.

[Meta](https://cryptobriefing.com/markets/meta/) took down some of those Iranian networks earlier in 2026.

**China** is working at volume. Chinese operations tracked under the names Spamouflage and Green Cicada consist of thousands of artificial accounts, with AI used to manage those accounts and amplify their narratives.

### AI, tech, and the markets they move—in one daily briefing.

Daily. Free. Join 34,000+ readers across crypto, finance, and policy.

Email address Subscribe free
[We respect your privacy. Unsubscribe anytime.](https://cryptobriefing.com/privacy-policy/)

## The AI companies push back

OpenAI banned accounts tied to Russian and Iranian influence operations on October 8, 2026.

According to the research findings, OpenAI disrupted several Russian and Iranian campaigns that month. Those efforts involved inventing fake journalists and fake organizations, which were then used to spread misleading narratives.

Still, there are important limits on what is known. Investigators are still assessing the full scale of these operations and how directly they target the midterms specifically.

There is also a notable absence of evidence that any of these groups are trying to disrupt voting infrastructure directly. The threat, as currently understood, is to what voters believe, not to the machines that count their ballots.

## How we got here

The Kremlin has run social media disinformation campaigns since 2016 to sow chaos in American elections, the New York Times reported on September 18, 2026.

What has changed is the toolkit. In 2016, influence operations mostly relied on amplifying messages through social media. A decade later, generative AI lets operators produce content cheaply and run campaigns at a scale that would have been hard to staff before.

## What this means

OpenAI’s October bans show these companies can detect and remove bad actors. But detection after the fact means some content has already escaped into the wild.

Meta’s takedowns earlier in 2026 show enforcement is happening, yet the Chinese networks alone reportedly involve thousands of fake accounts.

According to the research findings, Washington has struggled to put comprehensive countermeasures in place against AI-enhanced tactics, and faces growing questions over whether it can keep pace with a threat that changes this quickly.

When a network fabricates clips designed to look like CNN, it borrows that outlet’s credibility.

What to watch next: whether more AI companies publish takedown reports, whether platforms announce additional network removals and whether US agencies release updated assessments before Election Day.

The other open question is whether investigators find any evidence of efforts aimed at election infrastructure itself. For now, the record points to a battle over perception rather than over polling places.

title: South Korea Expands its Defense Ties Amid Great Power Competition and Uncertain Inter-Korean Relations
summary: South Korean President Lee Jae Myung is seeking a greater role in international security and defense supply chains while also pursuing a more self-reliant defense posture. South Korea's expanding defense partnerships reflect a broader effor
content:
South Korean President Lee Jae Myung is seeking a greater role in international security and defense supply chains while also pursuing a more self-reliant defense posture. South Korea's expanding defense partnerships reflect a broader effort to translate its growing defense-industrial capacity into political influence and reduce strategic vulnerabilities amid intensifying US-China competition. Yet as Lee advocates for “peaceful coexistence” with North Korea, Pyongyang's continued military development and deepening cooperation with Russia underscore the potential limits of this approach. Together, these trends create new opportunities for defense-industrial and security cooperation in Southeast Asia, the Middle East and North Africa, but raise uncertainty about the Korean peninsula’s longer-term security environment.

#### **Seoul Navigates a Contested Security Environment**

Since taking office in June 2025, the Lee administration has sought to balance its relations with the US and China while deepening ties with middle powers to reduce its dependence on either country for security or economic stability. Although the US-South Korea alliance remains strong, with Secretary of War Pete Hegseth praising Seoul’s efforts to increase defense spending, the Trump administration’s more transactional approach to foreign policy has encouraged Seoul to diversify its strategic partnerships. That perception has been strengthened by Washington’s position that South Korea assumes primary responsibility for deterring North Korea, articulated in the 2026 National Defense Strategy, as well as President Trump's decision to scale back the annual Ulchi Freedom Shield exercise in August.

Lee has also notably departed from the hardline approach to North Korea taken by his predecessor, Yoon Suk Yeol. At the UN General Assembly last month, Lee proposed a three-pillar policy to facilitate a “peaceful coexistence” with Pyongyang, advocating for renewed US-North Korea talks and suggesting sanctions relief in exchange for a freeze on Pyongyang's nuclear and ballistic missile programs.

So far, Seoul’s calls for renewed dialogue and engagement have had minimal impact on Pyongyang’s missile tests and military development. North Korea removed all references to reunification in its constitution and continues to reject calls for denuclearization, conducting ballistic missile tests and advancing its sea-based nuclear deterrent. Shaping Pyongyang's calculus are lingering tensions stemming from the Yoon administration, deteriorating relations with Japan, and expanding technical and military cooperation with Russia. The Kim regime likely views its partnership with Moscow as a major strategic advantage, reducing its incentive to participate in talks with the US or South Korea.

With engagement efforts toward North Korea yielding few tangible results and uncertainty surrounding US policy persisting, Seoul is building up its domestic capabilities. South Korea tested its first domestically produced hypersonic glide vehicles this month, marking a notable advancement in its missile capabilities. Seoul has also sought to accelerate the transfer of wartime operational control (OPCON) from the US-led Combined Forces Command to the South Korean military, a process that has spanned multiple presidencies, but the Lee administration has especially pushed for. However, US military officials, including the former commander of US Forces Korea, have cautioned that Seoul has not yet attained all military capabilities necessary to assume OPCON, particularly in missile defense and critical C5ISR capabilities (Command, Control, Communications, Computers, Cyber, Intelligence, Surveillance, and Reconnaissance).

#### **Deepening Defense Cooperation with Middle Powers**

In its pursuit of greater strategic autonomy and deterrence, the Lee administration has leveraged defense-industrial development to advance diplomatic objectives and strengthen global influence. Prior to Lee’s tenure, South Korea saw a substantial increase in arms exports along with initiatives aimed at strengthening defense-industrial capacity. These initiatives began following the Russia-Ukraine war and substantially deepened Seoul’s defense ties with Europe, which needed alternative suppliers to quickly replenish depleted stockpiles and to rapidly boost military capabilities. Amid intensifying US-China strategic competition, however, the Lee administration has increasingly framed these efforts as part of a broader hedging strategy. Pursuant to this strategy, the Lee administration has deepened ties with Middle Eastern and Southeast Asian middle powers to diversify its defense and economic relationships without diminishing its defense alliance with the US. Moreover, the Lee administration has expressed willingness to aid partners in building their domestic defense industries, presenting another avenue for Seoul to expand its influence.

Following a years-long trend of South Korean governments advancing security partnerships with Indo-Pacific nations, the Lee administration upgraded its special strategic partnership with Indonesia to a special comprehensive strategic partnership in April, South Korea’s highest level of bilateral ties short of a formal alliance. As part of this partnership, the two countries agreed to proceed with joint production of the KF-21 fighter jet, a program more than a decade in development, while expanding defense-industrial cooperation to include anti-tank guided missile systems and ammunition. The deal helps secure Seoul’s interests in Indonesia, including access to critical minerals and LNG, as South Korea's traditional energy suppliers in the Gulf have faced significant disruptions. More broadly, the move reflects Seoul's effort to strengthen partnerships with members of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations.

Seoul has also extended its footprint outside the Indo-Pacific. In the Middle East and North Africa, Seoul has expanded partnerships traditionally centered on energy to include arms exports, localized manufacturing, cybersecurity cooperation and other aspects of defense. In October 2026, South Korea upgraded its bilateral ties with Egypt to a strategic partnership, signing a memorandum of understanding on shipbuilding and broadening joint defense production beyond the manufacture of K-9 self-propelled howitzers, which began earlier this year. Egyptian officials also confirmed discussions over the potential sale of 36 FA-50 aircraft to Cairo. The Lee administration has pursued similar defense-industrial arrangements with the UAE and Saudi Arabia.

For Seoul, strategic defense partnerships with other middle powers enhance its credibility as a reliable defense cooperation partner and support its broader effort to reduce dependence on any single security partner. For its partners, particularly in the MENA region, acquiring South Korean systems that are compatible with Western platforms improves interoperability during joint exercises while reducing exposure to the political sensitivities and potential restrictions that can accompany purchases of Chinese defense equipment (although defense cooperation with Beijing is likely to continue).

#### **Implications for Businesses**

South Korea's push for joint defense production presents opportunities for firms involved in manufacturing, systems integration, logistics, workforce development, and lifecycle sustainment. Across partnerships with Egypt, Saudi Arabia and the UAE, Seoul has increasingly paired defense exports with technology-transfer arrangements, training, and long-term maintenance support. This approach aligns with regional efforts to develop indigenous defense industries and could generate demand for industrial infrastructure, engineering services, supply-chain integration, and advanced manufacturing capabilities. However, commercial opportunities will depend on whether political agreements and memorandums of understanding translate into funded procurement programs.

As South Korea's strategic partnership with Egypt expands to include shipbuilding and maritime cooperation, the security of the Suez Canal and Red Sea shipping routes will be of even greater importance for Seoul. Building on the Cheonghae Unit's long-standing anti-piracy mission in the Gulf of Aden, future cooperative frameworks with Cairo could focus on maritime domain awareness, technology transfers in unmanned systems, and the protection of critical infrastructure. Such initiatives would advance Seoul's interest in safeguarding the maritime corridors through which much of its trade and imported energy flow. Recent disruptions to regional shipping and energy markets have only heightened the importance of these routes for South Korea's economic security. Greater South Korean support in preserving freedom of navigation and regional capacity-building could help reduce insecurity and uncertainty for commercial vessels transiting the Bab el-Mandeb or Strait of Hormuz.

In addition to its growing security interests abroad, Seoul must also contend with evolving security challenges on the Korean peninsula. Obstacles to Lee’s peaceful coexistence policy could increase pressure on Seoul to demonstrate that its military can independently execute critical military capabilities as it works toward assuming OPCON. This, in turn, could shape South Korea’s procurement priorities, generating demand for technologies integral to enhancing C5ISR capabilities, including secure communications, command-and-control systems, AI, and unmanned platforms. However, specific procurement contracts will depend on military modernization priorities and the US and South Korea’s assessments of progress toward OPCON transfer requirements.

title: Loaded for Bear: Why Minister Mantashe’s affection for coal is rooted in BEE, transformation
summary: Mineral and Petroleum Resources Minister Gwede Mantashe proudly wears his label, “Old King Coal”, and he boosts the fossil fuel every chance he gets. That has provoked a lot of understandable criticism from environmentalists, as the flames
content:
Mineral and Petroleum Resources Minister Gwede Mantashe proudly wears his label, “Old King Coal”, and he boosts the fossil fuel every chance he gets.

That has provoked a lot of understandable criticism from environmentalists, as the flames of climate change linked to the use of coal, oil and gas threaten to engulf our burning planet.

But what is often overlooked is that Mantashe’s affection for coal is in large part explained by one of his trademark political and policy priorities: transformation and raising the levels of Black ownership and management in the mining industry and the wider economy.

As such, it provides a revealing lens into African and non-African views of the green energy transition, economic development and the use of natural resources.

“Everybody in coal is a Black company, owned and managed by Black South Africans,” Mantashe said last week during his address to the Joburg Mining Indaba. “Today you find Exxaro, Seriti, Thungela and so forth. The old is dying and the new is emerging.”

That is indeed the case, with some caveats.

### Into the weeds

For example, Exxaro, which has coal as its core commodity but is diversifying into manganese, bauxite and copper, is 31.47% “Black empowered”, according to its latest annual report. And its C-suite is predominantly Black, with Ben Magara as its CEO.

Thungela is 67.55% Black owned, according to its latest compliance report to the Broad-Based Black Economic Empowerment Commission and its executive team under CEO Moses Madondo is mostly Black. Unlisted Seriti is overwhelmingly Black owned and managed.

Viewing this transformed landscape, it is useful to recall that Thungela was demerged from Anglo American in 2021 against the backdrop of growing foreign investor aversion to coal because of the unfolding climate crisis.

Anglo’s removal of thermal coal from its portfolio was in response to investor pressure, including from the likes of the pension board for the Church of England.

The bottom line is that foreign capital has been ditching South African coal, and mostly Black, domestic investors have moved into this abandoned space.

This is surely a reflection of conflicting perceptions of the green energy transition, but the issue is seldom framed that way.

On one hand, the urgency of the climate crisis clearly calls for immediate action. The science is gin clear: the CO 2 emissions unleashed by the Industrial Revolution are accelerating climate change and warming our planet at an unprecedented pace.

In the latest flashing red light, this past September was the second-warmest on record and was the second consecutive month in 2026 that saw global temperatures exceed 1.5°C above pre-industrial levels.

But historically, the majority of CO 2 that has been pumped into the atmosphere has been from the “Global North” or the industrialised economies of Europe and North America. China, India and Indonesia have become big-league members of this club in recent decades.

By contrast, Africa – the world’s poorest continent and the one where climate change will probably have its worst impacts – currently accounts for only about 4% of global emissions.

Viewed through this prism, the “case for coal” in Africa boils down to the perceived unfairness of the region being constrained from using its resource endowment in the same manner that gave rise to industrialisation and high-income levels in advanced economies.

### Rich vein

Mantashe is tapping a rich vein on this front and, politically, it speaks to a wide swathe of his base including the National Union of Mineworkers (NUM), which is staunchly opposed to shuttering South African coal operations for environmental reasons – a stance that is also clearly linked to its membership numbers.

South Africa’s ranking among global CO 2 emitters is 15th – largely because of Eskom and Sasol – but it is dwarfed by the big guys, and Africa as a whole is hardly responsible for our warming world.

Many investors up North may not want coal in their portfolios, but the backlash against the commodity is more muted here for historical reasons. The reluctance to invest in or provide financing for coal projects has been melting like a polar ice cap up North as well.

In 2021, when Anglo was answering the Church of England’s prayers and spinning off Thungela, the UN convened the Net-Zero Banking Alliance (NZBA) – a move that captured the prevailing zeitgeist as a growing number of banks and fund managers were turning their backs on coal.

The NZBA ceased to function a year ago after a tsunami of banks left its shores, including heavyweights such as JPMorgan and Citigroup – and global coal demand reached a record high last year.

There is still a lot of hostility to coal from the finance sector outside Africa. Major European banks such as ING and BNP Paribas remain committed to rapidly reducing their exposure to coal. In South Africa, Nedbank is a leader in this regard.

But in the developing world, Mantashe is not an outlier, and his critics on this issue have often failed to grasp this point. In South Africa, the sector is clearly more “transformed” than most, which surely helps to explain Mantashe’s enthusiasm for it.

This does not mean that it should not be subjected to scrutiny and criticism. But context is important.

South Africa’s BBBEE policies are also widely seen as a deterrent to the foreign investment the economy desperately needs, given our low domestic savings rates, and that is a fair point. But with coal, foreign capital flowed out, and domestic Black investment flowed in.

It’s also the case that South Africa’s coal producers have embraced renewable energy projects. Seriti Green, for example, is focused on this sector.

Global distribution of coal exports in 2025.

For the record, I think the sooner we can dispense with coal, the better. But then, I still own and drive vehicles powered by internal combustion engines and don’t plan to trade them in for a horse and wagon anytime soon. My own lifestyle and standard of living are largely rooted in fossil fuels.

More broadly, this contested terrain over Africa’s resource wealth can be seen in other areas such as debates around the sustainable use and consumption of wildlife products and trophy hunting.

For example, the opposition to reopening the global trade in sustainably harvested rhino horn and trophy hunting in Africa is almost exclusively driven by affluent members of the middle and upper classes in the Global North.

But the scientific spoor of most peer-reviewed studies highlights the positive conservation and economic outcomes of regulated trophy hunting, which is pointedly sanctioned by democratically elected African governments such as Botswana’s and South Africa’s, and supported by rural Black communities that bear the brunt of living [alongside dangerous wildlife](https://conbio.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/con4.70080).

Like Mantashe’s stance on coal, this does not mean that such policies should not be subjected to scrutiny and criticism. But it’s important to keep in mind that what makes greens see red in the Global North does not always press African buttons the same way. **DM**

# Northern Taiwan to see showers Thursday as day-night temperature gap widens

10/14/2026 08:15 PM

[](jsvscript:)[](jsvscript:)[](javascript:void(0))[Listen](javascript:)

Taipei, Oct. 14 (CNA) Northern Taiwan will see local showers on Thursday, with weather conditions over the following days expected to stabilize, according to the Central Weather Administration (CWA).

However, a wider day-night temperature gap is expected to persist through Tuesday, the CWA added.

Although the northeasterly monsoon will weaken on Thursday, moisture levels are set to increase, bringing localized showers to Keelung's northern coast, mountainous areas of Greater Taipei, eastern Taiwan and the Hengchun Peninsula, according to the CWA forecast.

Yilan is expected to see the most significant rainfall on Thursday, CWA forecaster Wang Pin-hsiang (王品翔) said.

Temperatures in northern and northeastern Taiwan will be relatively low, with highs of 28-30 degrees Celsius, while highs in central and southern Taiwan will reach 32-33 degrees on Thursday, Wang said.

After Thursday, moisture levels will gradually decrease across Taiwan, with sunny to cloudy skies expected from Friday through Tuesday, he added.

Eastern Taiwan and the Hengchun Peninsula will see localized showers, while mountainous areas in central and southern Taiwan will experience sporadic showers.

From Friday, daytime highs could exceed 30 degrees across Taiwan, with temperatures in central and southern areas ranging from 33-35 degrees, Wang said.

However, the day-night temperature difference will be most pronounced in western Taiwan, with lows of 23-25 degrees, he added.

Owing to radiative cooling, some parts of Taiwan could see lows below 20 degrees Celsius, Wang said.

(By Chang Hsiung-feng and Lee Chieh-yu)

title: Padel Pilipinas makes historic Asian Games debut as Abad, Malazarte break into Asia’s Top 4
summary: **MANILA, Philippines** — From the bottom seed to the final four, Filipino national athletes Danna Abad and Joshea Malazarte delivered a breakthrough performance for padel at the 20th Asian Games Aichi-Nagoya 2026. The youngest pair in Team
content:
**MANILA, Philippines** — From the bottom seed to the final four, Filipino national athletes Danna Abad and Joshea Malazarte delivered a breakthrough performance for padel at the 20th Asian Games Aichi-Nagoya 2026.

The youngest pair in Team Padel Pilipinas entered the women’s draw as the No. 23 seed — the lowest-seeded pair in the 23-team field — but battled through three rounds of competition to earn a semifinal berth in padel’s historic Asian Games debut.

Held at the Higashi Sports Center from September 28 to October 3, the padel competition brought together 13 nations — the Philippines, Lebanon, Qatar, Iran, the United Arab Emirates, Kazakhstan, Kuwait, Thailand, Indonesia, Malaysia, Hong Kong, and Japan, with Saudi Arabia competing exclusively in the women’s division.

*   [Eala eyes fresh start at Ningbo Open](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/14/sports/eala-eyes-fresh-start-at-ningbo-open/2445183)

“Being part of the Asian Games is a huge step for padel in the Philippines. Our athletes showed that they can compete on this stage, and more importantly, they gained the experience of going up against some of the best in Asia. This is an important foundation for where we want to take the sport next,” said Padel Pilipinas President Jeff Cheng.

In the first match of Team Philippines, Abad and Malazarte opened with a dominant 6-1, 6-0 victory over Saudi Arabia’s Samaher Alkurdi and Lina Alabdullatif, immediately setting the tone for what would become a breakthrough showing.

National Team Captain LA Cañizares and Jason Tamayo followed with a 6-1, 6-4 victory over Indonesia’s Christian Alvin Edison and Giorgio Soermarno, while Tao Yee Tan and Marian Capadocia battled Kazakhstan’s Albina Khabibulina and Mariya Sinitsyna to a 6-3, 2-6, 6-2 victory.

The Round of 16 brought another pair of victories for the Philippines, with Abad and Malazarte overcoming Hong Kong’s Venise Chan and Hiu Wai Lau, 6-1, 6(5)-7, 6-3, in a tightly contested three-set battle. Cañizares and Tamayo also advanced after defeating Hong Kong’s Kwan Lam Vincent Chau and Lok Pui Lawrence Lo, 6-2, 6-2.

Tan and Capadocia, meanwhile, bowed out after a closely contested three-set match against Hong Kong’s Hiu Laam Chan and Yik Yan Law, falling 7-5, 4-6, 4-6. The Philippines’ second men’s pair, Abdulqoahar Allian and Raymark Gulfo, also concluded their campaign after losing to the United Arab Emirates’ Fares Al Janahi and Abdullah Alabdulla.

*   ![Image 1: Pangilinan seeks reversal of ruling on Duterte’s dropped charges](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/14/1258438.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Pangilinan seeks reversal of ruling on Duterte’s dropped charges](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/14/news/pangilinan-seeks-reversal-of-ruling-on-dutertes-dropped-charges/2445025)

Abad and Malazarte kept their momentum rolling in the quarterfinals, overcoming Iran’s Saba Najafi Dehaghi and Neda Mohammad Taghipour, 6-2, 3-6, 6-2, to punch their ticket to the semifinals.

On the other hand, Cañizares and Tamayo faced a tough quarterfinal challenge against Malaysia’s Christian Didier Chin Zao Quan and Aidan Yunus. After taking the second set, the Filipino pair ultimately fell 3-6, 6-3, 3-6, bringing their run to a close.

Entering the tournament as the No. 23 seed — the lowest-seeded pair in a 23-pair field — Abad and Malazarte quickly became one of the tournament’s surprise stories. They climbed through the draw, knocking out higher-ranked opposition and earning their place among the final four, alongside three top-seeded teams: Japan’s No. 2 seed and Indonesia’s No. 3 and No. 7 seeds.

In the semifinals, the duo faced Indonesia’s Fadona Kusumawati and Fitriani Sabatini. They lost and returned to compete for bronze against Indonesia’s Novela Putria and Beatrice Gumulya, ultimately finishing fourth.

*   ![Image 2: Lacson asks Padilla to clarify ‘disregard for law’ comment on Duterte trial](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/13/1256725.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Lacson asks Padilla to clarify ‘disregard for law’ comment on Duterte trial](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/13/news/lacson-asks-padilla-to-clarify-disregard-for-law-comment-on-duterte-trial/2444142)

From the bottom seed to the final four, Abad and Malazarte became one of the defining moments at the Asian Games. Securing Top 4 in Asia marked a breakthrough for the next generation of padel in the Philippines.

Secretary General Duane Santos said, “We are proud of how every athlete represented the Philippines in Nagoya. Some matches did not go our way, but each pair showed resilience, competed hard, and gained valuable experience on the Asian Games stage. This is only the beginning, and we look forward to seeing these athletes continue to grow and push the sport forward. Our focus now is on building a stronger pipeline of athletes through grassroots programs, developing young players from an early age, and giving them more opportunities to train and compete. We want to make sure that the next generation has the foundation and support to take padel in the Philippines even further.”

Senator Pia Cayetano, a competitive padel player and the founder of Padel Pilipinas, marvelled at Team Philippine’s showing in the first ever padel tournament in the Asian Games. She said, “I’ve seen the work our players have put in and think we’ve been able to show that with proper and consistent training throughout the year, and the support our national team receives, we can compete on the Asian stage.” The team’s campaign was backed by a dedicated coaching staff led by Head Coach Bryan Casao, with Coach Tomás Vasco, Mental Performance Coach Ayel Estrañero, Strength and Conditioning Coach Jaric Lavalle, and Coach Eric Marquez working together to prepare the athletes for the competition.

The national padel athletes showed grit, composure, and competitive fire against some of Asia’s strongest. Together, they carried the flag with honor and made the country’s historic padel debut one to remember. The result provides a strong foundation for the continued growth of the sport and the athletes who will carry the sport forward.TMT

title: Eala slump continues with Wuhan exit
summary: IT may be the case of fatigue kicking in, the law of averages catching up, a slump getting in the way, or a combination of the three. Whatever the reason, Filipino tennis ace Alexandra “Alex” Eala found herself on the wrong end of an upset
content:
IT may be the case of fatigue kicking in, the law of averages catching up, a slump getting in the way, or a combination of the three.

Whatever the reason, Filipino tennis ace Alexandra “Alex” Eala found herself on the wrong end of an upset loss for the third straight time.

World No. 19 Eala fell to Chinese qualifier and No. 217 Shi Han, 6-4, 3-6, 3-6, to make a first-round exit at the WTA 1000 Wuhan Open in China Monday night, Oct. 12.

*   ['Time for Alex to really regroup. A very disappointing loss' — Noli Eala](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/13/sports/time-for-alex-to-really-regroup-a-very-disappointing-loss-noli-eala/2444175)

Eala held off Shi in the first set and even took a 3-2 lead in the second.

Shi went on a rampage from there, winning seven straight games to take control for the rest of the way and handing Eala her worst loss of the season.

# ‘Pax Silica to be culturally sensitive’

[![Image 18: the author image](https://manilatimes.net/uploads/authors/4138_1768618327.jpg)![Image 19: the author image](https://manilatimes.net/uploads/authors/4138_1768618327.jpg)](https://www.manilatimes.net/author/allen-limos "author image")

PRESIDENT Ferdinand Marcos Jr. assured the public that the government will be culturally sensitive to concerns of displacement caused by the Pax Silica initiative.

In a press briefing on Tuesday, The Manila Times asked Marcos about concerns of Capas, Mayor Boots Rodriguez, that local communities might be displaced because of the planned 4,000-hectare AI hub and concerns that ancestral burial grounds might be disturbed.

“We are very sensitive to that. That’s not something that people should worry about. We are very sensitive about such cultural concerns, and those are very much part of the discussions,” said Marcos.

*   [ICC prosecutor removes 253 items from evidence list in Duterte case](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/13/news/icc-prosecutor-removes-253-items-from-evidence-list-in-duterte-case/2444598)

When asked about livelihood concerns on the project, Marcos said that is the opposite of what the Pax Silica initiative is designed to do.

“I cannot see how such a development will endanger local livelihood. I’m not sure I understand the question simply because this is quite big; this is projected to create tens of thousands of jobs,” he said.

“If you would look at what we did as chair of Asean, one of the things that we did as the chair of Asean was to define the roadmap for Asean for AI. But that was even before the whole idea of Pax Silica emerged,” he said.

title: Visa gets approval to prepare for domestic business in China
summary: US payments firm Visa has received approval from China’s central bank to begin preparations for a domestic bank card clearing institution in the country, ending years of waiting to tap into one of the world’s largest payment markets. The mo
content:
US payments firm Visa has received approval from China’s central bank to begin preparations for a domestic bank card clearing institution in the country, ending years of waiting to tap into one of the world’s largest payment markets.

The move marks a major step for Visa to join rivals American Express and Mastercard in operating bank card clearing services in China and represents a further opening up of the nation’s tightly controlled financial sector.

The People’s Bank of China (PBOC) issued an administrative approval to Visa Information Technology (Beijing) Co. Ltd. permitting it to begin preparatory work, according to the central bank’s website.

*   [Prepare for El Niño, Marcos urges Filipinos](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/13/business/top-business/prepare-for-el-nio-marcos-urges-filipinos/2444065)

Visa Information Technology (Beijing) is a foreign-invested enterprise established in China by Visa.

“The approval of our Application to Prepare marks a significant step forward in Visa’s long-standing commitment to China,” Visa CEO Ryan McInerney said in a statement on Tuesday.

The approval comes after US President Donald Trump’s summit with Chinese leader Xi Jinping earlier this year in China, which included more than a dozen CEOs of top US companies, including those of Mastercard and Visa.

“We greatly appreciate the important role of the leaders of the United States and China in pursuing a constructive and strategically stable relationship between the world’s largest economies,” McInerney said.

Visa must complete its preparations within one year, after which it can apply to open for business, the PBOC said.

The central bank, together with the nation’s top banking regulator, will review the application and, if it approves, issue a bank card clearing business license.

A goodwill gesture?

*   ![Image 3: ICC prosecutor removes 253 items from evidence list in Duterte case](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/13/1257681.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[ICC prosecutor removes 253 items from evidence list in Duterte case](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/13/news/icc-prosecutor-removes-253-items-from-evidence-list-in-duterte-case/2444598)

Visa was hoping to break into the Chinese market, which is dominated by state-controlled China UnionPay, with an unprecedented 100-percent ownership stake in a future joint venture license, sources have told Reuters.

“This should be viewed as a goodwill gesture from Beijing toward Washington ahead of the next meeting between Presidents Xi Jinping and Donald Trump,” said George Chen, partner and chairman of digital practice at The Asia Group. The two are expected to meet again on the sidelines of the APEC Economic Leaders’ Meeting in Shenzhen in November.

Greater market access in financial services has long been a priority for Washington, which has consistently urged Beijing to provide a more open and level playing field for foreign firms operating in China’s financial sector, said Chen.

Mastercard, partnering with local clearinghouse NetsUnion Clearing Corp., won approval to prepare to set up its bank card clearing business in China in 2020.

American Express’ joint venture in the country was cleared to start bank card clearing services later that year.

In China, bank cards processed 4.6 trillion transactions worth 963.60 trillion yuan ($143.92 trillion) in 2025, according to data from the central bank, highlighting the market’s enormous potential.

# Kim Jones to open first global flagship at Henderson's Central Yards in 2027

British designer Kim Jones will open his first global flagship at Henderson Land's Central Yards in Hong Kong in 2027, occupying a duplex maison with about 4,000 square feet. Henderson Land chairman Martin Lee Ka-shing called it a vote of confidence in Hong Kong's creative capital status.

 By [Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk), Editor in Chief

British fashion designer Kim Jones will open the first global flagship for his newly launched label at Central Yards in Hong Kong in 2027, developer Henderson Land announced on Tuesday.

Henderson Land chairman Martin Lee Ka-shing said Jones's presence was “a powerful vote of confidence in Hong Kong's standing as a global creative capital,” describing him as “a visionary bridging street culture and high fashion.”

The flagship will occupy one of five signature duplex concept maisons at Central Yards overlooking Victoria Harbour. The store will span about 4,000 square feet across two levels and feature open terraces, internal staircases and entrances connecting indoor and outdoor areas.

“Hong Kong is a city I know well, and opening our first flagship at Central Yards gives us an opportunity to explore those ideas in a new context,” Jones said. “I'm looking forward to developing a space that reflects the identity of the label and how I want it to evolve.”

Phase one of Central Yards will include about 300,000 square feet of retail space, with around 100 brands and concepts across fashion, lifestyle and dining, according to Henderson Land. The retail area will extend from the ground floor to Level Three, with a promenade-style layout linking indoor and outdoor spaces. Duplex retail spaces on Level One will feature interiors inspired by the themes of “Sea, Land and Sky.”

Beyond retail, Central Yards will present a program of cultural, arts and community experiences, anchored by unprecedented open spaces, the city's only private Broadway-calibre theatre, and 12 world-class outdoor event spaces enlivened by pop-up kiosks, cultural markets and seasonal festivals.

# 挪威军演士兵发现中国产汽车拍摄军事设施密码等敏感信息引安全担忧

在挪威上月的一次军事演习中，中国制造的汽车被发现拍摄了敏感信息，其中包括军事设施的入口密码以及人员动向，这引发了人们对联网汽车所带来的风险的担忧。

发表时间： 17/10/2026 - 12:17 更改时间： 17/10/2026 - 12:18

 8 分钟 浏览时间

 长安深蓝S07 Ultra插电式混合动力车于10月2日在希腊雅典举行的车展上首次亮相，这是该车型的欧洲首秀资料图片。 © 美联社图片

 作者： [弗林](https://rfi.fr/cn/%E4%BD%9C%E8%80%85/%E5%BC%97%E6%9E%97/ "弗林")

广告

继续浏览后续

据挪威《商业新闻报》（Dagens Næringsliv）报导，在9月14日至18日于奥斯陆机场举行的一次安全演习期间，一些待命的士兵在操作车内屏幕时，意外发现了由车载摄像头录制的视频。这些视频记录了人员的上下车情况、车辆行驶路线，甚至还包括用于开启军事设施大门或房门的密码。

在这场演习结束三周后发布的报道中，《商业新闻报》指出，这些视频来自租赁车辆——其中至少有两辆是深蓝汽车品牌汽车，由中国国有控股车企长安汽车生产。这些车辆由赫兹挪威（Hertz Norge）公司提供给军方，而该公司由中国汽车集团吉利间接持有。

挪威国民卫队发言人格罗斯伯格豪根（Per Gunnar Grosberghaugen）中校向法新社证实了这一点：“是的，挪威国民卫队的士兵在这些车辆的系统内发现了由车载传感器所记录的视频”。目前尚不清楚这些视频记录是否曾被分享给第三方，特别是中国，但该军官表示无法排除这种可能性。

这一事件凸显出一个矛盾：尽管欧洲各国军队正在加强防范间谍活动和混合威胁，但他们所使用的车辆本身却能够收集敏感信息。据《商业新闻报》报导，即便在发现这些数据泄露后，由于缺乏替代方案，挪威军方仍继续使用这些车辆直至演习结束；而士兵们则将这些视频进行了删除。

挪威军方认为，全面禁止中国制造的车辆所带来的影响，与其可能实现的安全收益相比并不相称；因此，挪威军方倾向于针对不同场所采取量身定制的安全措施——例如，无论车辆产自何处，若其配备了摄像头和传感器，则可在特定区域内对其采取禁入措施。

挪威赫兹（Hertz Norge）强调，公司始终遵守挪威及欧洲的相关法规。该公司市场与传播总监内尔博维克（Hallvard Nerbovik）向法新社表示：“我们能够确保客户数据的安全”。

内尔博维克补充道：“除非有明确的法律依据，否则我们不会与汽车制造商、公司所有方或其他第三方共享任何与租赁业务相关的个人数据”。但他并未明确说明车内影像资料是否曾被传输给第三方。长安集团未就法新社的提问作出回应。

去年，针对奥斯陆公共交通服务营运商Ruter进行的测试显示，中国制造商宇通客车理论上可以通过其“空中下载技术”（OTA）更新系统，远程锁定其电动巴士，使其无法运行。在紧急情况下，挪威或许会动用这些巴士来疏散民众。Ruter表示，此后其已引入相关机制，能够监控并延迟接收到的信号，从而对系统更新进行管控。

现代交通工具并非唯一的潜在“特洛伊木马”。智能手表以及深受跑步爱好者青睐的健身应用，如 Strava，也可能导致敏感的军事信息外泄。2018年，Strava公布的数据使得外界能够识别出军事设施及士兵的行踪，尤其是在阿富汗和叙利亚地区。

今年3月，法国《世界报》得以在地中海东部近乎实时地确定法国海军“戴高乐”号航空母舰的位置——这正是因为舰上一名水兵使用了该应用程序。

content: 作者臉書 2026-10-15 近日，德國安聯集團最新發佈的《2026全球財富報告》，公佈台灣人均金融資產淨值高達164,470歐元（約新台幣594萬元，折合人民幣123萬7,989元），高據全球第五位，僅次於美國、瑞士、丹麥和新加坡。 同一個研究公佈的中國大陸人均金融資產淨值是16,160歐元（相當於120,657元人民幣，即每個中國人擁有資產12萬以上，可能是根據中共的官方數字統計，以李克強的六億中國人月入一千元常識判斷，實不可能），相對於台灣的164,470歐元，台灣足足高了十倍。 國際貨幣基金組織最新發佈的《世界經濟展望》，預估台灣2026年實質GDP經濟成長率將高達10.7%，而中國大陸的經濟還在「保5」的位置上苦苦掙扎，非官方的經濟學家，有的預測只有2-3%，有的甚至說是負數。 台灣去年全年資金淨流入數額高達368.48億美元，今年前9個月外資淨流入已高達1,083億美元，相當於人民幣7,246億元。與此相反，2026年中國商務部統計的實際使用外資，同比下降10.3%至2,877億元人民幣，只及台灣三分之一強，以大陸經濟體規模相較於台灣，更顯數字可憐。 台灣今年股巿巿值大幅飇升約新台幣55.64兆元（折合1.35兆美元），累計漲幅67.37%。對比中國大陸，上證指數徘徊在3800點左右，自2015年起，十餘年後仍在原位起落。 因為經濟暢旺，賴清德政府決定向全體台灣人民每人派發一萬台幣，將經濟發展紅利及時與國民分享。相比中國大陸，即使在經濟最好的年代，也從來沒有向全體國民派錢的舉措，政府有錢都拿去搞維穩，收買亞非拉窮國，搞一帶一路，支援世界革命了。 台灣社會非常穩定，國家民主體制趨於成熟，即使在選舉年頭，不同政治派別的民眾仍保持互相尊重，媒體也不會壁壘分明，新聞自由充份。台灣有全世界最好的醫療保障體系和社會保險制度，高科技稱雄全球，進出口呈現高速增長勢頭。 就外部環境來看，台灣也處於史上最好的年頭。美國與歐盟國家，先後對聯合國2758號決議作出深刻反省，不齒中共的曲解誤導，強調中華民國與中華人民共和國互不隸屬。 台灣現任與退休官員，到美日歐盟國家參訪，在議會公開發言，都已經是常態。在美歐日推動下，台灣參與世衛等國際組織活動也是遲早的事，形勢正朝著對台灣有利的方向發展。 美日北約視台灣海峽為國際水域，西方國家的軍艦輪番在海峽通過，等於向中共示威，意味著西方國家不容忍中共侵佔台灣，因為台灣一旦被中共佔領，西方就無法自由通航。 近年，以台積電為首的台灣高科技頭部企業，廣受世界各國的青睞，各國競爭AI，無不要看台灣臉色，台灣掌握高科技世紀的利器。 台灣內外形勢不是小好，而是空前大好，而且會越來越好，這應該成為台灣朝野的共識，成為台灣人作出任何政經決策時的底氣。 台灣往上走，大陸往下沉，海峽兩邊呈現不同的發展勢頭，在這種形勢下，國民黨以鄭麗文為首的舔共派，卻一天到晚唱衰台灣，以爭取和平為名，行投共賣台之實。 其實，國民黨大可不必靠舔共來活命。國民黨最高的政治訴求是什麼？既不是和平，也不是統一，是再度上台執政，國民黨不能靠舔共來爭取選票，因為投共恰恰是票房毒藥，它將失去更多熱愛台灣的同胞的選票。 相反的，只要始終站在台灣利益立場，為民興利除弊，就足以與民進黨展開良性競爭，爭取在政治路線與地方行政方面得到台灣人認可，他們就有重新執政的機會。 國民黨與中共，歷史上都不共戴天，兩蔣時代如此，李登輝時代也如此，直至連戰當年敗選，國民黨突然向北京叩頭，企圖借中共改革開放紅利，幫助國民黨重奪執政權。這是一個歷史性的路線錯誤，面對今日台灣內外大好形勢，應該徹底反省了。 真正有心舔共賣台的人，在台灣一定是極少數，多數台灣人只是不希望發生戰爭。中共借戰爭威脅，來達到他脅迫台灣的目的，但中共的武裝犯台只是虛張聲勢，在今日台灣內外大好形勢下，稍有常識的人，都不會相信中共敢於陷自己於萬劫不復之地。 只要國民黨不舔共，中共就無法統戰台灣，中共在台灣沒有立足點，沒有它的第五縱隊，就無從干涉台灣內政，那時就不是國民黨要討好中共，反而是中共要討好國民黨。今日形勢下，國民黨根本可以站在台灣利益的立場，從容與中共周旋，佔取政治上主動。 近年來，國民黨主流政客正在悄然調整他們的政治路線，馬英九在大陸強調「台灣命運要由台灣二千三百萬人民決定」，便是最直接的宣示。韓國瑜鼓吹的「親美和中」，也將兩岸關係降格到美台關係之下，「親」與「和」是兩種不同層次的立場，親是自己人親，和是與對手和。為什麼韓國瑜不說「親中和美」？因為親美比親中更重要。 回歸台灣本位立場，這是國民黨的活路，否則，在舔共路上越走越遠，與中共越親，離台灣人越遠，那就是自我毀滅之路，國民黨再執迷不悟，只有死路一條。趙少康說過，任由中共介選，國民黨就完蛋，台灣就完蛋，中華民國就完蛋——旨在斯言！

# 欧盟正准备新贸易防御工具，中国警告：欧方不能幻想以施压换好处

欧盟委员会主席冯德莱恩周五证实，欧盟正在准备一项新的工具，以便欧盟在与第三国发生贸易冲突时，能够“迅速有效地”关闭欧盟市场的准入。中国商务部发警告。

发表时间： 17/10/2026 - 00:44

 4 分钟 浏览时间

 2026年10月15日，参加欧盟峰会的欧盟领袖在一起交谈。 AP Photo/Geert Vanden Wijngaert - Geert Vanden Wijngaert

 作者： [阿曼亭](https://rfi.fr/cn/%E4%BD%9C%E8%80%85/%E9%98%BF%E6%9B%BC%E4%BA%AD/ "阿曼亭")

广告

继续浏览后续

欧盟正在准备措施，以便在发生贸易冲突时能够“迅速地”保护欧盟市场。

法新社报道，欧盟委员会主席冯德莱恩周五证实，欧盟正在准备一项新的工具，以便欧盟在与第三国发生贸易冲突时，能够“迅速有效地”关闭欧盟市场的准入。布鲁塞尔此举借鉴了法国和德国提出的联合提案，该提案旨在加强欧盟在与中国发生贸易冲突时的防御能力。

就欧盟打算扩大对中国的贸易防御措施，中国商务部周五晚放话说，欧方不能幻想以施压换取好处，更不要低估中方维护自身利益的决心和能力。

中国商务部官网16日晚间发布“就欧盟峰会提出对华‘双轨’思路答记者问”的新闻稿。

根据该新闻稿，中国商务部新闻发言人在回答记者提问时称，中欧经贸磋商的目的是要透过对话协商妥处分歧，照顾彼此关切。双方都要拿出解决问题的诚意。“欧方不能幻想以施压换取好处，更不要低估中方维护自身利益的决心和能力”。敦促欧方与中方相向而行，推动中欧经贸关系健康稳定发展。

路透社15日报导，欧盟领袖在欧盟峰会期间讨论如何因应中国出口激增。峰会的草案结论显示，欧盟领袖希望欧盟委员会继续与北京对话，同时充分运用贸易防卫措施，并增设新的贸易工具以保障欧盟利益。

内容提要：中国共产党正在推动用中华文化和社会主义价值观“滋养”宗教。十多年来，党机关一直使用这种策略来削弱宗教团体的组织和精神独立性，这是党国学者用来描述宗教中国化的四个机制之一。 “饱和”创造了新的与党一致的规范，必须遵循这些规范以避免迫害。它需要通过基层检查和技术手段进行监督，以确保合规性。在缺乏国家宗教法规的情况下，地方政府多年来仅在党的指导下开展中国化运动。然而，《促进民族团结进步法》包含一些与宗教相关的条款，将导致新的努力。在2026年上海宗教界中华文化周开幕式上，上海天主教堂沉斌主教介绍了“中华文化渗透宗教倡议”（澎湃新闻7月17日）。 “开放”一词是指将中华文化和中国特色社会主义融入宗教，成为宗教中国化的一种机制。
2023年，中国社会科学院世界宗教研究室主任郑筱筠将宗教管理概括为“导”、“和”、“润”、“化”（郑，2023）。 [1]每一种策略都为中国共产党（CCP）通过统战部（UFWD）和地方民族宗教事务办公室（ERA）实现宗教中国化提供了框架。在许多党和国家的指示和报告中，多种策略被引用为党的宗教工作的目的或手段，郑的启发有助于表明中国化是多方面的。 “饱和”尤其说明了中共强制社会主义与宗教的融合，使得宗教团体的独立性在组织上和精神上都受到侵蚀。自2015年统战工作会议以来，党和国家的宗教事务工作明确走中国化道路，习近平总书记指出宗教“必须坚持中国化方向”（《人民日报》，2025年5月21日）。最近颁布的《促进民族团结进步法》随后规范了中华人民共和国（PRC）各地零星的汉化方法，这可能会导致新的努力（中国简报，3月27日、4月2日）。
民族团结法以涉及宗教的方式扩展了现有程序，特别是在家庭和学校中政党结盟的授权方面；但省、县、市政府不需要针对宗教制定全国性法律。以前，在没有广泛的全国性法规的情况下，党的指导足以开展中国化工作，十多年来党机关一直通过“饱和”推进中国化，地方政府执行指导。地方文件显示“饱和”努力“饱和”是重塑宗教、将中国特色社会主义融入个人身份的尝试。书籍捐赠让宗教图书馆充满了社会主义和党的文献，例如习近平谈治国理政

【原文 English Original】
Executive Summary: The Chinese Communist Party (CCP) is pushing to “saturate” (浸润) religion with Chinese culture and socialist values. Party organs have used this tactic for more than a decade to wear down the organizational and spiritual independence of religious groups, and it is one of four mechanisms in a framework Party-state scholars use to describe the sinicization of religion. “Saturation” creates new Party-aligned norms that must be followed to avoid persecution. It demands surveillance, both through grassroots inspections and through technical means to ensure compliance. Local governments have run sinicization campaigns for years following Party guidance alone in the absence of a national statute on religion. However, the Promotion of Ethnic Unity and Progress Law contains some provisions relevant to religion and will lead to renewed efforts. At the opening ceremony of the 2026 Shanghai Religious Community Chinese Culture Week, Shen Bin (沈斌), the bishop of the Catholic Church of Shanghai, introduced the “Initiative on Chinese Culture Saturating Religion” ( The Paper , July 17). The term “saturate” (浸润) refers to the integration of Chinese culture—and socialism with Chinese characteristics—into religion, acting as one mechanism for the sinicization of religion. In 2023, Zheng Xiaoyun (郑筱筠), director of the department of world religion research at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences, characterized the management of religion as consisting of “导” (guidance), “和” (harmonization), “润” (saturation), and “化” (transformation) (Zheng, 2023). [1] Each tactic provides a framework for the Chinese Communist Party (CCP) to sinicize religion through its United Front Work Department (UFWD) and local ethnic and religious affairs (ERA) offices. In many Party-state directives and reports, multiple tactics are cited as the ends or means of the Party’s religious work, and Zheng’s heuristic is useful in showing that sinicization is multi-faceted. “Saturation” is particularly illustrative of the CCP’s mandatory integration between socialism and religion, such that the independence of religious groups is both organizationally and spiritually eroded. The Party-state’s religious affairs work has explicitly followed the path of sinicization since the United Front Work Conference in 2015, when General Secretary Xi Jinping said that religion “must adhere” to this direction (必须坚持中国化方向) ( People’s Daily , May 21, 2025). The recently enacted Promotion of Ethnic Unity and Progress Law then standardized the sporadic approaches to sinicization across the People’s Republic of China (PRC), which will likely lead to renewed efforts (China Brief, March 27 , April 2 ). The ethnic unity law expands on existing procedure in ways that touch religion, especially regarding mandates on Party alignment in the home and in schools; but provincial, county, and municipal governments do not need a national law to target religion. Party guidance previously sufficed to carry out sinicization efforts in the absence of a wide-ranging national statute, and Party organs have been promoting sinicization through “saturation” for over a decade, with local governments executing their guidance. Local Documents Show ‘Saturation’ Efforts “Saturation” is an attempt to reshape religion and integrate socialism with Chinese characteristics into personal identity. Book donations fill religious libraries with socialist and Party-aligned literature, such as Xi Jinping’s Talks on Governance and Regulations on Religious Affairs . ERA committees also install flagpoles and put up propaganda posters. Shenyang City boasted donations of more than 2,000 books and more than 500 national flags in the years leading up to 2020 ( Liaoning ERA Committee , December 18, 2020). Party-guided education in history also plays a role in reshaping identity. In the northeast region, studying the Korean War is cited as helping to “cultivate the patriotism of the religious community, sharpen the ambition of strengthening the country, and practice service to the country” (培养深植宗教界爱国之情、砥砺强国之志、实践报国之行) ( Liaoning ERA Committee , December 18, 2020). In Hubei province, the ERA committee celebrated the “Hubei Religious Community ‘Red Education’ Base,” a historical showcase that celebrates the CCP and its sinicization efforts ( Hubei ERA Committee , April 24, 2022). The PRC’s Patriotic Education Law calls for developing and visiting these sites ( China Brief , December 15, 2023). What the CCP calls “excellent traditional Chinese culture” (中华优秀传统文化) provides yet another vector for influencing religious identity. In Hubei and elsewhere, religious sites will hold traditional festival celebrations and recitations of the Chinese classics ( Hubei ERA Committee , April 24, 2022). Along with legal measures, using traditional culture for religious sinicization establishes that “the nation is greater than religion” (国大于教) ( UFWD , May 19). Xu Xiaohong (徐晓鸿), chairman of the National Committee of the Three-Self Patriotic Movement, a state-sanctioned body that oversees Protestant churches in the PRC, put this in a zero-sum context, saying that sinicization is a modern effort to prevent a reality where “one more Christian is one fewer Chinese” (多一个基督徒就少一个中国人) ( Xinhua , March 11, 2019). This indicates that the fusion of religion and secular culture is an attempt to maintain a solely “Chinese” identity. “Saturation” of religion also calls for the Party to influence theology itself. This can occur indirectly from book donations and ideological education, but is achieved more directly by encouraging religious leaders to align their messaging with the CCP. In Zhengzhou, the Protestant liang hui (两会) held a competition soliciting sinicized sermon manuscripts, and reportedly received 461 submissions ( Zhengzhou ERA Bureau , July 9, 2024).  [2] Sinicized sermons have covered themes such as “taking dedication to work as a sacrifice” (以敬业为祭) and “being a patriotic Muslim” (做一名具有爱国情怀的穆斯林) (China Islamic Steering Committee, 2021; The Protestant Church in China , July 1).  [3] For these religious leaders, contests provided an incentive for alignment, but they also serve the CCP’s goal of bringing ideology into churches. The Party-state’s tactics of identifying, cultivating, and co-opting willing religious leaders to advance its “saturation” of religion mirrors its work in overseas united front operations ( China Brief , February 11). ‘Saturation’ Demands Grassroots and Technical Surveillance Governing religion through “saturation” creates ideological norms that must then be upheld by religious followers. In Pengxi county, located in Sichuan province, cadre inspections include “heart-to-heart talks” (谈心谈话) and soliciting opinions before meetings. This is an attempt to increase “ideological contact” (思想碰触), and forces Christians, Muslims, and Buddhists to embrace ideology or be marked as anti-CCP elements ( Pengxi County UFWD , July 28, 2023). Sending cadres into religious sites serves as a tool for monitoring religion and identifying the people, ideas, and value systems that threaten the Party’s interests. The experience of Uyghurs in the Xinjiang Uyghur Autonomous Region (XUAR), where indicators of religious extremism came to be defined so expansively as to include growing a beard or maintaining foreign contacts, shows how Party narratives shape what is tolerated and what is seen as religious fanaticism ( United Nations , August 31, 2022). The Party-state uses grassroots means to identify areas of interest and concentrate its monitoring efforts. In Jincheng, Shanxi province, the municipal united front work report discussed “targeted surveys and assessments covering villages with concentrated religious populations” and “foreign religious influences,” seeking to “fortify defenses against religious infiltration and expansion in key sectors and regarding specific religious groups” by “firmly grasping the city’s religious data” (对信教群众聚居村、外来宗教和教育系统开展专项摸排，全面掌握全市宗教数据，筑牢重点领域、重点宗教抵御渗透蔓延的防线) ( Taixing Daily , February 28, 2022). In a sub-district of Wuxi City, “grid staff” (网格员) must conduct inspections of religious sites daily and maintain a registration ledger of religious leaders ( Wuxi ERA Bureau , January 21). A local government in Anhui province also made reference to inspections by “grid staff” and “work ledgers,” where this refers to a report on investigative findings ( Suncun Township Government , June 3, 2020). The same inspection and monitoring tactics are used to identify “underground” religious sites. In advance of the 100th anniversary of the CCP’s founding in 2021, a local government in Huoqiu county, Anhui province, distributed an internal directive to villages and local bureaus. Party branches were ordered to inspect village units, shops, supermarkets, and hotels to identify unauthorized gathering points, including home-based gatherings ( Wulong Town Party Committee and Government Office , 2021). The document names “core members” (骨干分子) of “underground” churches that had previously been broken up, both as subjects for long-term monitoring and nodes within continuous investigations to ensure that their organizations do not return. At least during this “Large-Scale Inspection and Rectification Campaign” (大排查大整治行动), village Party officials were to “provide renewed education and guidance” (再次进行教育引导) for these “core members.” Religion-specific indicators are used to determine threats, reinforcing the Party’s desire to “saturate” and co-opt religious groups. According to a work plan released by Shiti town, located in Dazhou, Sichuan province, the threats emerging from different religions vary, but all must be “checked and changed” (要边查边改) ( Dazhou District People’s Government , September 22, 2018). Buddhists and Taoists are identified as constructing unauthorized temples and statues; the supposed threats in Christianity come from private gatherings, self-appointed preachers, and foreign influence; and for Islam, the Party is concerned by the appointment of imams from the northwest, foreign missions, and illegal classes ( Dazhou District People’s Government , September 22, 2018). These issues are seen as threats because they reflect religion taking on a form that the Party feels is beyond its control. “Saturation” is a way to re-center ideology and Chinese identity. The Party-state turns to technical surveillance to reinforce cadre inspections. In 2022, Zhejiang province’s “religious intelligent patrol” (宗教智巡) used real-time monitoring and early warning to identify three instances of illegal missionary activities, 11 illegal Buddhist events, three illegal renovations, and 49 cases of minors entering religious places ( Daishan County Government Office , August 23, 2022). A document from Nantong, a city in Jiangsu province, shows that video surveillance is ubiquitous, with 534 surveillance cameras outfitted to the city’s 178 religious sites. All video is fed to the county’s “governance command center” (治理指挥中心) that has supposedly “achieved full coverage of site monitoring and no blind spots” (实现场所监控全覆盖、无死角) ( ERA Commission of Jiangsu Province , April 25, 2025). Local Public Security Bureaus in Zhejiang also used the social media app Douyin to identify illegal Christian private gatherings ( Daishan County Government Office , August 23, 2022). Local governments rely on technical platforms built by the private sector. Baotou Pasis Network Technology (包头市派司网络科技), for instance, offers a “smart religion management system” (智慧宗教管理系统) that integrates and analyzes data such as personnel, activities, and finances, in part with assistance from artificial intelligence ( Pasis , accessed October 4).  [4] There are also mobile applications intended to facilitate ERA work, as have emerged across departments in the PRC in recent years ( China Brief , April 28). One, which is offered on Apple’s App Store, is meant to support inspections and assessments ( Apple App Store , accessed October 4). Other companies offer similar products. In 2024, Jiangsu Cable Data Network (江苏有线数据网络) won a bid to provide a digitalized platform for the Jiangsu government, writing in the press release that the project would “actively publicize relevant policies, regulations, and socialist core values through audio and video systems and terminals, and promote the implementation of religious sinicization” (动态宣传相关政策法规和社会主义核心价值观，助力宗教中国化宣贯) ( Jiangsu Cable Data Network , April 24, 2024). Figure 1: AI-enabled video monitoring service advertised by Pasis (Source: Pasis , accessed October 4) Conclusion The CCP describes the threat it faces from unmitigated religious practice, in part, as foreign “infiltration” (渗透), with sinicization as the response. It is difficult to understand sending cadres into religious sites, shaping sermon rhetoric, cultivating ideology, and other aspects of religious “saturation” as anything other than the “infiltration” of religion by the Party itself. By acting against religious groups in much the same way that it describes the threat, the Party expresses its view that religion offers rival value systems and organizations that cannot remain independent. Zero-sum framing, such as Xu Xiaohong’s statement that without sinicization “one more Christian is one fewer Chinese,” only underscores this perspective.   Notes [1] Zheng Xiaoyun [郑筱筠], “‘Guide,’ ‘Harmonize,’ ‘Saturate,’ ‘Transform’: Several Theoretical Reflections on Deepening the Sinicization of Religion in China [‘导’ ‘和’ ‘润’ ‘化’——深入推进我国宗教中国化的几点理论思考],”  Studies in World Religions  [世界宗教研究], no. 7 (2023): 1–10. [2] The term liang hui (两会) refers to the two organizations that manage Protestant churches in the PRC, the Chinese Christian Three-Self Patriotic Movement Committee (中国基督教三自爱国运动委员会) and the Chinese Christian Council (中国基督教协会). [3] China Islamic Affairs Steering Committee [中国伊斯兰教教务指导委员会], ed., New Collection of Wa’z Sermons, Vol. 7 [新编卧尔兹演讲集（第七辑）] (Beijing: Commercial Press [商务印书馆], 2021), https://archive.ph/DJnEL . [4] The company also offers similar services for an “ideological management system” ( Pasis , accessed October 4). # 中国拟限禁AI、生物医药和光伏三领域共40项技术的出口

中国商务部、科技部周五（16日）发布2026年第48号公告，就修订《中国禁止出口限制出口技术目录》（以下简称《目录》）公开征求意见，并对相关技术实施出口前登记的临时管理措施。

发表时间： 16/10/2026 - 16:19

 10 分钟 浏览时间

 中国商务部资料图片 © 美联社图片

 作者： [弗林](https://rfi.fr/cn/%E4%BD%9C%E8%80%85/%E5%BC%97%E6%9E%97/ "弗林")

广告

继续浏览后续

据上述公告介绍，“此次公开征求意见涉及人工智能、生物医药、光伏三个领域40项技术。人工智能领域包括大模型、智能体、算力集群、信息处理相关23项技术；对已通过开源、发表学术论文等方式进入公共领域的技术，不纳入管理范围。生物医药领域包括细胞和基因治疗、小核酸药、病原微生物相关5项技术；对不涉及所有权转让的对外授权模式，适用自动许可等便利措施。光伏领域包括多晶硅制造、硅片制造、电池制造相关12项技术；技术管理范围也包含承载相关技术的关键和核心设备”。

公告指出：“（一）自本公告发布之日起，至《中国禁止出口限制出口技术目录》正式修订并实施之日止，技术出口经营者在出口本公告附件所列技术前，应当在商务部业务系统统一平台技术贸易管理信息应用登记。已经开始但尚未完成的出口，在登记范围内”。

公告提到，“需开展登记的出口情形包括：1.向境外转让技术所有权，如知识产权转让；2.境内技术授权境外使用，如知识产权授权使用；3.境内技术的所有权人或者实际控制人变更为境外主体；4.商务部以通知等形式明确要求登记的其他情形”。消息指，公众可在10月16日-11月15日期间，就新增技术范围、指标、管控政策、便利措施等提出意见。

就上述两部门公布的这一消息，中国商务部新闻发言人以答记者问方式表示，“近年来，人工智能、生物医药和光伏相关技术在敏感领域的应用不断拓展，各主要经济体均实施了不同程度的出口管控。中国参考国际通行做法，依法实施必要的管理，既防范技术失控和不当扩散风险，也保障正常国际技术交流合作，推动科技向上向善、安全可控、造福人类”。

就《目录》拟新增技术的范围，该发言人说，“此次公开征求意见涉及拟增列的人工智能、生物医药、光伏三个领域40项关键技术。其中，拟禁止出口技术14项，包括：人工智能驱动的恶意代码生成与变异技术、具有自主知识产权的细胞和基因治疗技术工艺平台、钙钛矿及叠层电池组件生产技术等；拟限制出口技术26项，包括：人工智能辅助漏洞挖掘技术、具有自主知识产权的通用型细胞和基因治疗全新靶点发现和验证技术、单线产能≥3万吨/年的多晶硅工程技术等”。

就拟增列的人工智能技术，主要有哪些考虑，该发言人指出，此次拟将人工智能大模型、智能体、算力集群、信息处理相关23项关键技术增列至《目录》，主要有以下考虑：一是确保人工智能技术安全可控；二是鼓励开源开放、合作共享。该发言人还提到，“中方支持全球南方国家加强人工智能能力建设，弥合数智鸿沟，促进可持续发展。对于世界人工智能合作组织成员间开展能力建设国际合作、技术共享和规则共建所需的技术出口，将提供更多便利和支持”。

就“人工智能大模型在海外本地化部署、向境外提供模型调用等各类‘出海’形式，是否属于技术出口管理范围？” 该发言人则回答说，“判别具体‘出海’情形是否属于技术出口管理的范围，核心在于是否涉及限制类技术从中国境内向境外转移”。

该发言人补充道：“有关措施正式实施后，绝大部分人工智能技术仍可以自由出口。对于纳入限制类的人工智能技术，开展海外本地化部署，属于技术出口管理范围；如果部署在海外自有云等风险相对可控的情形下，可适用自动许可等便利措施。对于企业利用限制类大模型对外提供API调用、APP/网页交互、SaaS应用、本地端侧轻量化部署等情形，不属于大模型技术出口管理范围”。

就拟增列的生物医药技术，该发言人表示，“现行《目录》中已有部分生物医药技术，此次拟增列病原微生物、细胞和基因治疗、小核酸药相关5项技术，主要有以下考虑：一是维护人类生命健康安全；二是支持我国生物医药技术依法依规有序开展国际合作；三是践行人类卫生健康共同体理念”。此外，北京方面此次拟将多晶硅制造、硅片制造、电池制造等环节的12项光伏技术增列至《目录》。
