title: Taiwan drugmaker PharmaEssentia plans US$46 million Puerto Rico plant as it expands global reach - Focus Taiwan
zh_title: 台湾制药商 PharmaEssentia 计划在波多黎各投资 4600 万美元建厂，以扩大全球影响力 - 聚焦台湾
summary: 中新社台北 10 月 17 日电 总部位于台湾的生物制药公司 PharmaEssentia Corp. 正在扩大其全球制造和商业足迹，计划在波多黎各投资 4600 万美元的生产设施于 2027 年开始运营，同时巩固其北美业务，以支持其血癌药物 Ropeginterferon alfa-2b (Ropeg) 的国际增长。该公司表示，此次扩张是其在台湾和美国建立制造基地、增强供应链弹性并支持 Ropeg 在监管部门批准后的全球增长战略的一部分。
content:
中新社台北 10 月 17 日电 总部位于台湾的生物制药公司 PharmaEssentia Corp. 正在扩大其全球制造和商业足迹，计划在波多黎各投资 4600 万美元的生产设施于 2027 年开始运营，同时巩固其北美业务，以支持其血癌药物 Ropeginterferon alfa-2b (Ropeg) 的国际增长。

该公司表示，此次扩张是其战略的一部分，该战略旨在在台湾和美国建立生产基地，增强供应链弹性，并支持 Ropeg 在用于治疗原发性血小板增多症（ET）的药物获得监管部门批准后的全球增长。ET 是一种以血小板生成过多为特征的罕见血液癌症。

据该公司称，PharmaEssentia 董事会于 2026 年 2 月批准了对波多黎各子公司的 4600 万美元投资，并于 3 月签署了新工厂的投资协议。

该工厂位于波多黎各 Toa Baja，预计将于 2027 年开始运营，但需获得监管部门批准。 PharmaEssentia 表示，该工厂的设计将遵循 PharmaEssentia 位于台湾中部台中的制造工厂的质量标准，当地员工计划在台湾接受培训，作为技术转让过程的一部分。

该公司表示，扩大台湾以外的制造能力将有助于分散生产风险并增强其全球供应链的弹性。
PharmaEssentia还于6月以3650万美元完成了对加拿大制药公司FORUS Therapeutics Inc.的收购，获得其100%的股份。 PharmaEssentia表示，此次收购将使公司能够整合两家企业的团队和资源，扩大在加拿大的业务，并建立更广泛的北美运营平台。

此次海外投资是为了扩大Ropeg的应用范围，该产品以BESREMi品牌销售，该品牌由PharmaEssentia创始人兼首席执行官林国钟开发。

据PharmaEssentia称，Lin开发的Ropeg采用专有的聚乙二醇化技术和先进的小分子合成技术，将聚乙二醇（PEG）与干扰素α连接起来，生产出化学结构稳定、成分均匀的长效干扰素。

Ropeg 于 2019 年在欧盟首次被批准用于治疗真性红细胞增多症 (PV)，这是另一种被归类为骨髓增生性肿瘤 (MPN) 的罕见血癌，随后于 2021 年在美国和 2023 年在日本获得批准。该公司表示，此后已在大约 50 个国家获得批准并推出用于真性红细胞增多症的治疗。

2026 年 5 月，台湾批准 Ropeg 用于对羟基脲治疗耐药或不耐受的成人 ET 患者。据该公司称，日本和美国随后于 8 月获得批准。
PharmaEssentia 表示，Ropeg 是美国食品和药物管理局 (FDA) 近三十年来批准的第一种治疗 ET 的新疗法，也是目前该机构批准的唯一一种同时治疗 ET 和 PV 的药物。

该公司表示，临床试验表明，与派罗欣（一种传统的聚乙二醇干扰素疗法）每周一次的标准治疗方案相比，Ropeg 可以每两周注射一次，注射频率较低。

PharmaEssentia 表示，该公司还在其 3 期 SURPASS-ET 和 2 期单臂 EXCEED-ET 临床试验中采用了优化的高初始剂量加速滴定 (HIDAT) 方案。

【原文 English Original】
Taipei, Oct. 17 (CNA) Taiwan-based biopharmaceutical company PharmaEssentia Corp. is expanding its global manufacturing and commercial footprint, planning a US$46 million production facility in Puerto Rico to begin operations in 2027 while consolidating its North American business to support the international growth of its blood cancer drug ropeginterferon alfa-2b (Ropeg).

The company said the expansion is part of its strategy to establish manufacturing bases in Taiwan and the United States, strengthen supply chain resilience and support Ropeg's global growth following regulatory approvals for the drug to treat essential thrombocythemia (ET), a rare blood cancer characterized by excessive platelet production.

PharmaEssentia's board approved the US$46 million investment in a Puerto Rico subsidiary in February 2026, and the company signed an investment agreement for the new facility in March, according to the company.

Located in Toa Baja, Puerto Rico, the plant is expected to begin operations in 2027, subject to regulatory approvals. It will be designed to follow the quality standards of PharmaEssentia's manufacturing facility in central Taiwan's Taichung, with local staff scheduled to receive training in Taiwan as part of the technology transfer process, PharmaEssentia said.

The company said expanding manufacturing capacity outside Taiwan would help diversify production risks and strengthen the resilience of its global supply chain.

PharmaEssentia also completed the acquisition of Canadian pharmaceutical company FORUS Therapeutics Inc. in June for US$36.5 million, acquiring 100 percent of its shares. PharmaEssentia said the acquisition will enable the company to integrate the two businesses' teams and resources, expand its presence in Canada and build a broader North American operating platform.

The overseas investments come as the company expands the applications of Ropeg, marketed under the brand name BESREMi, which was developed by PharmaEssentia founder and CEO Lin Ko-chung (林國鐘).

Lin developed Ropeg using proprietary PEGylation technology and advanced small-molecule synthesis techniques to link polyethylene glycol (PEG) to interferon alfa, producing a long-acting interferon with a stable chemical structure and uniform composition, according to PharmaEssentia.

Ropeg was first approved to treat polycythemia vera (PV), another rare blood cancer classified as a myeloproliferative neoplasm (MPN), in the European Union in 2019, followed by the United States in 2021 and Japan in 2023. It has since been approved and launched for PV treatment in approximately 50 countries, the company said.

In May 2026, Taiwan approved Ropeg for adult ET patients resistant to or intolerant of hydroxyurea treatment. Japan and the United States followed with approvals in August, according to the company.

PharmaEssentia said Ropeg is the first new treatment approved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) for ET in nearly three decades and the only drug currently approved by the agency to treat both ET and PV.

Clinical trials have shown that Ropeg can be administered once every two weeks, compared with the standard once-weekly regimen for Pegasys, a conventional pegylated interferon therapy, offering a less frequent injection schedule, the company said.

PharmaEssentia said it had also adopted an optimized High-Initial-Dose Accelerated Titration (HIDAT) regimen in both its Phase 3 SURPASS-ET and Phase 2 single-arm EXCEED-ET clinical trials, allowing patients to reach the target dose more quickly.

Under the HIDAT regimen, the initial dose of 250 micrograms is increased to 350 micrograms in the second week and to the target dose of 500 micrograms by the fourth week, it said.

Meanwhile, the company said it is conducting a global Phase 3 clinical trial, HOPE-PMF, to evaluate Ropeg as a potential treatment for primary myelofibrosis (PMF), another rare blood cancer with limited treatment options.

The study focuses on patients with early-stage PMF, who are typically monitored without treatment because no drug therapies are approved for this stage of the disease, PharmaEssentia said.

From PV and ET to PMF, PharmaEssentia said it is expanding its MPN portfolio, hoping to bring accessible treatment options to more patients worldwide.

Founded in 2003, PharmaEssentia specializes in biologics for hematologic cancers and has developed capabilities spanning drug discovery, clinical trials, manufacturing and global commercialization.

The company said its experience holds broader significance for Taiwan's biotechnology industry, demonstrating how home-grown drug candidates can reach international markets when research, manufacturing, regulatory and commercial capabilities are developed in tandem.

Since 2017, PharmaEssentia has established subsidiaries in the United States, Japan, Hong Kong, China, South Korea and Singapore, while expanding into Europe and Latin America through licensing partnerships.

In 2026, PharmaEssentia's market capitalization approached US$20 billion, making it Taiwan's only biotechnology company among the country's 50 largest listed companies by market value.

(By Ho Hsiu-ling and Chen Chia-yu)

title: Seditious display homemaker gets three-month hospital order
zh_title: 煽动性展示家庭主妇获得三个月的住院令
summary: 香港 一名患有精神分裂症的 61 岁家庭主妇因在天水围公屋外发表煽动性材料而被判入院三个月。法官统治殖民时代的旗帜和抗议口号，显示出挑战中国主权的意图 [![图1：Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk) 作者：[Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk),主编 香港时间 2026 年 10 月 16 日 18:01 · 阅读 2 分钟 一名 61 岁家庭主妇患精神分裂症被判入狱
content:
香港
一名患有精神分裂症的 61 岁家庭主妇因在其天水围公屋外发表煽动性材料而被判入院三个月。法官裁定殖民时代的旗帜和抗议口号显示出挑战中国主权的意图

[![图片1：Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)

作者：[Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)，主编

2026 年 10 月 16 日，香港时间 18:01 · 阅读 2 分钟

一名患有精神分裂症的 61 岁家庭主妇因故意在其天水围公屋住所外发表及展示煽动性物品，被西九龙裁判法院判处三个月住院令。

首席裁判官苏文龙宣判，认为杨秋基在2024年3月至2024年11月期间公开展示的殖民时代旗帜、抗议口号和书面言论的累积影响，表明其明显意图挑战中国对香港的主权权威。
根据国家安全法，杨面临一项故意出版或展示煽动性出版物的罪名，涉及她在天颂苑颂锦楼的公寓内实施的行为。据检方称，她在前门、客厅窗户和公寓外的公共走廊墙上贴上了殖民地香港旗帜、英联邦旗帜和印有抗议口号的文件。

被告出庭辩护，表示自己不认罪，并作证称，她的行为完全是出于与小区物业管理人员和保安人员的个人纠纷。她声称自己没有任何煽动目的，并认为安全人员会在路人看到这些材料之前立即将其移走。
苏裁判官在作出裁决时表示，虽然法庭接纳她对屋村员工有不满，但所展示的内容远远超出了标准的管理投诉。法官指出，杨女士没有提出改善服务的建设性建议，并指出，如果她无意向公众展示这些标语，她本可以将它们保留在她的私人住所内。苏裁判官裁定，在外部走廊和窗户上贴上大型彩色材料，表明她很清楚其他人会看到这些材料，反映出其意图煽动对宪政制度的不满，并质疑中央政府的主权管辖权。

提交给法庭的精神评估显示，杨患有精神分裂症，并伴有疑似妄想症状，但法医证实她的精神状态仍然适合认罪并接受审判。法院获悉，杨此前曾有两起互不相关的前科，在成为家庭主妇之前曾在保险、化妆品和安全行业工作过。

在她的减刑请求中，她表示她与小儿子住在一起并照顾她，并补充说她持续的关节疼痛在拘留期间恶化了。苏法官接受了两项独立精神评估的建议，得出结论认为有必要进行强制医疗，并下令将杨拘留三个月。

【原文 English Original】
Hong Kong
A 61-year-old homemaker with schizophrenia was sentenced to a three-month hospital order after being found guilty of publishing seditious materials outside her Tin Shui Wai public housing flat. The magistrate ruled the colonial-era flags and protest slogans showed intent to challenge China's soverei

[![Image 1: Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)

By [Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk), Editor in Chief

16 Oct 2026 at 18:01 HKT · 2 min read

A 61-year-old homemaker suffering from schizophrenia was sentenced to a three-month hospital order at West Kowloon Magistrates' Courts after being found guilty of knowingly publishing and displaying seditious materials outside her Tin Shui Wai public housing residence.

Principal Magistrate Don So Man-lung delivered the verdict, finding that the cumulative impact of colonial-era flags, protest slogans, and written statements publicly displayed by Yang Chau-kei between March and November 2024 demonstrated a clear intention to challenge China's sovereign authority over Hong Kong.

Yang faced one count of knowingly publishing or displaying seditious publications under national security legislation, covering acts committed at her flat in Chung Kam House at Tin Chung Court. According to the prosecution, she affixed colonial Hong Kong flags, Commonwealth flags, and papers featuring protest slogans on her front entrance, living room windows, and the public corridor wall outside her apartment.

The defendant, who represented herself at trial, pleaded not guilty and testified that her actions were solely motivated by personal disputes with property management personnel and security guards at the residential estate. She asserted that she lacked any seditious purpose and presumed that security staff would promptly remove the materials before passers-by could see them.

Delivering his ruling, Magistrate So stated that while the court accepted she harbored grievances against estate staff, the displayed content far exceeded a standard management complaint. The magistrate observed that Yang included no constructive suggestions for service improvements and noted that had she not intended to display the slogans to the public, she could have kept them inside her private living quarters. Magistrate So ruled that affixing large, multi-colored materials across exterior corridors and windows indicated that she was well aware others would see them, reflecting an intent to incite dissatisfaction against the constitutional system and dispute the central government's sovereign jurisdiction.

Psychiatric assessments presented to the court revealed that Yang suffered from schizophrenia alongside suspected delusional symptoms, though medical examiners confirmed she remained mentally fit to enter a plea and face trial. The court heard that Yang had two prior unrelated convictions and had previously worked in the insurance, cosmetics, and security sectors before becoming a homemaker.

In her mitigation plea, she stated that she lived with and cared for her younger son, adding that her ongoing joint pain had worsened during her period in custody. Accepting the recommendations of two independent psychiatric evaluations, Magistrate So concluded that compulsory medical treatment was necessary and ordered Yang detained under a three-month hospital order.

title: Hong Kong Science Museum showcases 2026 Future Science Prize laureates' work
zh_title: 香港科学馆展示2026年未来科学奖得奖者作品
summary: 香港 香港科学馆举办展览，展示今年未来科学奖获奖者的作品，涵盖生命科学、材料科学和数学。互动展览探讨密码学、乙型肝炎感染和单原子催化，并安排科学峰会 [![图片 1: Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk) 主编 [Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk) 2026 年 10 月 16 日，香港时间 15:45 · 阅读 2 分钟 香港科学馆推出「2026 未来科学园」
content:
香港
香港科学馆举办展览，展示今年未来科学奖获奖者的作品，涵盖生命科学、材料科学和数学。互动展览探讨密码学、乙型肝炎感染和单原子催化，并安排了一场科学峰会

[![图片1：Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)

作者：[Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)，主编

香港时间 2026 年 10 月 16 日 15:45 · 阅读时间 2 分钟

香港科学馆推出“2026未来科学奖展览”，展示今年获奖者的研究成果。未来科学奖设立于2016年，每年三届奖励中国大陆、港澳台地区杰出科学成就的科学家，旨在用科学精神激励中国、世界和子孙后代。

今年的生命科学奖颁给了张宏博士，以表彰他在揭示多细胞生物特有的自噬机制及其生理功能方面做出的开创性贡献。材料科学奖授予赵东源教授，以表彰他在介孔材料方面的开创性工作，包括受控合成、机理理解和工业应用。袁新一教授因其对算术几何的基础性贡献而荣获数学与计算机科学奖。
该展览以多种多媒体和互动装置为特色，以通俗易懂的方式解释了之前获奖项目背后的科学原理，包括密码学、催化和肝炎病毒。 “数字指纹实验室”让参观者体验密码学的防伪威力，探索2019年数学与计算机科学奖获得者王晓云教授的研究领域。互动展览展示了乙型肝炎病毒感染肝细胞的机制，展示了2022年生命科学奖获得者李文辉教授的突破性研究，他发现了乙型肝炎和丁型肝炎病毒如何利用人体肝细胞上的特定受体。通过“催化反应模拟器”，参观者可以了解2024年材料科学奖获得者张涛教授和李亚东教授的单原子催化研究，以及这种方法如何提高工业效率。

展览期间，将举办“2026未来科学大奖周”，其重头戏“科学峰会”将于11月6日至7日在博物馆报告厅举行。世界知名科学家将分享前沿研究成果。详情请浏览hk.science.museum/tc/web/scm/exhibition/fsp.html。

Hong Kong
The Hong Kong Science Museum has opened an exhibition featuring the work of this year's Future Science Prize winners, covering life science, material science and mathematics. Interactive exhibits explore cryptography, hepatitis B infection and single-atom catalysis, with a science summit scheduled f

[![Image 1: Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)

By [Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk), Editor in Chief

16 Oct 2026 at 15:45 HKT · 2 min read

The Hong Kong Science Museum has launched the "2026 Future Science Prize Exhibition", showcasing the research achievements of this year's laureates. The Future Science Prize, established in 2016, presents three annual awards to scientists from mainland China, Hong Kong, Macau and Taiwan for outstanding scientific accomplishments, aiming to inspire China, the world and future generations through scientific spirit.

This year's Life Science Prize goes to Dr Zhang Hong for his pioneering contributions in revealing the autophagy mechanisms unique to multicellular organisms and their physiological functions. The Material Science Prize is awarded to Professor Zhao Dongyuan for his groundbreaking work on mesoporous materials, including controlled synthesis, mechanistic understanding and industrial applications. Professor Yuan Xinyi receives the Mathematics and Computer Science Prize for his foundational contributions to arithmetic geometry.

The exhibition features multiple multimedia and interactive installations that explain in accessible terms the science behind previous prize-winning projects, including cryptography, catalysis and hepatitis viruses. The "Digital Fingerprint Laboratory" lets visitors experience the anti-counterfeiting power of cryptography, exploring the research field of Professor Wang Xiaoyun, winner of the 2019 Mathematics and Computer Science Prize. An interactive exhibit on the mechanism of hepatitis B virus infection of liver cells presents the breakthrough research of Professor Li Wenhui, the 2022 Life Science Prize winner, who discovered how specific receptors on human liver cells are exploited by hepatitis B and D viruses. Through the "Catalysis Reaction Simulator", visitors can learn about the single-atom catalysis research of Professor Zhang Tao and Professor Li Yadong, winners of the 2024 Material Science Prize, and how this approach improves industrial efficiency.

During the exhibition period, the "2026 Future Science Prize Week" will be held, with its highlight event, the "Science Summit", taking place on 6 and 7 November at the museum's lecture hall. World-renowned scientists will share cutting-edge research findings. Details are available at hk.science.museum/tc/web/scm/exhibition/fsp.html.

# Pakistan companies move into lithium battery assembly with China partners

Rapid influx of Chinese solar panel boosts Pakistani demand for rechargeable power

Pakistan Inc. and its Chinese partners are preparing to assemble lithium-ion batteries domestically despite the local average price of the power packs having fallen by half since 2024 "due to a global price decline and overproduction by China," according to one analyst. (Nikkei montage/Source photos by AP and Reuters)

ADNAN AAMIR

October 16, 2026 11:47 JST

Listen

English (Original)

[](https://twitter.com/share?text=Pakistan+companies+move+into+lithium+battery+assembly+with+China+partners&url=https%3A%2F%2Fasia.nikkei.com%2Fbusiness%2Fbusiness-trends%2Fpakistan-companies-move-into-lithium-battery-assembly-with-china-partners&via=NikkeiAsia)[](https://www.facebook.com/sharer/sharer.php?u=https%3A%2F%2Fasia.nikkei.com%2Fbusiness%2Fbusiness-trends%2Fpakistan-companies-move-into-lithium-battery-assembly-with-china-partners)[](https://api.whatsapp.com/send?text=Pakistan+companies+move+into+lithium+battery+assembly+with+China+partners+https%3A%2F%2Fasia.nikkei.com%2Fbusiness%2Fbusiness-trends%2Fpakistan-companies-move-into-lithium-battery-assembly-with-china-partners)[](https://t.me/share/url?text=Pakistan+companies+move+into+lithium+battery+assembly+with+China+partners&url=https%3A%2F%2Fasia.nikkei.com%2Fbusiness%2Fbusiness-trends%2Fpakistan-companies-move-into-lithium-battery-assembly-with-china-partners)[](mailto:?subject=Pakistan%20companies%20move%20into%20lithium%20battery%20assembly%20with%20China%20partners&body=https%3A%2F%2Fasia.nikkei.com%2Fbusiness%2Fbusiness-trends%2Fpakistan-companies-move-into-lithium-battery-assembly-with-china-partners)

ISLAMABAD -- Chinese solar panels are pouring into Pakistan, fueling demand for lithium-ion batteries and persuading local companies to partner with Chinese manufacturers to assemble the power packs domestically, even as prices plunge globally and insiders predict they will fall even further.

ME Solar Energy, a Karachi-based solar power solutions company, is setting up an assembly plant in the city through a tie-up with China's Contemporary Amperex Technology Co., Ltd. (CATL). With a $15 million investment and technical support from CATL, the plant will be operational in March and able to produce 10,000 5-kilowatt lithium-ion batteries per month, ME Solar CEO Zubair Ahmed told Nikkei Asia.

ME Solar Energy is not alone.

Advertisement

According to disclosures submitted to the Pakistan Stock Exchange, Treet Battery, a subsidiary of blade and razor manufacturer Treet Corporation, is planning to set up a lithium-ion battery assembly plant with China's Contemporary Nebula Technology Energy. Also, Kohinoor Energy, an Islamabad-based independent power producer, plans to build a battery assembly plant in partnership with China's Hebei Juhang Energy Technology Group.

The companies aim to capture growing local demand for lithium-ion batteries that foreign suppliers currently feed.

According to United Nations data, Pakistan's imports of lithium-ion electric accumulators, or rechargeable batteries, jumped nearly threefold to $171 million in 2025 from $60 million the previous year, with China accounting for $167 million. Ember, a U.K.-based think tank that compiles Chinese customs data, says that, in a broader category, these battery imports from China rose to $294.3 million in 2025 from $147.1 million in 2024. In the first eight months of this year, these imports came to $537.2 million.

"The clearest industrial opportunity is therefore not simply to import more batteries; it is to move part of the engineering, assembly, testing and integration value chain into Pakistan," the Pakistan Solar Association said in a recent report.

Industry insiders say China's Dongjin Group has operated a battery factory in Karachi since 2021, producing lithium-ion batteries on a limited scale. But Pakistani companies and their Chinese partners are now venturing into battery assembly one after another as a solar boom spreads across the country.

According to Ember, Pakistan was the second-largest importer of Chinese solar panels in 2025, up from fifth in 2023, behind the Netherlands, and imports of Chinese panels hit a record high of 16.86 gigawatts in 2025, more than double 2023. The World Nuclear Industry Status Report 2026, authored by a group of independent analysts, says Pakistan generated an estimated 36.3 terawatt-hours of power from solar panels in 2025, 60% more than from reactors.

Higher electricity tariffs and declining grid reliability are pushing people to install solar panels, which need rechargeable batteries to store the energy they collect.

"Pakistan's battery market could [create] a multibillion-dollar industrial opportunity," Osama Rizvi, a global market and product strategist at Primary Vision, a U.S.-based energy market consultancy, told Nikkei Asia. "At current import volumes, even capturing a fraction would support skilled employment and domestic industry," he said.

However, declining local battery prices could cap revenues for companies now preparing assembly plants. Ahmed of ME Solar Energy said the local average price of a basic 5-kw battery has halved since 2024 to $720 "due to a global price decline and overproduction by China" and, if a new assembly plant becomes operational in Pakistan, the average price "could fall by 18%" to $590.

Experts also warn that Pakistan cannot afford to consider integrated production of lithium-ion batteries beyond assembly.

"Assembly is relatively feasible in the short term, but manufacturing battery cells requires significant capital, technological expertise, and economies of scale," Khalid Waleed, a research fellow at the Sustainable Development Policy Institute in Islamabad, told Nikkei Asia.

Vaqar Ahmed, an Islamabad-based economist, agrees, saying Pakistan's market cannot afford to move to "full cell manufacturing," as it "requires a market size and capital intensity." He added that the realistic near-term approach is "capturing assembly, integration and warranty value rather than cell production," meaning embedding the battery cell in a comprehensive system and after-sales services.

[![图片1：Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)

作者：[Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)，主编

香港时间 2026 年 10 月 15 日 19:13 · 阅读时间 2 分钟

汇丰银行一位高级管理人员周四表示，未来两到三年内，汇丰银行将把其香港人工智能 (AI) 团队的规模从 150 名专家扩大一倍至约 300 名。

汇丰银行亚洲及中东地区联席首席执行官廖亦坚表示，该行的技术和人工智能专家分布在香港、英国和其他主要市场。该团队开发了工具来帮助客户经理与客户互动并提高客户服务中心的案件处理质量。

廖还援引集团首席执行官Georges Elhedery的话说，汇丰银行将在香港设立全球人工智能研究院，预计于2027年初开始运营。该研究院初期将专注于人工智能应用案例、后量子密码学和区块链技术。
廖在接受记者采访时表示，香港是集团的本土市场，自然也是高管的基地。该集团运营委员会的四名成员、区域运营委员会成员和各级高管均驻扎在这座城市，他将其描述为集团的中央决策引擎和未来的全球人工智能发展中心。

他补充说，香港资本和财富管理市场充满活力，集团拥有庞大的客户基础和业务增长，有信心在香港部署更多技术和前线员工。

针对有媒体报道香港金管局质疑汇丰为何将人工智能中心设在新加坡而不是香港，廖重申香港是汇丰亚太和中东地区的决策中心，也是科技和人工智能人才的大本营。他表示，该行继续在香港投资，虽然在中国大陆和伦敦设有人工智能团队，但应用程序的整体领导地位位于香港。他指出，该集团与监管机构有着积极、频繁的沟通。

廖表示，汇丰银行在香港金融管理局第二阶段生成式人工智能沙箱下成功测试了两个用例：一个使用生成式人工智能将文本转换为手语，另一个用于预防欺诈，在 eKYC 流程中检测与深度伪造相关的金融诈骗。
他还表示，相信分别在香港和深圳举行的亚太经合组织财长会议和领导人非正式会议将鼓励更多对话和透明度，该组织将积极参与。

HSBC's Asia and Middle East co-CEO says the bank will double its 150-strong Hong Kong artificial intelligence team within two to three years, and will set up a global AI research institute in the city in early 2027. The bank has tested two generative AI use cases under Hong Kong's regulatory sandbox

[![Image 1: Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)

By [Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk), Editor in Chief

15 Oct 2026 at 19:13 HKT · 2 min read

HSBC will double the size of its artificial intelligence (AI) team in Hong Kong from 150 specialists to about 300 within the next two to three years, a senior executive said on Thursday.

Liao Yi-kin, co-chief executive of HSBC for Asia and the Middle East, said the bank's technology and AI specialists are based in Hong Kong, Britain and other major markets. The team has developed tools to help relationship managers interact with clients and to improve the quality of case handling at customer service centres.

Liao also cited group chief executive Georges Elhedery as saying that HSBC will establish a global AI research institute in Hong Kong, expected to begin operations in early 2027. The institute will initially focus on AI application cases, post-quantum cryptography and blockchain technology.

Speaking to reporters, Liao said Hong Kong is the group's home market and naturally serves as the base for senior executives. Four members of the group's operating committee, members of the regional operating committee and executives at various levels are based in the city, which he described as the group's central decision-making engine and a future global hub for AI development.

He added that Hong Kong has a vibrant capital and wealth management market, and the group has a large client base and business growth, giving it confidence to deploy more technology and frontline staff in the city.

Responding to media reports that the Hong Kong Monetary Authority had questioned why HSBC placed its AI centre in Singapore rather than Hong Kong, Liao reiterated that Hong Kong is the group's decision-making hub for Asia Pacific and the Middle East and a stronghold for technology and AI personnel. He said the bank continues to invest in Hong Kong, and while it has AI teams in mainland China and London, the overall leadership of applications is based in Hong Kong. He noted the group has positive and frequent communication with regulators.

Liao said HSBC successfully tested two use cases under the Hong Kong Monetary Authority's second phase generative AI sandbox: one using generative AI to convert text into sign language, and another on fraud prevention that detects deepfake-related financial scams in the eKYC process.

He also said he believed the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation finance ministers' meeting and leaders' informal meeting, to be held in Hong Kong and Shenzhen respectively, would encourage more dialogue and transparency, and that the group would participate actively.

title: Former US official praises Taiwan’s drills transformation
summary: ## ENGAGING PARTNERS: Dennis Blair called for greater international cooperation to enhance early-warning capabilities and for partners to maintain maritime presence Dennis Blair, former US director of national intelligence and a retired US
content:
## ENGAGING PARTNERS: Dennis Blair called for greater international cooperation to enhance early-warning capabilities and for partners to maintain maritime presence

Dennis Blair, former US director of national intelligence and a retired US Navy admiral, yesterday praised Taiwan’s decision to transform its large-scale annual military exercises into a whole-of-society defense effort in the past few years.

Speaking virtually at a security conference in Taipei, Blair said that Taiwan’s decision to transform the Han Kuang exercises from “a purely military one” into what he described as a “nation-defensive exercise” was a great decision.

By doing so, Taiwan would be “making sure that all of the capabilities of Taiwan are mobilized and brought to bear,” said Blair, a former commander in chief of the US Pacific Command before retiring in 2002.

## Former US director of national intelligence and retired US Navy admiral Dennis Blair, on the screen, speaks virtually at the International Conference on Sea Lane Security held by the Ocean Affairs Council in Taipei yesterday.

Photo: Wang Kuan-jen, Taipei Times

He said that Taiwan’s all-out effort to demonstrate its determination to defend itself would help convince like-minded countries and regional partners to come to its aid in an emergency.

“And of course, helping Taiwan is very much in the interests of all seafaring nations,” he said.

“After all, if Taiwan can be bullied into giving up parts of its sovereignty, then Japan, the Philippines, Vietnam, Malaysia, Korea, all of the countries of the world have to wonder, the region has to wonder about whether they are next,” he added.

The annual Han Kuang exercises have served as Taiwan’s primary war games since 1984, testing the country’s combat readiness in the event of a possible Chinese invasion.

Originally involving only military personnel from all branches of the armed forces, the exercises have over the past few years been expanded to incorporate whole-of-society defense resilience drills to promote active civil-military operations.

Blair also suggested in his address that Taipei should continue its efforts to monitor maritime activities and enforce laws in waters under its jurisdiction, as China continues to send civilian and government vessels into Taiwan’s waters.

Beyond these monitoring and enforcement efforts, he said Taiwan needs an active campaign of diplomacy and public outreach, similar to what the Philippines has undertaken in its disputes and confrontations with Beijing in the South China Sea.

“The objective is to convey the message that Chinese claims and operations are both illegal and inept. In order to win and retain world attention, Taiwanese public diplomacy needs to be inventive and fresh. Taiwan cannot allow China to establish a new normal in the international public perception,” he said.

Blair made the remarks remotely during the International Conference on Sea Lane Security, organized by the Ocean Affairs Council.

At the opening of the one-day conference, National Security Council Deputy Secretary-General Lii Wen (李問) thanked like-minded partners for jointly voicing opposition to China’s destabilizing actions in the East China Sea, the Taiwan Strait and the South China Sea.

He called for greater international and regional cooperation to enhance early-warning capabilities and for international partners to maintain their maritime presence through measures such as freedom of navigation operations and regional cooperation to combat maritime crime.

content:
A Lifeline for Healing and Hope

My name is Lori Engel. I’m 59, homebound in Oregon. I live completely alone with life-altering neurological injuries and disabilities that have reshaped every part of my world.

My Background

I grew up as a missionary child in Brazil, where faith, service, and compassion became the foundation of my life. As an adult, I carried that forward—serving six years as a missionary teacher in Taiwan, then eleven years as a chaplain, walking alongside people in illness, grief, crisis, and loss. Caring for others wasn’t just my work; it was my identity. The last two years of my career, I was the Director of Chaplain Services for a healthcare organization.

Prior to becoming a chaplain, I was an English teacher for almost two decades, teaching both in Taiwan and at universities in the U.S.

How Everything Changed

That path shifted profoundly starting in late 2006. Over time, I sustained multiple traumatic brain injuries and a toxic reaction to Cipro that damaged my nerves and muscles. I developed serious neurological conditions, including cerebellar damage, ataxia, polyneuropathy, spasticity, severe balance impairment, swallowing difficulties, and vision disturbances, to name a few. These affect my ability to walk, stand, use my arms consistently, regulate my nervous system, or handle even basic daily tasks.

Despite these initial injuries, I continued working as a chaplain until 2015, pushing through pain and limitations to serve others, through God's grace and the aid of nutraceuticals. Additional neurological injuries in 2015 made it impossible to continue, leaving me homebound ever since, unable to drive.

Here is a brief summary of all my injuries:

My injuries consist of multiple TBIs (traumatic brain injury) from falling backward onto the kitchen tile floor, hitting the back of my head; slamming my forehead into a concrete bunk bed; and falling and hitting the side of my head here in Oregon. I also experienced medical malpractice that damaged my cervical spine. I was erroneously prescribed fluroquinolones Avelox and Cipro for 30 days straight, which severely damaged my nerves and tendons. (The FDA has issued warnings about these drugs.) Then I got a bad infection. Later, I also experienced thermal burns to my spine and base of my head.

Then, I was exposed to and living in wildfires so severe that ashes were all around me here in Oregon in 2020, which exponentially exacerbated all my autonomic, nerve, and vascular damage, as well as breathing. Then in 2021 I had Covid, which causes neurological issues in even healthy people. For me, it created additional issues.

There has been a compounded, cumulative effect of all the layered injuries. Most people struggle to comprehend such a parade of horribles, but I do have records.

It has been more than I can ever put into words. I am just thankful to be alive. I am thankful for the many years I worked as a chaplain, until there were just too many injuries.

My Daily Reality

Simple things most people take for granted—opening a package, standing at the sink, stepping outside, or even too much visual input—can overload my fragile system, causing loss of balance, neurological shutdown, or crushing exhaustion. Some days I can’t get out of bed. Others, I push through just to care for myself and my faithful dog Teddie, only to crash afterward.

I haven’t seen my family in 13 years (they live on the East Coast), and for the last 10-plus years I can’t travel. I receive no family financial support. The isolation is profound, and Teddie—my constant companion, emotional anchor, and service companion in many ways—is one of the biggest reasons I keep going, in addition to God's miraculous care.

What I Am Fighting For

Yet every day, I fight to heal and hold onto as much independence as possible. As my health allows, I write devotional pieces that integrate faith, neuroscience, and psychology—sharing insights on resilience, hope, and spiritual growth on social media. It’s a small but meaningful way I continue to give back and encourage others, even from home.

My lifeline is an intensive, carefully managed regimen: specialized therapies, targeted nutrition, and essential supplements that stabilize my brain, muscles, emotions, and overall functioning. When I can stay consistent with these protocols, I feel more like myself—steadier, clearer, hopeful. When I can’t, everything declines quickly: neurologically, physically, and emotionally.

How Your Support Helps

My disability income is severely limited (SSDI), and it does not even cover rent. Ongoing costs far exceed what I can cover. Neurological medications/nutraceuticals alone are expensive and not covered by Medicare. I also need nutritious food tailored to my conditions, basic utilities, in-home support, and care for Teddie.

I’m not asking for luxuries—only the basics that allow me to continue healing, stay safe at home, avoid further decline, and keep writing when possible.

Your monthly - or one-time - support will directly help cover:

• Essential neurological and immunological supplements to stabilize my system and medical care not covered by Medicare.

• Food and daily living necessities

• Basic in-home support and utility expenses

• Veterinary care, food, and supplies for Teddie, my vital companion

• Unexpected critical needs that protect my independence and safety

A Message of Gratitude and Hope

Every gift—no matter the size—becomes part of this lifeline. It prevents eviction. It helps me get through the hardest days, hold onto hope for continued (even if gradual) improvement.

Sharing this campaign is also a huge gift. When you’re largely invisible due to homebound disability, profound isolation, and no nearby support network, awareness can make all the difference.

After a lifetime of caring for others, I now humbly need care myself. It’s been a difficult shift, but I’m grateful for every act of kindness.God has never failed me during these long, lonely years.

It's been a long, agonizing road, but I still believe healing is possible. I still hold fast to faith that God can bring restoration, step by step—and use even my writing to touch lives. I will never stop trying.

Thank you for seeing me, for caring, and for helping carry what I cannot carry alone. Your support—financial, prayerful, or simply shared—means more than words can express.

With deepest gratitude and hope,

Lori Engel

"Out of suffering come the strongest souls."

(With friends who brought Lori food in 2017)

In 2021, after wounds discovered under hair

2026

In 2009, as a chaplain.

下载全文 PDF 台湾积体电路制造公司 (TSMC，台湾积体电路制造公司) 生产 90% 以上的先进芯片，为人工智能开发提供动力，显着提升了台湾在全球事务中的战略重要性。近年来，认知影响力行动仍然加剧了许多台湾老年人的担忧，担心台积电的海外扩张可能会损害台湾的经济利益、战略影响力和才华横溢的工程师。然而，像我这样的台湾年轻人可能会认为这些担忧被夸大了。台积电一再强调，其最先进的研发能力将留在台湾，台湾将继续作为公司技术开发和全球生产网络的核心。台湾人不应该担心台积电在美国扩大生产，主要有以下三个原因。首先，此次扩张使台积电能够更好地服务美国领先客户并增加其商机。其次，将生产从台湾转移出去有助于减少环境压力和地缘政治风险，并增强半导体供应链的稳定性。最后，台积电的国际发展计划增强了台湾的全球影响力，并加强了与世界各地合作伙伴的联系。
市场准入、政府补贴和下游供应链效益尽管人们对台积电在美国工厂建造和生产半导体的高成本存在合理的担忧，但值得承认这项活动的长期好处：使台积电能够更快地接触全球客户。尽管在海外建立业务需要更高的成本，但这种扩张在财务上已被证明是可行的，正如台积电亚利桑那州所证明的那样。仅 2025 年，亚利桑那州晶圆厂的净利润就达到新台币 42.​​32 亿元（1.358 亿美元），乍一看似乎是全年数据，但实际上仅在一个季度内就实现了这一收入。台积电亚利桑那州取得成功的关键原因之一是全球芯片市场的变化。美国主要依赖台湾制造尖端逻辑芯片。通过在美国建设更多晶圆厂，台积电能够更好地满足其主要客户的产能需求，其中包括AMD、苹果、英伟达和高通等美国公司。这可以实现更快、更个性化的客户服务，从而与大公司建立信任和亲和力，并鼓励他们将来从台积电购买产品。除了贴近客户之外，美国政府还积极利用立法来鼓励半导体公司在国内建设。
美国商务部根据 CHIPS 和科学法案向台积电提供 66 亿美元的直接拨款资金，并获得 50 亿美元的低息联邦贷款。这笔资金有助于抵消美国比台湾更高的建设和运营成本。此外，台积电在美国的扩张不仅建立了跨行业联系，还为长春集团和三立化学等台湾重要供应商在美国运营铺平了道路，从而推动了广泛的芯片生态系统。当这些主力晶圆厂搬迁到新的土地时，整个材料供应网络也随之移动，从而带来更多的商机。通过授权这些供应商扩展到全球市场，此类行动最终会改变

【原文 English Original】
DOWNLOAD FULL ISSUE PDF Producing more than 90 percent of the advanced chips powering AI development, Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC, 台灣積體電路製造公司) has significantly elevated Taiwan’s strategic importance in global affairs. In recent years, cognitive influence operations have nonetheless fueled fears among many older Taiwanese that TSMC’s overseas expansion could cost Taiwan economic benefits, strategic leverage, and talented engineers. Younger Taiwanese like myself, however, may see these concerns as overstated. TSMC has repeatedly emphasized that its most advanced research and development (R&D) capabilities will remain in Taiwan, and that the island will continue to serve as the heart of the company’s technology development and global production network. Taiwanese should not be concerned about TSMC expanding its production in the United States for three main reasons. Firstly, this expansion allows TSMC to better serve leading-edge US customers and grow its business opportunities. Secondly, diversifying production away from Taiwan helps reduce environmental strains and geopolitical risks, and strengthens the stability of the semiconductor supply chain. Finally, TSMC’s international development plans enhance Taiwan’s global presence and strengthen connections with partners around the world. Market Access, Government Subsidies, and Downstream Supply Chain Benefits Although there are valid concerns about the high cost of building and producing semiconductors at TSMC facilities in the United States, it is worth acknowledging the long-term benefit of this activity: providing TSMC with quicker access to customers worldwide. Even though establishing operations abroad entails higher costs, this expansion has proven financially viable, as demonstrated by TSMC Arizona. In 2025 alone, the Arizona fab recorded a net income of NTD 4.232 billion (USD 135.8 million) —income that, at first glance, may appear to have been full-year data, but was actually made in just one quarter. One key reason why TSMC Arizona has been successful has been changes in the global market for chips. The United States relies primarily on Taiwan for the fabrication of leading-edge logic chips. By building more fabs in the United States, TSMC is better able to satisfy the capacity demands of its key customers, including American companies such as AMD, Apple, Nvidia, and Qualcomm, among others. This enables faster, more personalized customer service, which builds trust and affinity with large companies and encourages them to buy from TSMC in the future. Beyond customer proximity, the United States government has actively employed legislation to encourage semiconductor companies to build domestically. The US Department of Commerce has awarded TSMC USD 6.6 billion in direct grant funding under the CHIPS and Science Act , along with access to USD 5 billion in low-interest federal loans. This funding helps offset the higher costs of construction and operation in the US compared to Taiwan. Furthermore, TSMC’s American expansion not only builds cross-industry connections, but it also drives a broad chip ecosystem by paving the way for critical Taiwanese suppliers such as the Chang Chun Group and Sunlit Chemical to operate in the United States. When these anchor fabs move to new land, the entire material supply network also moves with them, leading to more business opportunities. By empowering these suppliers to expand into global markets, such actions ultimately transfer international investment back into Taiwan’s domestic economy. Therefore, continued expansion in the United States represents a strategic investment in TSMC’s long-term financial future. Image: TSMC Fab 21 under construction in Phoenix, Arizona (November 2023). (Image source: Wikimedia Commons ) Environmental Risks and Geopolitics In order to maintain satisfying relationships with customers, TSMC must operate a stable and unbroken semiconductor production line. Some Taiwanese believe that this stability can be maintained at home, yet growing environmental risks and geopolitical realities indicate that relying on production in Taiwan alone is increasingly fragile. Within this context, TSMC’s expansion to the United States can help maintain a stable semiconductor production line. As TSMC continues to expand its production capacity, Taiwan is gradually reaching the limits of its environmental carrying capacity. Semiconductor fabs consume vast amounts of water and electricity. Building more and more fabs in Taiwan will put too much pressure on the power grid. Increasing load will risk energy shortages and infrastructure strain, thus destabilizing production lines not only for TSMC but also for other businesses in Taiwan. By contrast, locations for TSMC’s expansion, such as Arizona, possess far more abundant resources. Arizona has one of the biggest energy grids in the United States, operating over 6,551 megawatts (MW) of installed solar capacity alongside nearly 3,900 megawatts (MW) of battery energy storage systems. Beyond electricity, water is also essential for the semiconductor industry; a single advanced chip factory can consume up to 38 million liters of water per day (an amount approximately equivalent to the daily water usage of a medium-sized city). As a small island with finite resources, Taiwan simply lacks the physical capacity to sustain such immense environmental pressure. Crowding the nation with dozens of new factories would push its fragile water supply to a dangerous breaking point, placing a burden on the everyday lives of Taiwanese citizens. Moreover, an earthquake that hit eastern Taiwan in 2024 caused TSMC factories in Tainan to shut down temporarily, as chip fabs are designed to automatically cease production when any tremors occur. For instance, EUV chipmaking machines possess sensors that detect infinitesimal movements that cannot be noticed by humans; if the EUV machine senses the floor moving, it will shut down completely. Indeed, continuing to print during tremors can blur the circuit lines and potentially result in significant financial losses as wafers must be discarded. Hence, moving factories to locations like Arizona helps mitigate natural disaster risks such as earthquakes and provides a more controllable environment, rendering chip production lines more efficient. Given the relative availability of land, water, and electrical resources in North America, building factories in the United States may ultimately be beneficial for maintaining the stability of the Taiwanese production lines. By expanding its manufacturing capacity overseas, TSMC can reduce its exposure to geopolitical risks – and, in the event of war, help sustain the industrial capacity of the “arsenal of democracy.” For more than seven decades , Taiwan has faced persistent tensions across the Taiwan Strait, which have intensified in recent years and created significant geopolitical uncertainty. A war in the Taiwan Strait could severely disrupt global semiconductor supply chains, triggering shortages of advanced chips and inflicting trillions of dollars in economic losses worldwide. If key fabs in Taiwan are damaged or destroyed, rebuilding the lost production capacity could take years. By expanding its manufacturing capacity into the United States, TSMC can help key geopolitical partners like America maintain access to chips during wartime situations. Soft Power and Continuity Many Taiwanese argue that TSMC is the “ silicon shield ” protecting Taiwan against China. Therefore, they claim that the protection of this shield would be forfeited should TSMC build more factories in the United States. However, I believe TSMC’s global expansion can also help Taiwan garner greater international recognition by building stronger connections with local communities overseas. One example is the collaboration between Japan Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing (JASM) and the TSMC Education and Culture Foundation, which brought Taiwan’s OneSong Orchestra to Kumamoto for a cultural concert . When locals connect with Taiwanese culture through these activities, it transforms Taiwan from an unfamiliar chip supplier into a culturally rich nation that bonds with local communities on a personal level. Such community bonds naturally encourage local communities to support strong diplomatic ties between their government and that of Taiwan. Additionally, these community investments extend into classrooms, where local universities partner with TSMC to build a new generation of semiconductor professionals who have been trained through Taiwanese resources. In the context of Japan, cultural exchanges between TSMC and the local community not only strengthen the company’s ties with Kumamoto residents, but also help build public support for its overseas expansion. In this sense, TSMC’s overseas expansion does more than diversify production—it can also expand Taiwan’s international presence and strengthen its ties with key partners around the world. Many Taiwanese refer to TSMC as the nation’s “Guardian Mountain” (護國神山) because of its crucial role in safeguarding Taiwan’s economic prosperity and national security. TSMC’s global expansion can strengthen the resilience of the semiconductor supply chain, bring production closer to its customers, expand its business opportunities, create new possibilities for young Taiwanese, and enhance Taiwan’s international presence. Some Taiwanese elders may worry that sending engineers to the United States represents a loss of human resources for Taiwan. However, these Taiwanese engineers are not abandoning Taiwan. Instead, they are stepping into global leadership roles and establishing important cross-border industry networks. When these professionals eventually return to Taiwan, they will be able to train the next generation of engineers preparing to go overseas and advance Taiwan’s economic prosperity. Expanding into the United States, therefore, does not mark the end of TSMC’s role as Taiwan’s “Guardian Mountain.” Rather, it is a pragmatic step toward ensuring that TSMC can continue to fulfill that role in a rapidly changing world. One Youth’s Perspective As a junior in the International Bilingual School at Hsinchu-Science-Park, many of my classmates’ parents are employed at TSMC. Drawing inspiration from their parents, some have also decided to pursue a career at TSMC. The establishment of TSMC Arizona has encouraged even more of them to pursue this track, and many of my peers are excited about the new job opportunities abroad that have been created. Indeed, these new job opportunities appeal to Taiwanese teenagers who had never yet been able to imagine their part in the “American Dream.” Ironically, according to a 2024 ABC News/Ipsos survey of US adults, public confidence in the American Dream has significantly eroded. Yet, new TSMC subsidiaries in the United States not only stabilize the production chain but also help revive the long-faded “American Dream” for Taiwanese youth. The main point: While many commentators in Taiwan suggest that TSMC’s expansion to the United States weakens Taiwan’s economic and national security, the business decisions may actually prove more economically viable, and relieve pressure on Taiwan’s grid and water supply. Meanwhile, the opportunities to work in the United States revive the long-faded “American Dream” among Taiwanese youth. The post A Taiwanese Youth’s Perspective: TSMC’s US Expansion and the American Dream appeared first on Global Taiwan Institute .

title: Climate change-HIV connection and how to report on it
summary: On 12 April 2022, Mfundo Shezi woke when the skies cracked open and unleashed a merciless[deluge over KwaZulu-Natal](https://bhekisisa.org/special-reports/climate-change/2025-09-22-the-falling-down-place/). The 32-year-old, who usually slee
content:
On 12 April 2022, Mfundo Shezi woke when the skies cracked open and unleashed a merciless[deluge over KwaZulu-Natal](https://bhekisisa.org/special-reports/climate-change/2025-09-22-the-falling-down-place/). The 32-year-old, who usually sleeps in a park in Umbilo in Durban, immediately fled for shelter, abandoning all he owned.

Shezi didn’t have much, but by the time he returned the next morning, he found that the flood had taken all of his possessions. That included his ID and his monthly supply of[antiretroviral (ARV) treatment](https://www.cdc.gov/hiv/basics/livingwithhiv/treatment.html) for HIV, which he had been taking faithfully since he started treatment in 2021.

“On that day, I missed a dose for the first time,” he[told Bhekisisa](https://bhekisisa.org/article/2022-11-17-i-missed-a-dose-for-the-first-time-how-the-kzn-floods-derailed-hiv-treatment/). Without taking his HIV medications consistently, he knew he’d get sick.

He panicked. He tried to get to the local clinic but wasn’t able to get there. So Shezi walked to the government hospital. It was open, but without his ID book – or a transfer letter from his regular clinic, which would allow him to get his medication – they couldn’t help.

Experts say a[changing climate](https://www.un.org/en/climatechange/what-is-climate-change) will probably bring on more bouts of severe weather like this flood, which killed more than 450 people. But the flood itself would not somehow make Shezi’s HIV more infectious or deadly. What changed was everything affected by it: the destroyed roads, the paper file that held his treatment history, the proof he was who he said he was.

Between 2010 and 2023, new[HIV infections fell by almost 60%](https://www.unaids.org/sites/default/files/media_asset/2024-unaids-global-aids-update_en.pdf) in Africa, meaning that for every 10 people who were getting HIV in 2010, four got it in 2023. But the region could start losing those gains as climate shocks collide with[shrinking HIV funding](https://bhekisisa.org/health-news-south-africa/2026-02-05-what-will-hiv-funding-look-like-in-2026/).

Climate scientist[Christopher Jack](https://www.csag.uct.ac.za/author/cjack/), deputy director of the Climate System Analysis Group at the University of Cape Town, and public health specialist[Coceka Nogoduka](https://www.linkedin.com/in/coceka-nogoduka-58026a96/), who, for 18 years, has helped to shape how South Africa deals with HIV and tuberculosis, spoke to a group of journalists in a[Bhekisisa webinar](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NtkddBhEJX4&t=20s) on the links between climate change and HIV, what it means and what can be done to get ahead of it. Here’s what we learned.

### Seven key connections

**1. Climate change does not make HIV more infectious**

Extreme heat, rain or drier conditions don’t make the virus more infectious or make people with HIV sicker. But it can[change people’s behaviour](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7810285/) and how, when and where they can get healthcare and medication.

**2. A warmer world could mean far more HIV**

If the world keeps pumping[greenhouse gases](https://wmo.int/topics/greenhouse-gases) such as carbon dioxide and methane into the air at the rate it is now, the average global temperature could, in a[worst-case scenario](https://www.carbonbrief.org/explainer-the-high-emissions-rcp8-5-global-warming-scenario/), be[5°C higher](https://sos.noaa.gov/catalog/datasets/climate-model-temperature-change-rcp-85-2006-2100/) than it was about 150 years ago.

If the air becomes that much warmer,[25-37% more people](https://link.springer.com/epdf/10.1007/s10584-020-02753-y?sharing_token=YQDHvAjqoziQRHk7PocWQ_e4RwlQNchNByi7wbcMAY5R9-bA9E9zn66vTSgGKi-DMwuqVeGJnPpC-bOEbU4UB9Zq5mPUVSkKVV9GlabNbooRhoxUCdCj1sv-tDiKPvWt1WGaKbjeY3_E12gGppB5PWg5DdUHSq4pOBZpRb8iWUc%3D) in sub-Saharan Africa might have HIV by 2050 than would have been expected without such harsh global warming, a modelling study shows.

Meanwhile, every time a bad drought hits – when there is less than 20% of the normally expected rainfall – HIV infections could[climb by 11%](https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1111/ecoj.12149) in rural areas in Africa, where many people already have HIV. Heavy rainfall and flooding can increase the[chances of getting HIV by 14%, and make it 11% more](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12039729/) likely for someone to get another sexually transmitted infection.

In the rest of our story, we explain why.

**3. When disaster forces people to move, normal treatment breaks**

Even when weather experts know a flood is on the way, people may still have to flee their homes suddenly. When that happens, they might lose their ID or find it impossible to get to their usual clinic, breaking the daily routine they need to stay healthy with HIV. In 2025, natural disasters across sub-Saharan Africa forced people to move nearly[3 million times](https://api.internal-displacement.org/sites/default/files/publications/documents/IDMC-GRID-2026-Global-Report-on-Internal-Displacement.pdf?_gl=1*5pvl8x*_ga*MTUzODA0NTg1NS4xNzc5MjY3MTQx*_ga_PKVS5L6N8V*czE3NzkyNjcxNDEkbzEkZzEkdDE3NzkyNjcxNTUkajQ2JGwwJGgw).

When people are displaced by extreme weather, their homes might be washed away with their identification documents, and they might not even be able to get into a new health facility and be able to identify themselves so that they can then be re-registered into our public health systems. – Coceka Nogoduka

For someone on treatment, that routine is a matter of life and death. If they can’t collect[medication regularly](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11800643/), the virus can get a foothold and start[multiplying](https://www.niaid.nih.gov/diseases-conditions/10-things-know-about-hiv-suppression), making people sick and able to[infect others](https://hivrisk.cdc.gov/can-increase-hiv-risk/).

**4. When people move, their medical records usually don’t**

South Africa has long planned a[national electronic patient record system](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10311353/) that would allow a person’s patient file to follow them if they move and seek care at a different clinic or hospital. But 10 years after it was[first proposed](https://nstiip.naci.org.za/knowledge-base/reports/573-e-health-strategy-south-africa-2012-2016-2/viewdocument/573), that system is not yet fully in place; only the Western Cape has a fully rolled out system in place. In most clinics, patient records are still kept on paper. Even if someone can get a transfer letter, which is needed to get treatment at a different clinic, they may be counted as someone who has stopped taking their medication in one place and considered a brand-new patient in another – something which could not only affect patient care but also[skew how HIV cases are counted](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10022370/) in national registers.

**5. Surviving a disaster can drive risky behaviour**

Women who move because extreme weather has destroyed their livelihood or their access to food are more likely to[trade sex for basic necessities](https://journals.lww.com/jaids/abstract/2022/08010/associations_between_mobility,_food_insecurity,.4.aspx) such as food or shelter.

When someone has to trade sex just to survive, they often lose their say in the relationship. Because they are relying on that partner for their basic needs, the power imbalance makes it much harder for them to insist on using a condom or to have safer sex. Research shows that when women are forced into these survival strategies, they are[twice as likely to get HIV](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9909688/).

**6. Repeated shocks wear down the system**

Stopping HIV needs both treatment and prevention in place – testing, clinic visits and offering condoms or[HIV prevention medication such as the daily anti-HIV pill or six-monthly HIV prevention shot, lenacapavir. HIV prevention meds lower someone’s chances of contracting the virus to close to zero.](https://www.who.int/teams/global-hiv-hepatitis-and-stis-programmes/hiv/prevention/pre-exposure-prophylaxis)Weather disasters put health systems under pressure: clinics close because they are flooded or have no power to keep medicines at the right temperature, and flooded roads and broken bridges stop delivery trucks from reaching remote areas. During major floods in[Namibia’s Ohangwena region in 2009](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1gFi1Li3X6gXj6sXlIXgmpj23ks1xJZFP/view?usp=sharing), damaged roads and floodwaters made 41 health facilities unreachable.

How many more HIV cases [could climate change bring](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-026-57530-1)?

When HIV-negative people can’t access their next HIV prevention medication dose in time, they’re[no longer protected against the virus](https://bhekisisa.org/health-news-south-africa/2026-09-16-want-the-six-monthly-hiv-jab-heres-your-nine-step-clinic-cheat-sheet/)and their chances of getting HIV increase.

While one flood or drought won’t undo decades of HIV progress, South Africa’s high number of[people living with HIV](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9165791/), alongside more[frequent and intense weather](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S2211464525000491) and sharp decreases in[HIV funding](https://bhekisisa.org/health-news-south-africa/2025-04-17-r2-82-billion-thats-what-we-need-to-plug-the-us-funding-gap-for-now/), means we’ll be even more vulnerable when the next climate shock lands.

Often we have inadequate infrastructure. The roads are not built well, or not well maintained, and bridges aren’t designed for extreme rainfall events. This often compounds with weak health systems; a non-climate driver is now compounded with this climate impact. These cascade through the system, through infrastructure, through access to healthcare, through health outcomes, and then beyond that into livelihoods, loss of primary breadwinners, and the education system. – Christopher Jack

**7. What could help**

Records that follow a patient would keep treatment going when people move. Health facilities can be built to withstand shocks, and leaders can be held to plans already on the books.

[South Africa’s Climate Change Act](https://cer.org.za/wp-content/uploads/2024/07/Climate-Change-Act-22-of-2024.pdf) came into operation on 17 March 2025, with a national adaptation strategy meant to follow within a year to help guide how the country prepares and responds.

After Cyclone Freddy swept away paper health documents, medicines and supplies in Malawi in 2023, its former health minister,[Khumbize Kandodo Chiponda, acknowledged it as a failure](https://www.newsweek.com/climate-crisis-escalates-building-resilient-health-systems-imperative-opinion-1843797) of the health system that should be urgently reformed. She set about introducing digitised health records, stronger emergency planning and health facilities that can withstand shocks – an example of how accountability can spur change.

### Connections and angles

Climate change and HIV are connected in many ways – and that’s often where the stories are. Here are some ideas on where to look and what to keep in mind.

**Before and after:** Talk to community members to find out how they were affected, and to healthcare providers, clinic managers and provincial health departments about what happened to patients after recent floods or droughts. Ask:

*   Were clinics accessible after severe weather?

*   Were drug supplies delayed?

*   Did testing or PrEP services pause?

*   Did more patients miss their HIV medication pickups?

*   Were people able to transfer smoothly from one clinic to another?

**Survey systems:** Find the gaps in transport, healthcare and medicine supply chains and the movement of people. That can give concrete examples of system failures that need to be addressed.

title: Dean delivers big blow for Twins in KBO postseason win on birthday
zh_title: 迪恩在生日那天为双胞胎队赢得了 KBO 季后赛胜利
summary: 作者：Yoo Jee-ho 首尔，10 月 14 日（韩联社）——LG Twins 球星奥斯汀·迪恩周三计划了一个更好的方式来庆祝他的 33 岁生日。这位美国重击手在首尔蚕室棒球场举行的韩国棒球组织 (KBO) 季后赛中，在第一局下半打出两分本垒打，帮助双城队以 4-1 击败斗山熊队，获得外卡资格。 10 月 10 日，在首尔蚕室棒球场举行的韩国棒球组织季后赛俱乐部外卡赛中，LG 双城队的奥斯汀·迪恩 (Austin Dean) 在对阵斗山熊队 (Doosan Bears) 的比赛中打出两分本垒打后庆祝。
content:
作者：柳智浩

首尔，10 月 14 日（韩联社）——周三，LG Twins 球星奥斯汀·迪恩 (Austin Dean) 计划了一个更好的方式来庆祝他的 33 岁生日。

这位美国重击手在首尔蚕室棒球场举行的韩国棒球组织 (KBO) 季后赛中，在第一局下半打出两分本垒打，帮助双城队以 4-1 击败斗山熊队，获得外卡资格。

2026 年 10 月 14 日，在首尔蚕室棒球场举行的韩国棒球组织季后赛俱乐部外卡赛中，LG 双城队的奥斯汀·迪恩 (Austin Dean) 在对阵斗山熊队的比赛中击出两分全垒打后庆祝。（韩联社）

在对阵先发球员郭本（Gwak Been）的第一次击球的第六球中，迪恩（Dean）得到了一个悬挂在该区域顶部的弧线球，迪恩（Dean）猛烈地挥杆并欣赏他的高耸射门，该球飞入左外野的看台深处。

“对我来说，这只是想找到一个好的球场来处理，”迪恩说。 “显然，如果你看了今天的比赛，你就会知道他们的计划是不给我任何中间的东西，或者相对而言任何好的击球。我觉得那里的那个球已经足够好，让我能够发挥出我最好的挥杆能力。我想他一扔球，我就很好地看到了球的出局。我一击球，就自动知道我得到了它。”

迪恩在接下来的三场本垒打中三振，但第一局的出色表现足以让他被评为本场最佳球员。
迪恩带领双城队在常规赛中打出了职业生涯最高的 41 个本垒打。不过，他在接下来的比赛中表现得很冷静，在 10 月份的 9 场比赛中只打出了 2 个本垒打，安打率只有 0.200，但他在本次季后赛的第一次击球中表现出色。

迪恩在最近的季后赛系列赛中表现非常挣扎。在 2025 年韩国系列赛中，迪恩在 5 场比赛中 20 场仅打出 1 次，双城队以 4-1 击败韩华老鹰队的系列赛轻松掩盖了这一低迷状态。在 2024 年第二轮对阵三星雄狮队的比赛中，迪恩在四场比赛中 15 投 1 中，双城队在卫冕过程中提前被淘汰。

LG 双城队的奥斯汀·迪恩于 2026 年 10 月 14 日在首尔蚕室棒球场举行的韩国棒球组织季后赛对阵斗山熊队的外卡比赛中被评为最佳球员后进行庆祝。（韩联社）

虽然大多数季后赛比赛都在 10 月进行，但这是迪恩自 2023 年加入双城队以来在生日那天的第一次季后赛比赛。

迪恩还在 2023 年 10 月 14 日打了一场常规赛，并在当天对阵熊队的比赛中打出了全垒打。

“我很少这样做，”他说。 “我并没有把我的生日当作什么大事。这只是又一天变老了，我的头上和胡须上的白发越来越多，但现在很酷。显然，我必须花时间和家人、孩子们在一起。获得生日本垒打总是一种奖励。”

【原文 English Original】
By Yoo Jee-ho

SEOUL, Oct. 14 (Yonhap) -- LG Twins star Austin Dean could not have planned a better way to celebrate his 33rd birthday Wednesday.

The American slugger launched a two-run home run in the bottom of the first inning to help the Twins defeat the Doosan Bears 4-1 for the wild card in the Korea Baseball Organization (KBO) postseason at Jamsil Baseball Stadium in Seoul.

Austin Dean of the LG Twins celebrates after hitting a two-run home run against the Doosan Bears during the clubs' wild card game in the Korea Baseball Organization postseason at Jamsil Baseball Stadium in Seoul on Oct. 14, 2026. (Yonhap)

On the sixth pitch of his first at-bat against starter Gwak Been, Dean got a curveball that hung over the top of the zone, Dean took a violent swing and admired his towering shot that flew deep into the stands in left field.

"For me, it was just trying to find a good pitch to handle," Dean said. "Obviously, if you watched the game today, you know their plan was to not give me anything in the middle or relatively anything good to hit. I feel like that one right there was just good enough for me to be able to put my best swing on it. I think I saw it out of the hand really well as soon as he threw it. I knew automatically, as soon as I hit it, that I got it."

Dean struck out in his next three trips to the plate, but the first-inning dinger was enough to get him named the Player of the Game.

Dean led the Twins with a career-high 41 home runs in the regular season. He had cooled off down the stretch, though, managing just two home runs and a .200 batting average in nine games in October, but he went deep in his very first at-bat of this postseason.

Dean struggled mightily in his recent postseason series. In the 2025 Korean Series, Dean batted only 1-for-20 in five games, a slump conveniently masked by the Twins' 4-1 series win over the Hanwha Eagles. And for the 2024 second round against the Samsung Lions, Dean went 1-for-15 in four games, as the Twins were eliminated early in their title defense.

Austin Dean of the LG Twins celebrates after being named the Player of the Game in a Korea Baseball Organization postseason's wild card game against the Doosan Bears at Jamsil Baseball Stadium in Seoul on Oct. 14, 2026. (Yonhap)

While most postseason games are played in October, this was Dean's first postseason action on his birthday since he joined the Twins in 2023.

Dean had also played a regular-season game on Oct. 14, 2023, and homered against the Bears that day, too.

"It's not very often I get to do that," he said. "I don't make a big deal of my birthday. It's just another day of getting older, getting more gray hairs on my head and my beard, but now it is cool. I got to spend the time with my family, with my kids, obviously. And getting the birthday home run is always a bonus."

Next up for the Twins will be the Kia Tigers, featuring their own MVP candidate in Kim Do-yeong.

Kim and Dean engaged in a memorable duel for the home run title, with Kim winning it by four homers, including one on Monday in their two teams' final regular-season meeting that sealed the third seed for the Tigers and sent the Twins to the wild card game.

Asked about another matchup against Kim and his Tigers, Dean said the postseason will be a different animal.

"The regular season is over with," Dean said. "Do-yeong is crowned the home run king. Congratulations to him. It is an awesome achievement, but now we are in the postseason mode. Your stats don't matter, what you did in the regular season. Now it is just trying to be a good team player and do what we can to win ball games.

"That is all that really matters right now."

title: HK and Chongqing launch cross-boundary data validation platform
zh_title: 香港与重庆推出跨境数据验证平台
summary: 香港 香港和重庆推出基于区块链的跨境数据验证平台，无需传输原始文件即可验证财务数据。该平台由重庆信用和微众银行科技服务有限公司运营，最初将支持开户等银行服务 [![图片 1: Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk) 作者：[Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)，主编 14 2026 年 10 月，香港时间 17:57 · 1 分钟阅读香港金融管理局 (HKMA) 和重庆当局关于 W
content:
香港
香港和重庆推出基于区块链的跨境数据验证平台，无需传输原始文件即可验证财务数据。该平台由重庆信用和微众银行技术服务公司运营，初期将支持开户等银行服务。

[![图片1：Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)

作者：[Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)，主编

香港时间 2026 年 10 月 14 日 17:57 · 阅读时间 1 分钟

香港金融管理局（金管局）和重庆当局周三推出了渝港跨境数据验证平台，这是一个基于区块链的系统，可以在不传输或存储原始文件的情况下验证数据，从而降低跨境结算中的合规和隐私风险。

该平台由重庆信贷和微众银行技术服务公司运营，微众银行是腾讯支持的微众银行的子公司。金管局表示，最初将重点关注两个城市之间的金融应用，由当地银行开发用例来验证北向和南向数据流。这将帮助客户获得银行服务，例如开户和贷款申请。
金管局总裁余伟文表示：“我们将与内地有关部门、银行业、前沿科技企业及其他持份者保持紧密联系，不断完善平台，造福两地居民和企业，支持实体经济发展。”

该技术已在深港跨境数据验证平台得到验证，该平台于2024年5月启动试点，并于2025年4月接入金管局商业数据交换平台。金管局表示，该平台已记录超过4万次使用，为10多家银行、10多个业务场景提供服务。

金管局表示，致力于根据2025年香港金融科技周期间公布的金融科技2030战略创建下一代数据基础设施，围绕数据基础设施、人工智能、弹性和代币化这四个“DART”支柱，将香港变成一个强大的、面向未来的国际金融中心。

[![图片3：Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)

【原文 English Original】
Hong Kong
Hong Kong and Chongqing have launched a blockchain-based cross-boundary data validation platform to verify financial data without transferring original documents. The platform, operated by Chongqing Credit and WeBank Technology Services, will initially support banking services such as account openin

[![Image 1: Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)

By [Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk), Editor in Chief

14 Oct 2026 at 17:57 HKT · 1 min read

The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) and Chongqing authorities on Wednesday launched the Chongqing-Hong Kong Cross-boundary Data Validation Platform, a blockchain-based system that verifies data without transferring or storing original documents, reducing compliance and privacy risks in cross-border settlement.

The platform is operated by Chongqing Credit and WeBank Technology Services, a unit of Tencent-backed WeBank. It will initially focus on financial applications between the two cities, with local banks developing use cases to validate northbound and southbound data flows, the HKMA said. This will help clients access banking services such as account opening and loan applications.

Eddie Yue Wai-man, chief executive of the HKMA, said: "We will maintain close liaison with the relevant Mainland authorities, the banking industry, frontier technology companies and other stakeholders to continuously enhance the platform. This, in turn, will benefit residents and corporates from both places and support the development of the real economy."

The technology has been proven on the Shenzhen-Hong Kong Cross-boundary Data Validation Platform, a pilot launched in May 2024 and connected to the HKMA's commercial data interchange in April 2025. That platform has recorded more than 40,000 usages, serving over 10 banks across more than 10 business scenarios, the HKMA said.

The HKMA said it is committed to creating next-generation data infrastructure under the Fintech 2030 strategy, unveiled during Hong Kong Fintech Week 2025, to turn Hong Kong into a robust, future-ready international financial hub around four "DART" pillars: data infrastructure, artificial intelligence, resilience and tokenization.

title: Kelly Clarkson and Brooklyn store clash on social media
summary: **NEW YORK —**It was something most people have likely done at one time or another: complain to others about feeling judged or dismissed during an interaction, maybe even take to social media to post about it. But just because we might all
content:
**NEW YORK —**It was something most people have likely done at one time or another: complain to others about feeling judged or dismissed during an interaction, maybe even take to social media to post about it.

But just because we might all have the same impulse, we all don’t have the same reach and impact. Exhibit A: a dispute between singer Kelly Clarkson and a small store in Brooklyn that's brought out angry fans and heated commentary.

The conflict from over the weekend, involving a high-priced mechanical bird, is raising more issues than just the quality of customer service. It's also a case study in power dynamics, and the differential that exists between someone with a high profile and those without.

*   [Marites Allen reveals fearless 2027 Fire Sheep forecast, pioneering ‘Destiny Is in Your Stars’ platform](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/14/entertainment-lifestyle/marites-allen-reveals-fearless-2027-fire-sheep-forecast-pioneering-destiny-is-in-your-stars-platform/2445260)

It started Saturday when Clarkson went to Art of Play, a store in Brooklyn that offers items like books, games and playing cards and also hosts magic shows. But the interaction turned negative, she said in a social media post, when she “was looked at as if I couldn’t afford it” and went on to say the store had “just lost a huge sale.” She named the store and gave it a thumbs down.

A back-and-forth ensued, with the store making its own posts saying initially that the item wasn't for sale and then adding that they had tried to find her an alternative. Clarkson said that wasn't true.

Since Clarkson's initial post, there's been a barrage of commentary online — and, the store owners say, in the real world. There have been hateful messages and reviews, and even someone showing up at the store, said Adam Rubin, one of the partners.

“I don’t understand why these people are willing to debase themselves on behalf of a celebrity they never met,” he said. Representatives for Clarkson did not respond to repeated attempts to get comment.

*   ![Image 1: Pangilinan seeks reversal of ruling on Duterte’s dropped charges](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/14/1258438.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Pangilinan seeks reversal of ruling on Duterte’s dropped charges](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/14/news/pangilinan-seeks-reversal-of-ruling-on-dutertes-dropped-charges/2445025)

[![Image 2: Kelly Clarkson. PHOTO BY RODIN ECKENROTH/GETTY IMAGES/ AFP](https://manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/14/1259060.jpg)](https://manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/14/1259060.jpg)
Kelly Clarkson. PHOTO BY RODIN ECKENROTH/GETTY IMAGES/ AFP

**The power of celebrity is potent**

Celebrities have power in different ways. They can influence what people feel as well as impact what they think or believe, said Alfred Archer, assistant professor at Tilburg University in the Netherlands, who has done research around the ethics and politics of fame.

In a situation like Clarkson's, the influence is heavily weighted in the celebrity's favor as a result, he said. That doesn't mean celebrities should be censored or barred from speaking, but they should be cognizant of that reality in determining what they say and how they say it.

*   ![Image 3: Marcos’ impeachment plot backfires](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/13/1258203.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Marcos’ impeachment plot backfires](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/14/opinion/columns/marcos-impeachment-plot-backfires/2444878)

“You can’t hold the celebrity responsible for everything that their followers do, of course,” Archer said, but those who have influence should remember that their words can resonate widely and “be careful about what they put on social media and what they communicate in public for that reason.”

That power can also have positive ripples — like when Ms. Rachel, the children's educator and YouTube star, asked people on social media for Black-owned businesses to support. She gave recognition to small businesses like a coffee shop in New Jersey, leading to a huge jump in sales and popularity.

“I think really the responsibility here is to use this power in a responsible way,” Archer said. “And of course, what that looks like in any individual case is going to be a decision for a particular celebrity to make. But they do have to think about it a bit more carefully than an ordinary member of the public does.”

*   ![Image 4: Lacson asks Padilla to clarify ‘disregard for law’ comment on Duterte trial](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/13/1256725.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Lacson asks Padilla to clarify ‘disregard for law’ comment on Duterte trial](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/13/news/lacson-asks-padilla-to-clarify-disregard-for-law-comment-on-duterte-trial/2444142)

[![Image 5: A general view shows Art of Play, Tuesday, Oct. 13, 2026, in the Brooklyn borough of New York. AP PHOTO](https://manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/14/1259027.jpg)](https://manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/14/1259027.jpg)
A general view shows Art of Play, Tuesday, Oct. 13, 2026, in the Brooklyn borough of New York. AP PHOTO

**Social media changed the equation**

While everyday people have always been fascinated by the famous, the explosion of social media and the glut of information — and the way we follow our family and friends right along with our favorite stars — means there's more of a likelihood that people can develop parasocial, or one-sided, unreciprocated relationships with celebrities. That can lead to the kind of harsh messages and bad reviews that the Brooklyn store says it has experienced.

That aspect of modern life is baffling to Franchesca Ramsey, a writer, podcaster, and content creator.

“I think social media itself has heightened people’s ability to feel a connection to a celebrity or a public person that they don’t know,” she said.

“Back in my day, you liked a musician, you put up a poster on the wall. You read the magazine articles about them. You maybe went to their concert. You watched their music videos. But beyond that, it didn’t feel like a two-way relationship. It felt like I’m the fan and this is the person that I really enjoy,” she said.

“Social media has... kind of created this false sense of reality where, I really think even the act of watching someone’s content on your phone and it looks like they’re talking directly to you," she said.

Asked what advice he would give another small-business owner facing this kind of situation, Rubin didn't have any. “This is not something that a small business owner has the capability to deal with,” he said. “This is something that happens on a level of fame and celebrity that I don’t have access to, (that) most normal people don’t have access to.”

Watching the crowd of reporters from his plumbing supply store next door to Art of Play, Daniel Graffeo couldn't believe the uproar was still going on several days after the initial encounter, but wasn't totally surprised. “Nowadays everybody's looking for something, you know, publicity,” he said.

He hoped it would never find him. “I would not want to be in that situation.”
